44718160.article_content:
Remember
back in 2023 when hackers exposed
(and fixed) malicious anti-repair software in Polish trains? Well, it turns out that the manufacturer, Newag, is at it again.
Just last month, three new trains got locked up in Poland. Newag initially refused to unlock them but relented in the end. But it gets worse. Much worse. Newag has now sued both the Polish repair service SPS that fixed those original trains, and has also gone after the individual members of ethical hacking group
Dragon Sector
, who studied the trains’ software and discovered Newag’s anti-repair measures. In total, the two lawsuits seek the equivalent of over $3 million USD.
But first, let’s see how we got here.
Attempt Third Party Repair? Here’s a Lockout For You
Back in 2022, members of
Dragon Sector
were called in by a train repair shop Serwis Pojazdów Szynowych (SPS) to work out why its trains were refusing to run. Digging into the code revealed a software trap that would disable trains if they were anywhere near a repair facility that wasn’t run by the manufacturer, Newag. But Newag used a pretty inaccurate way to determine when the trains were in a rival repair shop, which led to some unexpected consequences.
The original version of the locking mechanism seems to have counted how many days a train sat out of use. If it exceeded a time limit (originally ten days), it locked up the train.
This lock got triggered in the first few trains serviced by SPS (which had no idea what was really happening), and Newag claimed that the trains had locked up because the repair techs had broken something.
A few weeks later, two more trains were waiting to be sent to SPS (because the SPS storage facilities were full of locked-up trains). After SPS freed up some space, train owner Koleje Dolnośląskie found that they didn’t start anymore either, showing exactly the same symptoms as those that locked up at SPS. At this point, Michał Kowalczyk of Dragon Sector tells us, Newag’s version of events started to look suspicious. They said that the trains at SPS broke down because of faulty servicing. But these newly locked trains never even got near SPS, and they’d locked up in exactly the same way.
These two trains were subsequently repaired by Newag, but without revealing what they had actually fixed. When the Dragon Sector team analyzed them afterwards, they discovered that the locking system had been updated to wait for 21 days instead of ten.
And it gets better. Newag also added a new GPS component. This would check whether trains were near known workshop locations before disabling the trains. And of course, this trick also backfired. Newag ships slightly different software for each manufactured “batch”, so effectively each owner gets slightly different trains. And one batch of the 45WE EMU (electric multiple unit, the kind of train that doesn’t have a separate engine up front to pull the passenger cars), would switch off automatically when passing through the Mińsk Mazowiecki railway station. Trains full of passengers were left stranded.
You can probably guess what happened next. Newag not only denied that it had added such software, but claimed that it had been added by hackers, hinting that those hackers had done it on behalf of a rival company.
It seems like a lot of hassle on the part of Newag, but the rewards are huge. For example, Michał Kowalczyk told me that Newag was “taking around 25k EUR per unlock” in the past. That’s a chunk of money for sure, but Newag may also have been angling to monopolize the Impuls train service market, which is worth around $40 million USD annually. Think of it more as having to pay to get your cell phone unlocked from the carrier.
A Newag “Impuls” train passes the National Stadium Warsaw. Photo via
Schnitzel_bank on Flickr
.
Are Software Lockouts Legal?
In the US, companies like tractor maker John Deere have used the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) to
threaten independent repair shops
. Manufacturers put protections into their software, and sue under the DCMA, which makes breaking such protections illegal. The DMCA was meant to stop people from copying movies and music, but has since gone far beyond.
Criminal punishments under the DCMA include fines up to $500,000, up to five years in jail, or both. You can see why it’s such a powerful tool for suppressing both big and small repair outfits.
But we’ve been fighting for the last decade to make repair activities exempt, and we’ve had a lot of success. With our friends at Public Knowledge, we’ve won DMCA exemptions for everything from
cell phones
to
McFlurry machines
. Still, as we know from the continued existence of
illegal
“warranty void if removed” stickers, manufacturers don’t always seem to care about the law when it comes to abusing our rights to repair the products we bought and own.

文章主要讲述了波兰火车制造商Newag再次因其火车中的反维修软件引发争议。2022年，伦理黑客组织Dragon Sector发现Newag在火车软件中设置了锁机制，如果火车接近非制造商授权的维修点，软件会锁定火车。最近，Newag起诉了曾维修这些火车的波兰维修服务SPS，以及发现并分析该反维修措施的Dragon Sector成员，索赔超过300万美元。

此前，Newag的软件错误地锁定了几辆尚未送修的火车，甚至因GPS组件错误导致某型号火车在经过特定车站时自动停运。Newag不仅否认问题，还指责黑客干预。这种软件锁定策略旨在垄断维修市场，每次解锁费用高达2.5万欧元。

文章还提到，美国制造商利用《数字千年版权法》（DMCA）威胁独立维修店，但在欧盟，法律总体上更支持反向工程和维修权。

data.title: Built a rickroll machine that rickrolls you with microservices
data.author: darad
data.article_summary: "Chaotic Rickroll Machine" 是一个使用 Express 和 Node.js 构建的 API 项目，旨在让用户体验被 "rickrolled"（即被恶搞跳转到经典歌曲《Never Gonna Give You Up》的视频）。该项目可以视为一种 "RaaS（Rickroll as a Service）"。项目包含基本的 API 链和前端文件，代码托管在 GitHub 上，主要使用 JavaScript 和 HTML 编写，并采用 MIT 许可证发布。目前项目没有详细描述或网站。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对一个声称是“微服务”但实质上似乎只是简单API的项目的困惑和幽默反应

不同观点：
• coldfoundry认为该项目被描述为“微服务”是不准确的，因为它实际上只是一个简单的Express.js API，并且对每个路由处理程序进行复制粘贴是不必要的，建议使用单个端点即可。
• comrade1234的评论聚焦于幽默，表示“没有被rickrolled”是这个玩笑的一部分。
• jumploops从中获得灵感，创建了一个rickroll应用，并分享了其项目链接，带有自我宣传的性质。
• Garlef提出一个幽默的建议，认为真正的rickrolling应该是让所有人都来阅读歌词。
• napolux简单地质疑“微服务在哪里？”进一步呼应coldfoundry对项目描述的质疑。
• badgersnake用讽刺的语气指出，不需要为一个不好的笑话使用微服务，因为微服务本身就已经是一个不好的笑话。
• scionni表达了对Rust实现的需求，可能是在技术实现上有特定偏好。
• d--b表示很惊讶自己活了这么久却没有听说过rickrolling，带有个人感慨的性质。
• unfixed用缩写“RaaS”（Rickrolling as a Service）进行调侃，呼应主题。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次出现对“微服务”描述的质疑和对rickrolling这一网络文化现象的幽默反应。
• 一些评论者如jumploops和badgersnake将讨论引向技术实现和幽默应用的结合，展现出对项目创作的兴趣和创意。
• 争议的焦点主要集中在项目是否应被描述为“微服务”以及其实际技术实现的必要性上。

data.title: Rotring 600 Ballpoint Pen
data.author: Alupis
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了Rotring 600圆珠笔，它是经典款Rotring 600的圆珠笔版本，采用标准派克式笔芯，通过点击机制伸缩。该笔拥有全金属机身，手感扎实，点击声清脆但较响。外观上，它与Rotring 600自动铅笔非常相似，仅在笔头和字样上有细微差别。文章提到，虽然原装笔芯曾出现过故障，但更换后问题解决。总体而言，Rotring 600圆珠笔质量上乘，适合长期使用，尤其在打折时值得购买。笔的写作体验主要取决于所用笔芯，但其坚固的机身是其主要优势。

主要讨论点：各种书写工具（如圆珠笔、钢笔、铅笔）的优缺点及个人偏好

不同观点：
• amelius认为笔的核心功能在于笔芯，没必要对笔的外壳或品牌如Apple一般狂热追求。
• ktzar支持使用钢笔，认为钢笔耐用且环保，特别是在使用可充电墨囊和墨水瓶的情况下。
• WillAdams表达了对遗失的Rotring Quattro笔的怀念，但现在使用Skilcraft B3 Aviator作为便携多功能笔选项。
• kstrauser偏爱Uni Jetstream笔，认为其在书写性能上优于其他笔，且价格便宜。
• treetalker推荐Rotring 600笔，尤其是对有手汗的人来说，同时提到Uni Shift 0.9 mm铅笔的优点。
• qwertox分享了对Faber Castell Essentio Ballpoint Pen的喜爱，强调其手感好且耐用。
• LoveMortuus对比Parker和Pilot笔，认为Pilot笔在书写流畅性和性价比上更优。
• yumraj讲述了对Rotring 600铅笔和Pentel Orenz Nero铅笔的使用体验，后者因其自动进铅和可伸缩尖头成为新宠。

• alexalx666对Rotring笔的金属网格 grip 有不满，认为其导致手感不佳。
• xz18r比较Rotring 600/800铅笔和Pentel Graphgear 1000，认为后者价格更便宜且手感接近。
• TheSilva将讨论转向左撇子适用的笔芯，询问快速干燥的笔芯品牌以避免污迹。

• 左撇子适用的快速干燥笔芯成为一个新的讨论方向，表明用户对特定书写需求的关注。
• 不同用户对笔的书写流畅性、手感、耐用性和价格有不同偏好，展现了个人使用体验的多样性。

44686624.article_content:
The Rotring 600 ballpoint pen is the ballpoint variant of the classic Rotring 600. It takes a standard Parker-style refill that extends with a clicker mechanism. The Rotring 600 is pretty much a timeless classic among precision instruments, and its ballpoint variant stays true to the design.
A look at the pen, deconstructed
The Rotring 600 ballpoint features an all-metal body. It feels very solid to hold and seems to be pretty reliable. The clicking mechanism is crisp and satisfying to operate. However, it's also pretty loud, so fidgeting with it may annoy those around you. Other than the different mechanism, the pen looks pretty much identical to the
Rotring 600 mechanical pencil
. The only noticeable exterior differences are the different nib units and different lettering on the barrel. The mechanical pencil variant has a small opening and nib for the mechanical pencil lead, whereas the ballpoint version has a larger opening for the larger ballpoint refill. The red lettering on the mechanical pencils has more text that indicates the lead size inside.
The pen's nib with a refill inside
Rotring is well-known for making high-quality writing instruments, and the Rotring 600 is generally regarded as one of the best products that they put out. This holds generally true with the ballpoint variant of this pen. I do love the high-quality, all-metal build of the pen, but there are some parts of it that are pretty janky. In the past, when I was using the included Rotring ballpoint refill, the mechanism completely broke and I was unable to advance it. However, as soon as I swapped out the refill, the pen worked normally. I’m still unaware of what caused this problem, but I thought I should mention it. Regardless, I’m not too upset with this issue because I prefer gel pen refills and would have swapped it out anyways.
The clicker that advances the refill
Besides that problem with the included refill, I haven’t encountered anything else that has deterred me from this pen. It’s a great quality instrument at a decent price. I was lucky enough to buy mine during a sale a while back during a holiday sale (it’s been too long… I don’t remember which one it was, but if I were to make a guess, I’d say it was the President’s Day sale). If you can find the Rotring 600 ballpoint on sale, or even at a low price on a secondary market, I’d say it’s worth the purchase.
Writing sample
Unlike mechanical pencils and fountain pens, the writing experience of ballpoint pens is pretty much dependent on the refill you put inside them, so you can’t really rate the writing experience of this pen — it’s essentially the same as any other Parker-style ballpoint pen out there. The only difference is really the body. However, it is a great, high-quality build that is worth the money. If you’re interested in a ballpoint pen that’d last you quite a while, the Rotring 600 ballpoint pen may be a great contender.
Nathan Ma
Hi! I'm Nathan, and I'm a stationery enthusiast. I've been in love with anything regarding writing and have built up a huge collection that I can now share with others!
California

data.title: The leverage arbitrage: Why everything feels broken
data.author: tush726
data.article_summary: 文章指出，当前权力运作的速度出现了根本性变化，不同类型的权力（如劳动、资本和代码杠杆）以不同速度影响世界，导致“杠杆套利分化”。高杠杆行动者（如科技公司）能迅速改变社会，而传统机构（如教育、政府）反应迟缓，造成不平衡。这种分化正在侵蚀社会基础，如民主规范和经济流动性。文章认为，解决之道在于提升“杠杆素养”，帮助人们理解和有意识地使用不同类型的杠杆，并重新设计机构以适应不同杠杆速度。若不加以管理，技术能力将与社会协调能力失衡，可能导致文明崩溃。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：文章“为什么一切感觉都崩溃了，我们能做什么”中的观点及其争议

不同观点：
• halayli认为文章标题将个人问题扩大为集体问题。他建议标题应改为“为什么我觉得一切都崩溃了，我能做什么”，以更真诚地反映个人感知和偏见对这种感觉的影响。
• nosefurhairdo批评文章中没有证据支持的大胆断言，如高薪破坏创业精神、民主无法适应社交媒体等，并质疑人工智能系统需要特殊框架的说法。
• exmadscientist觉得文章收集了许多问题但未能解决，指出个人在面对庞大系统时缺乏实际影响力，并质疑自己是否真的拥有任何有效的“杠杆”。
• homeonthemtn同意文章的前提，但对解决方案感到失望，认为在信息过载的社会中，仅提高“意识”并不是有效的解决方案。
• germandiago指出官僚机构本质上较慢，并讨论了机构适应市场技术的问题，同时提到社会工程和影响活动可能对机构造成的影响。
• joules77强调工程/STEM培训不足以解决这些问题，需要多学科合作，并指出当前技术人员缺乏哲学和价值体系的意识，这是问题根源之一。
• PeterStuer强调敏捷性是新进入者挑战现有者的关键，但需要小心平衡创新与社会适应速度。
• jb_rad同意文章观察，但认为应加强解决方案，尤其是提高“杠杆素养”，并讨论如何加快社会机构的速度以跟上技术发展。
• raincole对文章使用em-dashes和“系统性”数学顺序的描述表示质疑，认为这些影响了文章的可读性和专业性。
• raydenvm引用歌曲表达对技术世界的感受，认为歌曲反映了当前技术世界的某种深层次问题。
• dvt认为文章中关于“杠杆套利”导致文明崩溃的说法过于夸张，并指出历史上杠杆套利更高时社会并未崩溃。
• ball_of_lint嘲笑文章提出的解决方案不切实际，认为即使资本主义被废除，全球性问题如全球变暖、战争、饥饿等也需要全球解决方案。
• sakoht从历史角度分析，认为人类历史上大多数人并未感到对自己生活的控制，并指出当前焦虑感可能源于现代人的一种特权感。
• bbor将文章观点与马克思主义理论联系起来，认为文章重新发现了社会主义论点的某些方面，并质疑“杠杆”框架是否足以理解社会方向。

补充讨论：
• 文章提出的“杠杆”概念引发了关于个人在社会系统中实际影响力的广泛讨论，部分评论者质疑个人是否真的拥有有效的杠杆来改变现状。
• 对技术与社会机构发展速度不匹配的讨论，尤其是在技术快速发展而社会机构反应迟缓的背景下，如何协调两者的速度以避免社会崩溃成为一个焦点。
• 多学科合作被认为是解决当前复杂社会问题的关键，技术人员需要更多地了解哲学和社会科学以提高其工作的有效性。
• 评论中多次提到资本主义和社会主义的对立，部分评论者认为废除资本主义可能是解决方案之一，但也有评论者指出全球性问题的复杂性。

争议焦点：
• 文章中关于高薪、民主适应性、人工智能框架等具体论点缺乏证据支持，引发多位评论者的质疑和批评。
• 个人在面对庞大社会和科技系统时的无力感及其可能的解决方案是另一个争议点，部分评论者认为文章提出的解决方案不切实际或过于理想化。
• 对“杠杆”概念及其在社会系统中作用的理解存在分歧，部分评论者认为这一框架不足以解释或解决复杂的社会问题。

44718369.article_content:
Something fundamental has shifted in how power works, and most of our institutions haven't noticed. We're living through what might be called "leverage arbitrage divergence"—a growing gap between how fast some actors can change the world and how fast others can respond to those changes.
Think about it: A small team at TikTok can alter the attention patterns of a billion teenagers in months. Meanwhile, educational institutions need years just to update their curricula, and democratic governments require decades to develop coherent responses to technological change. This isn't just about technology moving fast—it's about different types of power operating at completely different speeds.
The framework begins with a simple observation made by entrepreneur Naval Ravikant: there are three types of leverage.
Labor leverage
scales through human coordination—think committees, voting, traditional management.
Capital leverage
scales through resource deployment—investment, market creation, financial engineering.
Code leverage
scales through systematic automation—algorithms, platforms, network effects. Each operates at a different mathematical order: linear, exponential, and systematic respectively.
Here's where it gets interesting: we're experiencing massive "leverage arbitrage" where actors with higher-order leverage can extract value from systems faster than actors with lower-order leverage can maintain those systems. Google's compensation revolution didn't just raise tech salaries—it systematically destroyed entrepreneurial ecosystems globally by making employment more attractive than company-building. Social media platforms don't just connect people—they reshape democratic discourse faster than democratic institutions can adapt. AI systems aren't just tools—they're deployed faster than we can develop frameworks for understanding their social implications.
The result is what we might call the "modern tragedy of the commons." In Garrett Hardin's original formulation, everyone overused shared resources until they collapsed. Today, higher-leverage actors are strip-mining institutional commons—democratic norms, social trust, educational relevance, economic mobility—faster than lower-leverage actors can regenerate them.
This explains seemingly disconnected modern phenomena. Why do individuals feel powerless despite having unprecedented access to global platforms and financial markets? Because they're measuring their agency using frameworks designed for labor leverage while actually wielding code and capital leverage daily. Why do tech companies keep creating "unintended consequences" despite hiring brilliant people? Because engineers build complex adaptive systems while executives manage them using business metrics designed for predictable, linear growth.
Why does government regulation always feel like it's fighting the last war? Because bureaucratic processes designed for industrial-age problems can't keep pace with algorithmic systems that reshape society in real-time. Why do young people feel anxious about their futures despite living in the most opportunity-rich era in history? Because educational institutions prepare them for career models that economic change has already obsoleted.
The leverage arbitrage creates a vicious cycle. As the gap between different leverage types widens, traditional coordination mechanisms become increasingly ineffective. This drives more actors toward higher-leverage approaches, accelerating the divergence. Meanwhile, the institutional commons that make civilization possible—shared truth, democratic discourse, economic mobility, social cohesion—continue degrading because they depend on lower-leverage maintenance that can't compete with higher-leverage extraction.
But understanding this dynamic also suggests solutions. Instead of trying to slow down technological change or somehow make institutions faster, we need "leverage literacy"—helping people recognize the type of power they're actually wielding and use it more consciously. We need organizations designed to operate across leverage levels simultaneously, with decision-making processes that account for different mathematical orders of impact.
Most importantly, we need to redesign how we measure success and allocate resources. Current systems reward short-term optimization within single leverage types while ignoring long-term effects across leverage types. The result is systematic underinvestment in the institutional commons that higher-leverage systems depend on to function sustainably.
The stakes couldn't be higher. If we don't develop conscious approaches to managing leverage arbitrage, we risk a future where technological capability advances exponentially while social coordination capacity deteriorates linearly—a recipe for civilizational breakdown. data.title: Florida’s attorney general targets a restaurant over an LGBTQ Pride event
data.author: voxadam
data.article_summary: 文章主要讲述了佛罗里达州维罗海滩的一家餐厅因举办LGBTQ+骄傲活动，被州总检察长办公室传唤，要求提供监控视频、客人名单、预订记录及表演者合同等信息。尽管没有犯罪指控，且相关法律已被联邦法院判定可能违宪，总检察长仍推进调查，声称要保护儿童免受“变态成人”影响。此举旨在获取所有参与者的个人数据，严重侵犯公民自由。文章指出，这并非保护儿童，而是通过国家权力恐吓和审查不同意见者。类似情况可能导致人们因担心 surveillance（监视）而不敢参加合法活动，进而压制艺术表达和集会自由。文章警告，这种做法可能扩大为政治报复和广泛监视的工具。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：佛罗里达州的政策与个人自由之间的紧张关系

不同观点：
• [WarOnPrivacy] 表达了个人对佛罗里达州当前政治环境的反抗态度，提到自己因为州内的政策而更想去参加一个变装秀，暗示对某些政策的反感，并通过实际行动（想去参加变装秀）来表达对个人自由的支持。

• [fjfaase] 则将佛罗里达州的政策与历史上的悲剧进行对比，提到最近的一项行政命令可能针对有精神问题的人，并将其与纳粹德国的历史相联系。这个评论暗示了对政府权力扩张和潜在人权侵犯的深切担忧，特别是对弱势群体的影响。

补充讨论：
• [fjfaase] 的评论引发了对政府政策可能走向极端的警惕，通过历史类比（纳粹德国的集中营）来强调对某些群体（如精神病患者、无家可归者、罪犯等）的潜在威胁。这种类比试图引起公众对政策潜在后果的重视。

• 争议的焦点在于佛罗里达州政府政策的意图和后果。一方面，有人认为这些政策可能限制个人自由并对某些群体造成伤害；另一方面，政策的支持者可能认为这些措施是为了维护社会秩序和公共安全。

• 历史类比（纳粹德国的集中营）可能被一些人视为过于极端和不恰当，而另一些人则认为这是对潜在风险的必要警示。这种不同的看法可能会导致讨论的进一步分化。

44719194.article_content:
If you thought going to a Pride event or drag show was just another night out, think again. If you were in Florida,
it might land your name in a government database
.
That’s what’s happening in Vero Beach, FL, where the
Florida Attorney General’s office
has
subpoenaed
a local restaurant,
The Kilted Mermaid,
demanding surveillance video, guest lists, reservation logs, and contracts of performers and other staff—all because the venue hosted an LGBTQ+ Pride event.
To be clear: no one has been charged with a crime, and the law Florida is likely leaning on here—the so-called “Protection of Children Act” (which was designed to be a drag show ban)—
has already been blocked by federal courts as likely unconstitutional
. But that didn’t stop Attorney General James Uthmeier from pushing forward anyway. Without naming a specific law that was violated, the AG’s
press release
used pointed and accusatory language, stating that "In Florida, we don't sacrifice the innocence of children for the perversions of some demented adults.” His office is now fishing for personal data about everyone who attended or performed at the event. This should set off every civil liberties alarm bell we have.
Just like the
Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA)
and
other bills
with
misleading names
, this isn’t about protecting children. It’s about using the power of the state to intimidate people government officials disagree with, and to censor speech that is both lawful and fundamental to American democracy.
Drag shows—
many of which are family-friendly
and
feature no sexual content
—have become a political scapegoat. And while that rhetoric might resonate in some media environments, the real-world consequences are much darker: state surveillance of private citizens doing nothing but attending a fun community celebration. By demanding video surveillance, guest lists, and reservation logs, the state isn’t investigating a crime, it is trying to scare individuals from attending a legal gathering. These are people who showed up at a public venue for a legal event, while a law restricting it was not even in effect.
The Supreme Court
has ruled
multiple times
that subpoenas forcing disclosure of members of  peaceful organizations have a chilling effect on free expression. Whether it’s a civil rights protest, a church service, or, yes, a drag show: the First Amendment protects the confidentiality of lists of attendees.
Even if the courts strike down this subpoena—and they should—the damage will already be done. A restaurant owner (who also happens to be the town’s vice mayor) is being dragged into a state investigation. Performers’ identities are potentially being exposed—whether to state surveillance, inclusion in law enforcement databases, or future targeting by anti-LGBTQ+ groups. Guests who thought they were attending a fun community event are now caught up in a legal probe. These are the kinds of chilling, damaging consequences that will discourage Floridians from hosting or attending drag shows, and could stamp out the art form entirely.
EFF has long warned about this kind of mission creep: where a law or policy supposedly aimed at public safety is turned into a tool for political retaliation or mass surveillance. Going to a drag show should not mean you forfeit your anonymity. It should not open you up to surveillance. And it absolutely should not land your name in a government database.

44717382.article_content:
Adversarial ATProto PDS Migration
By David Buchanan, 28
th
July 2025
An ATProto account lives on a Personal Data Server (PDS), and that service needs to be hosted
somewhere
by
someone
. There are a lot of options here, like a Raspberry Pi in your closet, a rented VPS in a datacentre, or a batteries-included service like
bsky.social
.
Each option has its pros and cons, but whichever you choose, you should be able to change your mind at any time,
even if
your current PDS hosting provider doesnât want that to happen. Maybe your provider decided to jack up their prices. Maybe your Pi was carried off by a seagull. Whatever happens, there should be a path to recover your ATProto account and migrate to a new PDS, with minimal disruption.
This is an example of "credible exit", one of the ideas behind the
design of atproto
.
Non-Adversarial Migration
PDS migration in general is documented in the
atproto spec
. A more practical
guide by bnewbold
describes concretely how to perform a migration from one PDS to another, using the
goat
CLI tool.
Bryan's guide however only covers a "non adversarial" migration scenario, in which the
old
PDS still exists and is cooperating with the migration process.
The "credible exit" story would not be complete without having tools for the adversarial situations too - That's what this article is about. We will also be using
goat
, with some newly-added features to support this scenario.
I hope one day this process can be made more accessible to regular users, but for now this is an advanced developer-oriented process with lots of manual steps. Proceed at your own risk!
Prerequisites
During an adversarial migration, we can't rely on the "origin" PDS to retain any data, or to do anything at all. So we need to sort a few things out in advance (i.e. before the migration becomes necessary).
Things to do in advance:
Create a backup PLC rotation key (very important!)
Fetch recent backup of your repo CAR file, blobs, and private data.
Rotation Key
ATProto identity is rooted in
DID identifiers
, and your DID document points to your active PDS. So, PDS migration involves updating your DID document.
If you're using a
did:web
, no special preparations are required - control of the DNS name is all that's required to make updates.
Updates to
did:plc
identities on the other hand require a Rotation Key to authenticate updates. (If you're wondering whether you're using
did:web
or
did:plc
, you're using
did:plc
). Normally a PDS holds a rotation key so that it can make identity updates on your behalf (for example, when you change your atproto @handle).
You can have multiple rotation keys, and they have a priority order. To defend against a PDS that might "turn evil" in the future,
you need to enrol a backup rotation key
with higher priority than any rotation keys held by the PDS. For more details on this process, see
"Registering Identity Recovery Keys via PDS, using goat"
If you're only worried about the possibility of your PDS going
offline
(which, on balance, is more likely than it becoming actively adversarial), then the priority order of your rotation keys is less important.
Repo Backups
A repo backup is
technically
optional, but you'll have a very bad time without one.
Without, your identity will still be preserved (for example, all the people who "follow" you on Bluesky will continue to follow you), but all your previous posts and media would be gone.
I go into more detail on backup tools towards the end of this article, but for the purposes of this guide I'll assume you've used the
goat
CLI to create a full backup like so:
mkdir my_backup
cd my_backup
goat repo export $ACCOUNT_DID        # export your public data (bluesky posts, etc.)
goat blob export $ACCOUNT_DID        # export blobs (e.g. images, videos)
goat bsky prefs export > prefs.json  # export your private bluesky preferences
For more details about these commands, refer to
Bryan's migration guide
. The only difference is that here we're creating a copy of our data in advance, rather than in the middle of the migration process.
The Migration Process
Let's consider a hypothetical scenario:
Your PDS is hosted by
cheap-servers-r-us.example.com
You donât trust Cheap-Servers-R-Us a whole lot, so youâve set up a backup rotation key and take regular backups of your atproto data (as outlined above).
One day your PDS goes down, and Cheap-Servers-R-Us isnât responding to your customer support tickets. Oh no!
You decide you want to migrate to
better-servers.example.org
, and the PDS admin has given you an
invite code
.
Step 0: Preparation
Install a recent version of
goat
, and make sure you have all the required information on-hand:
Your PLC identity credentials (
$ACCOUNT_DID
,
$PLC_SIGNING_KEY
) (where the latter is in "multibase" format and may also be referred to as a "rotation key")
The host name of the new PDS (
$NEW_PDS_HOST
, e.g.
better-servers.example.org
)
An
invite code
for the new PDS (
$INVITE_CODE
)

主要讨论点：社交媒体平台的分享功能及名称

不同观点：
• dankwizard认为，有些网站的分享功能名称可能不同于常见的“分享”按钮，并以“retruthing”（影射Truth Social平台）为例，暗示某些平台可能采用独特的命名方式来代替传统的“分享”功能。

• jenders则提到Reddit这个网站，暗示Reddit的分享功能是众所周知且广泛使用的，并指出Reddit正在变得越来越流行，以此来回应或反驳dankwizard关于特殊分享按钮名称的观点。

补充讨论：
• dankwizard的评论中隐含了对某些新兴社交媒体平台（如Truth Social）的调侃，可能认为这些平台为了标新立异而采用不同的术语。

• jenders通过提及Reddit，强调了在主流社交媒体中，像Reddit这样传统且知名的平台仍然占据重要地位，并且其分享功能是用户所熟悉的，不需要特殊命名来区分。

• 争议的焦点在于是否需要或应该为分享功能采用独特的名称，以及不同平台间的功能和命名差异是否会影响用户的接受度和使用便捷性。

data.title: A low power 1U Raspberry Pi cluster server for inexpensive colocation (2021)
data.author: LorenDB
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个基于Raspberry Pi的低功耗1U服务器集群项目，旨在以低成本实现服务器托管。该设计在满足1U尺寸和1A @ 120V功耗限制的前提下，最大化计算能力、存储和性价比。项目包括详细的硬件部件列表和规格，如1U机箱、存储设备、交换机、Raspberry Pi单板计算机及其外壳、电源管理等，总成本约800美元。此外，文章还提供了硬件组装、软件设置、网络配置及远程电源管理的详细指南，确保服务器功耗在托管服务商的限制范围内（最高48W，0.4A @ 120V）。该项目适合希望在低功耗条件下搭建高效服务器的人群。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Raspberry Pi服务器集群项目的实用性、硬件选择、托管方式及其技术实现。

不同观点：
• **项目作者的观点**：作者表示该项目已有4年历史，现在使用Mac minis或mini PC可能更合理。提到廉价托管服务存在的安全隐患，如IP冲突问题，且曾因托管公司破产而拿回硬件。

• **Catbert59的观点**：建议使用Intel n100/n150/n305等处理器搭配32GB RAM，强调无转动部件的设备能减少故障。特别指出n150及以上型号需要主动散热。

• **mvip的观点**：推荐Mythic Beasts公司正在进行的将大量Raspberry Pi装入机架的项目，并提供相关博客链接以供参考。

• **procaryote的观点**：提出可以通过直接从引脚供电、增加串行控制台访问及电源按钮等方式改进项目。建议使用Pi5搭配M2板，并提到对电源开关设计的担忧。

• **nateb2022的观点**：认为该项目在性价比上不如其他托管服务提供商（如Hetzner），且可以通过在eBay上采购零件组装出更具性价比的服务器。

• **bullen的观点**：分享自己使用Raspberry Pi集群的经验，选择自建并在家庭光纤上自托管，强调空间节省和静音冷却，指出某些型号的散热问题。

• **rbanffy的观点**：提到有许多集群板可以实现更密集的系统，但制作新板需要大量工作，并对如何在PCB上实现以太网传输表示疑问。

• **omarqureshi的观点**：分享类似的设置，使用Pi 5和M2及PoE HAT，指出无需额外供电的优点，但提到风扇问题。

• **hawk_的观点**：对任意提供商的托管服务提出质疑，希望了解托管的特定用途。

• **dnemmers的观点**：担心该项目设备在运输过程中难以保持完整，建议在家中使用可能更合适。

• **asteroidburger的观点**：认为16GB DDR4内存和1.2TB存储在多个节点上分布并不充裕。

• **arnon的观点**：认为该项目不会持久，但肯定其作为起步的创意。

• **crinkly的观点**：指出许多托管公司对硬件要求严格，可能不接受此类微型集群，并提到IPv4成本问题。

• **pluto_modadic的观点**：建议可以用于IPv6集群，认为可能有趣。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中多次提到硬件散热和供电问题，显示出对设备稳定性的关注。
• 关于托管服务的性价比和适用性存在争议，部分用户认为其他托管服务商更具性价比。
• IPv4和IPv6在项目中的应用也被提及，显示出对网络地址类型的关注。
• 项目在运输和硬件完整性方面的可行性受到质疑，但被认为在家用环境下可能更合适。

Raspberry Pi 1U Server
There are server colocation providers that allow hosting a 1U server for as low as $30/month, but there's a catch: There are restrictions on power usage (1A @ 120v max, for example) because they're expecting small and power-efficient network equipment like firewalls.
This repo is about designing a server that fits within the 1U space and 1A @ 120v power constraint while maximizing computing power, storage, and value.

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Temu的低价优势与欧盟监管措施的争议

不同观点：
• **支持Temu的观点**：  
  - 用户shivasaxena认为Temu提供的商品价格远低于欧洲本地零售商，质量相同甚至更好，对企业尤其是小型企业非常有帮助。他以亲身经历为例，指出CEO从Temu购买的贴纸价格远低于本地商店，并认为欧盟的监管实际上是保护低效的欧洲零售商，属于监管俘获（regulatory capture），不利于消费者和企业。
  
• **对监管措施的支持与反对**：  
  - 用户dotandgtfo认为，尽管许多人声称在线平台规则是反美的，但这些规则旨在消除有害产品、增加平台透明度并让平台对违法行为负责。他指出，美国科技公司经常利用法律漏洞逃避监管，而现在欧洲对这些行为的监管引发了关于言论自由的讨论，但他不认为这种反对会成功。
  
• **对Temu可能受惩罚的讨论**：  
  - 用户lousken询问是否可以通过罚款或完全封锁Temu来迫使其遵守规定。  
  - 用户juliangmp则表示希望Temu被永久禁止，反映出对Temu的反感。

- 用户dotandgtfo提到数字平台在欧洲市场中的不良行为以及公众对这些行为的愤怒情绪，表明欧洲对这些平台的监管有其必要性。

data.title: Truchet Tiles
data.author: downboots
data.article_summary: Truchet tiles是用于信息可视化和图形设计的方形瓷砖，其图案不具有旋转对称性。最早由Sébastien Truchet在1704年提出，后由Cyril Stanley Smith在1987年推广。这些瓷砖可以通过不同方向的排列形成多种图案，常用于可视化信息。典型样式包括对角线分割的对比三角形和四分之一圆弧。Truchet tiles也被用于抽象策略游戏和生成迷宫图案，其连通性可通过渗透理论分析。此外，它们在计算机图形学和各种拼贴问题中也有应用。

44689453.article_content:
From Wikipedia, the free encyclopedia
(Redirected from
Truchet tiles
)
Square tiles used in graphic design
In
information visualization
and
graphic design
,
Truchet tiles
are square tiles decorated with patterns that are not
rotationally symmetric
. When placed in a
square tiling
of the plane, they can form varied patterns, and the orientation of each tile can be used to visualize information associated with the tile's position within the tiling.
[
1
]
Truchet tiles were first described in a 1704 memoir by
Sébastien Truchet
entitled "Mémoire sur les combinaisons", and were popularized in 1987 by
Cyril Stanley Smith
.
[
1
]
[
2
]
Variations
[
edit
]
Contrasting triangles
[
edit
]
The tile originally studied by Truchet is split along the diagonal into two triangles of contrasting colors. The tile has four possible orientations.
Some examples of surface filling made tiling such a
pattern
.
With a scheme:
With random placement:
Quarter-circles
[
edit
]
A second common form of the Truchet tiles, due to
Smith (1987)
, decorates each tile with two quarter-circles connecting the midpoints of adjacent sides. Each such tile has two possible orientations.
The Truchet tile
Inverse of the Truchet tile, created by any 90° rotation or orthogonal flip
We have such a tiling:
This type of tile has also been used in abstract strategy games
Trax
and the
Black Path Game
, prior to Smith's work.
[
1
]
Diagonal
[
edit
]
A
labyrinth
can be generated by tiles in the form of a white square with a black diagonal. As with the quarter-circle tiles, each such tile has two orientations.
[
3
]
The connectivity of the resulting labyrinth can be analyzed mathematically using
percolation theory
as bond percolation at the critical point of a diagonally-oriented grid.
Nick Montfort
considers the single line of
Commodore 64
BASIC
required to generate such patterns -
10 PRINT CHR$(205.5+RND(1)); : GOTO 10
- to be "a
concrete poem
, a found poem".

data.article_summary: Pony是一种开源、面向对象、基于actor模型并具备能力安全（capabilities-secure）的高性能编程语言。用户可以通过Pony Playground在线试用该语言。Pony的独特之处在于其不同于传统编程语言的特性，包括高效的并发处理能力以及内存安全机制。对Pony历史感兴趣的用户可以查阅相关资料，了解其早期发展历程。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Pony编程语言的特性、文档、适用场景及其与其他语言（如Rust）的比较

不同观点：
• [wongarsu] 赞赏Pony在数学运算方面的语法简洁性，尤其是对溢出处理的不同方式（如wrap around、raise exception、undefined behavior）。同时，提出Pony缺少饱和运算（saturating operations），认为尽管有些人认为饱和运算无用，但它对人类直觉和模拟设备非常友好。
• [voidUpdate] 抱怨Pony官网没有在首页提供代码示例，使得初次接触该语言的开发者无法直观感受其语法风格，直到在教程中才找到代码示例。
• [tomsmeding] 强调Pony的独特之处在于其语义而非语法，认为官网没有突出这些语义特点（如actor模型、引用可变性、session types、linear typing等）。建议提供简明的静态和动态语义概述，以吸引有经验的开发者。
• [pjmlp] 提到Pony的原设计者Sylvan Clebsch目前在微软研究类似Verona的项目，并指出Guido也在该项目中。这可能暗示Pony的部分设计思想在这些新语言中得到延续。
• [throwaway328] 对Hacker News的讨论参与者抱怨Pony文档和代码示例不够直观表示不满，认为这些开发者过于急躁，并建议Pony团队在官网导航菜单中添加“在浏览器中试用”的链接以提升用户体验。
• [delifue] 指出Pony与Rust的不同之处在于Pony允许容易的引用循环，并解释了Pony中的iso引用如何避免共享可变数据，这是其创新的一个关键点。
• [germandiago] 认为在实际项目中，有时可以牺牲正确性以换取开发速度，特别是在某些代码在99%的情况下都能正常工作时，这与Pony强调的“不允许不正确性”形成对比。
• [sbt] 表达了对Pony的喜爱，尤其是其引用能力和actor模型的匹配性，但遗憾的是Pony缺乏大公司的支持和特定的 niche 使用场景。
• [zelphirkalt] 关注Pony的生态系统，尤其是其可用的库，并提供了Pony官网上的包列表链接。
• [gpderetta] 对Pony宣称的“无死锁”特性提出质疑，认为死锁自由通常是算法属性而非语言属性，并询问Pony是否保证所有情况下的前进进度，或者是否需要在实现中提供死锁自由的证明。
• [ramon156] 抱怨Pony官网上的文档缺乏实际信息和使用场景示例，建议提供更多关于何时使用Pony的指导以及实际项目和公司的使用案例。

补充讨论：
• Pony的GC（ORCA）和共享模型被提及，并提供了Zulip聊天室和每周办公时间的链接。
• 一些评论提供了相关的讨论和资源链接，如四年前的相关讨论和关于选择编程语言的播客。
• 讨论中涉及Pony的设计者和相关新语言项目，如Verona，这可能为Pony的背景和未来发展提供更多信息。

44719413.article_content:
What is Pony?
¶
Pony is an open-source, object-oriented,
actor-model
,
capabilities-secure
, high-performance programming language.
If you are looking to jump in and get started with Pony
right now
, you can try it in your browser using the
Pony Playground
. Keep reading if you are interested in what makes Pony different and why you should consider using it.
If you are interested in the early history of Pony and how it came into existence, you’re in luck:
“An Early History of Pony”
.

data.title: The EU could be scanning your chats by October 2025
data.author: saubeidl
data.article_summary: 丹麦在其担任欧盟轮值主席国首日重新推出了备受争议的儿童性虐待（CSAM）扫描法案，即所谓的“Chat Control”提案。该提案要求所有在欧洲运营的 messaging 服务扫描用户聊天记录，包括加密信息，旨在打击网上儿童性虐待内容的传播。然而，自2022年5月以来，该提案一直未能获得足够的支持票数。丹麦计划在2025年10月14日前通过新规则，目前正努力在各成员国之间寻求妥协。隐私倡导者和技术专家担心该法案会削弱加密保护，导致大规模监控风险。此前，比利时和波兰曾尝试修改提案，但均未获得广泛支持。与此同时，欧盟的ProtectEU战略也旨在赋予执法机构解密私人数据的能力，进一步引发对隐私和安全的担忧。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：欧盟是否会通过并实施对用户消息的扫描政策，以及该政策的影响和背后的动机。

不同观点：
• **反对并质疑政策的实际推行**：[westpfelia] 认为该政策提议只是个别国家的行为，最终不会得到大多数成员国的支持，媒体报道只是为了吸引点击。类似的，[ricardobeat] 也指出文章标题有误导性，提案还在审议中。
• **对隐私和自由的担忧**：[an_ko] 表达了对持续监视的恐惧，认为即使政策未实施，反复讨论本身就让人们生活在恐惧中。[rckt] 认为最终政府会成功推行政策，但这将迫使注重隐私的人寻找其他安全通信方式。[44za12] 强调政府对隐私的不重视，认为反复提出该提案表明隐私只是被看作一种障碍，而非权利。
• **政策推行的现实阻力**：[Roark66] 指出其国家会否决此类政策，因为之前已有过大规模反对示威。 [Dev6345789] 认为由于公民和议员无法直接提出法律，该类提案会反复出现直到通过。
• **政府动机和双重标准**：[tobyhinloopen] 质疑政府为何执着于监控普通民众的聊天，而 criminals 依然会使用真正的加密手段。[mvdwoord] 讽刺地建议政府高官应先公开自己的聊天记录以示表率。[busssard] 认为欧洲各国政府出于对内部和外部威胁的恐惧，普遍在侵蚀隐私权。[lifeinthevoid] 进一步指出，欧盟内部一些国家可能受俄罗斯影响，使得情况更加复杂。
• **技术替代方案的讨论**：[sunshine-o] 提出当前聊天应用都存在各种问题，并建议使用如 Gotify 或 ntfy 之类的工具，通过简单的消息传递和手动密钥交换机制来避免被大规模监控。[IlikeKitties] 则认为在公共聊天中，强制内容扫描可能有助于防止不当内容，如儿童色情内容的传播。

补充讨论：
• **对政策推行的疲惫感**：[an_ko] 和 [44za12] 都表达了对反复出现的监控政策提案的疲惫和无奈。
• **个别国家的立场**：[Roark66] 提到其国家因政治结构和公众压力，会否决此类政策。
• **技术实现的可能性**：[sunshine-o] 和 [IlikeKitties] 提出了替代性的技术解决方案，讨论如何在避免被监控的情况下实现简单通信。

争议焦点：政策的实际可行性、隐私与安全的平衡、以及政府推行监控的真正动机。

44720103.article_content:
Image credit: Pixabay
(Image credit: Pixabay)
Denmark has reintroduced the disputed child sexual abuse (CSAM) scanning bill on the first day of its EU Presidency
The so-called Chat Control proposal could be adopted as early as October 14, 2025
The proposal has been failing to attract the needed majority since May 2022
Denmark kicked off its EU Presidency on July 1, 2025, and, among its first actions, lawmakers swiftly reintroduced the controversial child sexual abuse (CSAM) scanning bill to the top of the agenda.
Having been deemed by critics as
Chat Control
, the bill aims to introduce new obligations for all messaging services operating in Europe to scan users' chats, even if they're encrypted.
The proposal, however, has been failing to attract the needed majority since May 2022, with
Poland's Presidency being the last to give up
on such a plan.
You may like
Experts "deeply concerned" by the EU plan to weaken encryption
Europol doesn't only want an encryption backdoor, but also your metadata
"A war against online anonymity" – why Switzerland wants to change its surveillance law and what's at stake
Denmark is a strong supporter of Chat Control. Now, the new rules could be adopted as early as October 14, 2025, if the Danish Presidency manages to find a middle ground among the countries' members.
Chat Control is back – what we know so far
(Image credit: Getty Images)
The
Danish Parliament
has not yet disclosed the contents of the new compromises. At the time of writing, we know that another meeting is scheduled for later this week (July 11), with lawmakers expected to deliberate on the bill on October 14 (see page 31 of the
agenda
).
We also know that among the objectives of the Danish EU Presidency, there's a commitment to "focus on strengthening the abilities to make use of the digital development for law enforcement when fighting serious crime, while also addressing the misuse of new technologies for criminal or harmful purposes,"
Denmark's program reads
.
So-called Chat Control aims to halt the spread of CSAM content online by scanning all communications, especially encrypted ones. Over the years, however, the proposal has seen some twists and turns as privacy advocates, technologists, and even politicians raised concerns.
Experts worry that these new obligations will undermine encryption protections.
Encryption
is a technology that the likes of WhatsApp, Signal, ProtonMail, and even the
best VPN
apps use to scramble users' messages into an unreadable form, preventing unauthorized access and guaranteeing that chats remain private.
As per its first version, all messaging software providers would be required to perform indiscriminate scanning of private messages to look for CSAM – so-called '
client-side scanning
'. The proposal was met with a strong backlash, and the European Court of Human Rights ended up
banning all legal efforts to weaken encryption
of secure communications in Europe.
In June 2024,
Belgium then proposed a new text
to target only shared photos, videos, and URLs, upon users' permission. This version didn't satisfy either the industry or voting EU members due to its coercive nature. As per the Belgian text, users must give consent to the shared material being scanned before being encrypted to keep using the functionality.
🇬🇧🚨 Under Danish leadership, #ChatControl is to be adopted as early as October 14! https://t.co/dKVuSlrSJX (p. 31)The decisive factor is Germany: neither Conservatives nor Socialists have yet declared digital privacy of correspondence and secure encryption to be a red line.
July 1, 2025
Fast-forward to February 2025, Poland tried to find a better compromise by making the
scanning of encrypted chats voluntary
instead of mandatory and classified as "prevention." While experts found this version a "major progress," they still lamented the risk of mass surveillance, and, ultimately, lawmakers failed to attract the needed majority.
We could then expect the Danish text to try finding a compromise that appeals to most of the country's members.
According to the former MEP for the German Pirate Party, Patrick Breyer, Denmark crucially needs to manage to convince Germany of its proposed text. The new government has not yet taken a position at the time of writing.
What's certain, however, is that the controversial CSAM scanning bill is far from being the only proposal threatening encryption in Europe.
In the latest of these efforts, on June 24, 2025, the EU Commission published the first step in its ProtectEU strategy, which looked to enable law enforcement bodies to
decrypt your private data
by 2030.
You might also like
Telegram pledges to exit the market rather than "undermine encryption with backdoors"
Chat Control 2.0? Experts urge the EU not to undermine encryption with new ProtectEU plan
Secure encryption and online anonymity are now at risk in Switzerland
See more Computing News
Chiara Castro
News Editor (Tech Software)
Chiara is a multimedia journalist committed to covering

data.title: Hologram v0.5.0
data.author: bartblast
data.article_summary: Hologram 0.5.0 发布，带来重大更新，包括性能提升、架构改进以及新功能，为未来发展奠定更稳固基础。执行速度从毫秒提升到微秒，支持实时交互如鼠标移动事件。新功能包括全面的会话和Cookie管理、新的HTTP传输层、实时重载和增量编译。新增高性能bitstring实现、基准测试基础设施和基础CRDT支持。会话管理支持完整的服务器端会话，Phoenix框架下完全互操作。Cookie支持包括自动编码/解码。事件系统增加对指针和鼠标移动事件的支持，并优化事件属性。实时重载功能自动检测文件变化并显示编译错误。CRDT实现支持无冲突复制数据类型和基于时间戳的自动冲突解决。增量编译提升构建速度，跳过未更改模块，并优化构建过程持久化。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Hologram作为Elixir全栈Web框架的优点、性能、使用场景及争议

不同观点：
• **支持与兴奋态度**：
  - [bartblast] 作为Hologram的开发者，强调v0.5.0版本的重大性能改进，如微秒级的执行时间、全面的会话管理、实时重载功能等，并展示其在实时交互和图形绘制上的优势。
  - [jamauro] 对Hologram能够构建离线能力的全栈Elixir应用表示兴奋和期待。
  - [christophilus] 认为Hologram为Elixir开发者提供了统一语言的优势，类似于其他全栈框架，表示会尝试使用。

• **与LiveView的比较与争议**：
  - [doodlesdev] 认为Hologram网站在页面导航速度上表现出色，但初始加载时间较慢，包含过多未使用的JavaScript。建议通过HTML预取和缓存头来优化，而不是依赖JS。
  - [dsiegel2275] 询问Hologram是否可以与现有的Phoenix应用共存，特别是为了满足离线和低带宽需求。

44690158.article_content:
Hologram v0.5.0 Released!
Hologram 0.5.0 represents a major evolution of the framework, delivering significant new features, performance improvements, and architectural changes that provide a more robust foundation for future development.
This release brings substantial performance enhancements across the entire stack - execution times have improved from milliseconds to microseconds in many core client-side operations, making Hologram fast enough to handle real-time interactions like mouse move events for drawing applications. To showcase these capabilities, I've prepared an
SVG Drawing Demo
that demonstrates smooth, responsive drawing using pointer move events.
Key highlights include the introduction of comprehensive session and cookie management, a new HTTP-based transport layer, live reload functionality for enhanced development experience, and incremental compilation for faster build times. The release also features a new high-performance bitstring implementation, extensive benchmarking infrastructure, and foundational CRDT support for future distributed features.
With over 950 commits since version 0.4.0, this release includes important architectural changes that improve both developer experience and runtime performance, while laying the groundwork for advanced features in upcoming releases.
New Features
Session Management
Complete session handling system
- Full server-side session support for storing and retrieving user data across requests
Session operations in pages and commands
- Added
put_session/3
,
get_session/2
,
get_session/3
, and
delete_session/2
functions available in both page and component inits and page and component command handlers
Phoenix session integration
- When used on top of Phoenix, Hologram is fully interoperable with Phoenix session (not applicable when used as a standalone framework)
Cookie Support
Full cookie management
- Added
put_cookie/3
,
put_cookie/4
,
get_cookie/2
,
get_cookie/3
and
delete_cookie/2
functions with support for all standard cookie options (http_only, secure, same_site, etc.)
Server-side cookie operations
- Cookies can be read and manipulated during both server-side page/component rendering and command execution
Automatic cookie encoding/decoding
- Elixir data types are automatically serialized/deserialized when stored in cookies
New Events
Pointer events support
- Added support for
pointer_move
,
pointer_cancel
,
pointer_down
,
pointer_up
events with pointer-specific properties
Mouse move event
- Added new
mouse_move
event with support for client coordinates, movement deltas, offset positions, and screen positions
Select event
- Implemented text
select
event
Live Reload for Development
File watching and auto-reload
- Automatic detection of file changes in
.ex
and
.holo
files with intelligent debouncing (1 second delay)
Compilation error overlay
- Beautiful error overlay that displays compilation errors
Phoenix CodeReloader integration
- Seamless integration with Phoenix's code reloading system
CRDT Implementation
Last Writer Wins (LWW) CRDT Map
- Complete conflict-free replicated data type implementation for distributed state management (foundational work for future distributed features)
Delta operations
- Support for computing and applying delta operations between CRDT states
Timestamp-based conflict resolution
- Automatic conflict resolution using microsecond-precision timestamps
Enhancements
New Bitstring Implementation
Complete bitstring rewrite
- New JavaScript bitstring class with significant performance improvements: ~ x50 rendering speed improvements (!)
Enhanced pattern matching
- Better support for complex bitstring patterns and bitstring segment operations
Optimized text handling
- Fast paths for text-based bitstrings and UTF-8 operations
Incremental Compilation
Module digest tracking
- Implemented module digest PLTs (Persistent Lookup Tables) that track BEAM definition digests for all modules using fast phash2 hashing
Smart recompilation
- Only recompiles modules that have actually changed by comparing old and new module digest PLTs
Call graph patching
- Incrementally updates the call graph using
CallGraph.patch/3
by removing vertices for deleted modules, rebuilding paths for edited modules, and adding new modules
Build performance optimization
- Significantly faster incremental builds as unchanged modules are skipped entirely, with detailed benchmarking showing the performance improvements. The speedup is 2x-10x depending on project size.
Build artifact persistence
- Automatic loading and dumping of module digest PLTs and call graph to disk for persistence across compilation cycles
Enhanced Event System
Enhanced mouse and pointer event properties
- Added comprehensive coordinate and movement tracking with fields:
client_x
,
client_y
,
movement_x
,
movement_y
,
offset_x
,
offset_y
,
page_x
,
page_y
,
screen_x
,
screen_y
Event inheritance improvements
- ClickEvent now inherits from PointerEvent for better event property consistency (Firefox and

data.author: bookofjoe

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：机械掺杂（机械作弊）在自行车比赛中的存在和检测

不同观点：
• jamesblonde认为Fabian Cancellera在2010年巴黎-鲁贝比赛中被广泛怀疑使用机械掺杂，且Greg LeMond曾指控Chris Froome在环法自行车赛中作弊。他还提到，现在自行车比赛会通过X光检查自行车是否有马达，且车手不再像以前那样频繁更换自行车。
• throwaway81523指出，检查自行车是否使用马达并不是新鲜事，相关检查早已成为常规操作，并提供了维基百科链接支持其观点。
• gwelson认为，相比其他运动，自行车比赛中的欺诈和作弊现象更为普遍，并提出疑问为何这一现象在自行车比赛中更为常见。
• jmcdowell推荐了一个关于机械掺杂的深度播客系列"Ghost in the Machine"，讨论了当前技术如何可能被用于作弊，并提到了Femke van den Driessche的案例。
• stdclass提供了视频证据，声称Wout van Aert在2016年的比利时越野赛中多次使用马达作弊。
• jonplackett简洁地表示，问题的答案是否定的，即没有使用机械掺杂。
• arduenika以幽默的方式质疑马达的尺寸问题，提到在一定尺度上，线粒体是细胞的能量工厂。
• carlhjerpe认为，高水平比赛中应持续使用X光检查自行车，以防止机械掺杂问题，并指出相比药物测试，X光检查对隐私的侵犯较小。
• jnsaff2推荐观看讽刺性作品"Tour de Pharmacy"，暗示对自行车比赛中作弊现象的讽刺。
• aeternum以讽刺口吻建议，将电磁铁嵌入道路表面来帮助特定自行车加速或减速，质疑机械掺杂的实际操作性。
• blakesterz提到了对Lance Armstrong的旧指控，并提供了一个相关视频链接。
• aaronrobinson认为机械掺杂早已存在，并不是新现象。
• floodfx质疑使用马达在比赛中的实际效益，提出在自行车比赛中减轻重量的重要性，并希望看到使用马达的重量/功率/时间比计算，认为在爬坡赛段中使用马达并不值得。

补充讨论：
• 评论中多次提到使用X光检查自行车以防止机械掺杂，这被认为是有效的预防措施。
• 对自行车比赛中作弊现象的普遍性和原因进行了讨论，尤其是相比其他运动，自行车比赛中的作弊现象更为突出。
• 提供了多个具体案例和视频链接，支持和反驳机械掺杂存在的观点。
• 争议焦点在于机械掺杂是否在当前比赛中仍然存在以及其操作性和实际效益。

data.title: Intercepting 3I/Atlas at Its Closest Approach to Jupiter with Juno Spacecraft
data.author: TheBlight
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了利用延寿的“朱诺”号探测器拦截星际天体3I/ATLAS的可能性。3I/ATLAS预计在2026年3月16日距木星5360万公里处经过。作者团队通过计算表明，若在2025年9月14日对“朱诺”施加2.675公里/秒的推力，它可以从木星轨道转变轨迹，拦截3I/ATLAS的飞行路径。借助“朱诺”上的多种科学仪器，可以近距离探测该星际天体的性质。该任务的可行性取决于“朱诺”剩余的燃料量，而其初始ΔV为2.74公里/秒，接近任务需求的2.675公里/秒。若成功实施，这将延长“朱诺”的科学寿命，并为其赋予新的探测目标。

Intercepting 3I/ATLAS at Its Closest Approach to Jupiter with the Rejuvenated Juno Spacecraft
Avi Loeb
4 min read
·
9 hours ago
--
9
Listen
Share
Zoom image will be displayed
The
Juno
spacecraft. (Image credit:
NASA
)
The interstellar object
3I/ATLAS
was discovered on July 1, 2025. It is expected to arrive at a distance of
53.6 million kilometers from Jupiter
on March 16, 2026.
In a new paper (accessible
here
) that I wrote with the brilliant Adam Hibberd and Adam Crowl, we show that applying a thrust of 2.675 kilometers per second on September 14, 2025 can bring the
Juno
spacecraft
from its orbit around Jupiter to intercept the path of 3I/ATLAS.
The
Juno
spacecraft, named after the
wife and sister of Jupiter
in Roman mythology, was launched from Cape Canaveral on August 5, 2011, and entered a
polar orbit
around Jupiter on July 5, 2016 to conduct scientific measurements of Jupiter’s composition, gravitational field, magnetic field, and polar magnetosphere.
Juno
was originally planned to be intentionally deorbited into Jupiter’s atmosphere, but has since been approved to continue orbiting.
The close encounter of 3I/ATLAS to Jupiter provides a rare opportunity to shift
Juno
from its current orbit around Jupiter to intercept the path of 3I/ATLAS at its closest approach to Jupiter. The instruments available on
Juno
, namely a near- infrared spectrometer, magnetometer, microwave radiometer, gravity science instrument, energetic particle detector, radio and plasma wave sensor, UV spectrograph and visible light camera/telescope, can all be used to probe the nature of 3I/ATLAS from a close distance.
Our analysis exploits the software package known as
Optimum Interplanetary Trajectory Software (OITS)
, developed by Adam Hibberd. OITS solves the Lambert problem for one orbital cycle only: given two times, what are the 2 orbital arcs that connect them? Assuming that the positions at the beginning of the arc and the end of the arc are known, then there are 2 solutions, a short way and a long way. Having the short way and long way solutions, the way with the maximum velocity thrust
∆V
is rejected, leaving the lowest
∆V
solution. This procedure is conducted iteratively with different trial values of the initial and final times, until OITS has converged on the overall minimum ∆V solution.
Our calculation focuses on an intercept, namely a flyby, since a rendezvous, where the target’s velocity is matched by the spacecraft, is out-of-the- question, owing to the excessively high hyperbolic speed of 3I/ATLAS relative to Jupiter, 65.9 kilometers per second.
Based on this approach, we used OITS for a
Juno ∆V
application window covering the present as at the time of writing (July 27, 2025) to the possible end of the mission which is currently scheduled to occur in September 2025.
The feasibility of intercepting 3I/ATLAS depends on the current amount of fuel available from the propulsion system of
Juno
. However, some inferences can be drawn from the total
∆V
available at the beginning of the Juno mission. On its interplanetary trajectory, Juno conducted 2 Deep Space Maneuvers, and 1 Jupiter orbital insertion, both of which would have placed a significant demand on the chemical propulsion employed by
Juno
(Hydrazine and oxidizer nitrogen tetroxide).
The fuel reservoir on Juno allows an overall initial
∆V
available of 2.74 kilometers per second, similar to the
∆V
of 2.675 kilometers per second required to intercept 3I/ATLAS. However, the similarity of these numbers motivated our paper. This value is similar to the required
∆V
for Juno to intercept 3I/ATLAS. Although the engine of
Juno
was not operated since 2017, the required
∆V
might potentially be within
Juno
’s performance envelope. In that case,
Juno
would be able to get close to 3I/ATLAS and use its instruments to probe the nature of the interstellar object and any cloud of gas or dust around it.
Our paper shows that applying a thrust of 2.6755 kilometers per second on September 9, 2025, can potentially bring the
Juno
spacecraft from its orbit around Jupiter to intercept the path of 3I/ATLAS. With
Juno
’s many instruments, a fly-by can probe the nature of 3I/ATLAS far better than telescopes on Earth. The desired thrust constitutes a Jupiter Oberth Maneuver which requires an application of
∆V
only 8 days prior to the originally intended termination date for
Juno
’s plunge into the atmosphere of Jupiter. Having delivered this thrust to diminish Juno’s altitude, a further
∆V
is subsequently delivered, constituting a Jupiter Oberth Maneuver and resulting in an eventual intercept of the target 3I/ATLAS on March 14, 2026. In total, an overall
∆V
of 2.1574 + 0.5181 = 2.6755 kilometers per second is utilized.
If doable, this exciting new goal will rejuvenate
Juno
’s mission and extend its scientific lifespan beyond March 14, 2026.
Small corrections to
Juno
’s path might be needed if cometary activity 3I/ATLAS will be intensified as it comes closer to the Sun and its non-gravitational

data.title: Tog on Interface: Tognazzini, Bruce
data.author: tambourine_man
data.article_summary: 《Tog on Interface》是Bruce Tognazzini于1992年出版的一本关于计算机用户界面设计的经典书籍。本书探讨了人机交互的基本原则和最佳实践，提供了关于如何设计用户友好界面的深入见解和实用建议。书中包含了大量的参考文献和索引，适合界面设计师和开发人员参考。书籍由Addison-Wesley出版，全书共331页，语言为英语。通过Internet Archive平台存档，文件大小为606.3M。

data.title: Nothing to watch – Experimental gallery visualizing 50k film posters
data.author: bj-rn
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对一个电影画廊网站的体验和功能发表不同看法，涉及界面设计、内容推荐、技术问题等方面。

不同观点：
• JKCalhoun认为该网站推荐的电影多为近期流行影片，缺乏经典和有深度的电影。他推荐了一个名为"1001 Movies to See Before You Die"的列表，认为通过观看这些电影可以获得丰富的观影经验，并暗指该网站迎合了大众口味而非深度影迷。

• mentalgear批评该网站过于注重形式而忽视功能，认为其用户体验设计存在问题，尽管视觉效果可能不错。

• robeastham对该网站表示极度赞赏，认为这是他长时间以来在相关平台上看到的最酷的东西，显示出个人对该网站的强烈喜爱。

• svennidal和Mashim对网站的技术问题表示困惑和不满，前者没有看到预期的效果且无错误信息，后者遇到技术故障，如控制台报错和图像缩放问题。

• alias_neo提到作为一个有密集恐惧症的人，对网站的“深度”选项感到不适，并建议展示更多海报和标题以增强用户体验。

• gethly表达了对电影推荐引擎的需求，提到曾有创建基于用户评分的推荐系统的想法，但因数据获取困难而未能实现。

• kingforaday通过回忆微软Silverlight技术，对该网站的技术实现进行了历史对比，认为虽然该网站不错，但过去已有类似实现。

• VladVladikoff认为用LLMs（大型语言模型）解决“无电影可看”的问题更为有效，指出电影海报海洋的视觉化虽然酷，但并非最佳解决方案。

• flint提到在访问网站时电脑风扇开始高速运转，暗示网站可能对硬件资源要求较高。

• world2vec分享了自己通过Criterion Films列表选择未看过的电影的方法，认为这种方法效果很好。

• samsaga2简单评价网站创意不错但界面糟糕。

• sarthaksoni对网站表示赞赏，并对创作动机表示好奇。

• jonathantf2提到使用高配置工作笔记本访问网站时，Edge浏览器崩溃的问题。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于网站的内容推荐和用户体验设计，部分用户如JKCalhoun和mentalgear对内容和设计提出批评，而robeastham则极为赞赏。
- 技术问题如网站渲染错误、浏览器崩溃等也是用户反馈的重要部分，如svennidal、Mashim和jonathantf2的反馈。
- 用户对电影推荐的需求和实现方式也有讨论，gethly和VladVladikoff提出了数据获取困难和LLMs作为推荐解决方案的可能性。

data.title: Show HN: Terminal-Bench-RL: Training Long-Horizon Terminal Agents with RL
data.author: Danau5tin
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者成功构建了一个基于强化学习（RL）的可扩展基础设施，能够在32块H100 GPU上训练长时程的终端编码代理。该项目基于UC Berkeley Sky Lab的rLLM框架，扩展了自定义环境和基础设施，用于终端代理训练。作者的Qwen3-32B代理在Stanford的TerminalBench榜单上成为表现最好的Qwen3代理，超过了包括GPT-4.1在内的其他代理。然而，由于高昂的计算成本，作者未能进行充分训练，但项目展示了在多节点集群上训练的潜力。项目还包括详细的训练设置、数据集准备、以及未来改进方向，如课程学习和数据集扩展。

不同观点：
• **TarasBob** 表示愿意为该项目提供资金支持，并已联系创作者，显示出对项目潜力的兴趣和实际支持的意愿。
• **tjungblut** 关注技术细节，指出项目中的强化学习是通过 "verl" 实现的，并引用了一篇论文《HybridFlow: A Flexible and Efficient RLHF Framework》来解释其原理，提供了相关资源链接。
• **OtherShrezzing** 对创作者以较低成本实现优异成绩表示赞赏，认为这揭示了大AI实验室的技术壁垒。

• **anorwell** 试图澄清一些误解，指出项目尚未涉及实际训练，并强调了系统框架对基准测试结果的影响，提供了相关基准测试排行榜的链接。

🤓 Terminal-Bench-RL: Training Long-Horizon Terminal Agents with Reinforcement Learning
TL;DR:
I successfully built stable RL training infrastructure that scales to 32x H100 GPUs across 4 bare metal nodes for training long-horizon terminal-based coding agents.
In doing so, I developed Terminal-Agent-Qwen3-32b to become the
highest scoring Qwen3 agent on
terminal-bench
. WITHOUT training! (currently under submission):
Unfortunately I am too GPU poor to train a SOTA coding agent 😅 (estimated £30k-£50k in compute required), but if anyone has the GPUs, this project should get you there!
This project builds upon the
rLLM framework
developed by UC Berkeley Sky Lab, extending it with custom environments and infrastructure specifically designed for terminal-based agent training.

💻💰 Training on $1M worth of compute
This image shows my training code running at full throttle on 32x H100's, distributed across a 4x bare metal node cluster, training Qwen3-32B. Thank you
Hyperbolic
for such a streamlined experience! This was fun!
Due to the extreme cost of this level of compute, I was not able to run it forever! So I made sure it worked and also ran the code on less extravagent hardware setups too.
Other training runs
I also ran Qwen3-32B training for longer on a 2x bare metal node cluster with 16x H100s:
Also 1 VM instance with 8x H100s:
My longest training run was using 2xA100s on a single VM instance, where I trained Qwen3-8B for over 60 steps:
Note: I did not expect the 8B to begin learning the complex behaviours required to solve the tasks in the dataset. However it was great to run the training through the dataset and ensure the code is stable.
🏆 Placing a spot on the Terminal Bench Leaderboard
Terminal bench
is a brilliant benchmark created by Stanford and
Laude Institute
to quantify agents' ability to complete complex tasks in the terminal.
Through prompt engineering & custom tool design, my Qwen3-32B agent outperformed Stanford's Terminus-Qwen3-235B-30A MoE agent, as well as Deepseek R1 & OpenAI's GPT-4.1 with Codex agent, to become the highest scoring Qwen3 agent on the leaderboard.
The results.json for the eval run can be found
here
.
I am sure that with the compute budget for training, my agent would climb the leaderboard significantly.
Agent details
My motivation behind this entire project was to place on the leaderboard of terminal bench by using RL to train a sophisticated LLM agent. In order to do so, I developed the tools (inspired by Claude Code) which a capable AI agent would use to help complete complex terminal/coding tasks, as well as a
system message
which encouraged the agent to use those tools and approach the task in a specific way.
These tools can be found
here
and include:
📝 Todo Management
: Planning and tracking task progress
📁 File Operations
: Read, write, and edit files
🔍 Search Tools
: Grep, glob, and ls for file exploration
⚡ Bash Execution
: Run terminal commands wit

data.title: Wikimedia Foundation Challenges UK Online Safety Act Regulations
data.author: Nurw
data.article_summary: 下周，2025年7月22日和23日，伦敦高等法院将审理维基媒体基金会针对《英国网络安全法》分类规定的法律挑战。维基媒体基金会运营着维基百科及其他维基媒体项目，认为该法规威胁到维基百科及全球志愿贡献者的隐私和安全。基金会的法律挑战聚焦于这些新分类规定，这些规定可能对维基百科施加最严格的义务（1类义务），包括验证贡献者身份等，这将增加负担并威胁贡献者的隐私和安全，可能导致数据泄露、骚扰甚至迫害。同时，这也会分散资源，影响维基百科的维护和改进。此案是首次对《网络安全法》分类规定的法律挑战，并有英国维基百科志愿者作为共同原告参与。维基媒体基金会呼吁法院保护维基百科及其贡献者的隐私和安全。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：英国《网络安全法》（OSA）及其相关法规的合法性、适用性以及对互联网自由的影响。

不同观点：
• **Roark66**：将个人加密定为非法与《网络安全法》的比较，批评政府对复杂技术问题的理解不足，并提到英国已有法律要求用户向警方提供加密密钥，否则将面临监禁。
• **supermatt**：认为应通过家长控制来处理未成年人的内容访问问题，而非依赖大型科技公司。主张家长应负起责任，而不是让问题变得更复杂。
• **braiamp**：支持Wikimedia基金会挑战《网络安全法》的分类规定，认为根据现有法律，维基百科不应被归为1类义务对象，但分类规定可能导致这种情况。
• **chippiewill**：对Wikimedia的法律挑战持怀疑态度，认为分类规定是法定工具，可以进行司法审查，但Wikimedia没有提出为何这些规定是非法的，只是表达了不同意。
• **noodlesUK**：不喜《网络安全法》，认为法律过长且难以理解，但对Wikimedia的法律挑战基础存疑，指出不能仅因为“不喜欢”就挑战法律。
• **Havoc**：建议通过阻止英国政府IP来抗议。
• **miohtama**：提到工党正在考虑禁止VPN，进一步收紧网络控制。
• **hermitcrab**：分析《网络安全法》对无成人内容的论坛的影响，提供相关法律解释。
• **bargainbin**：反对政府以“保护个人自由”为名限制自由，认为这是政府利用恐慌来限制个人自由。
• **perihelions**：批评Wikimedia的特殊待遇要求，认为其与开放互联网的精神相悖，并指出Wikimedia的利益不代表公众利益。
• **jonathantf2**：惊讶于Jimmy Wales尚未通过大横幅向英国用户募捐以应对该法律。
• **IlikeKitties**：主张大多数网站应集体阻止英国用户访问以抗议法律，认为这样才能有效推翻法律。
• **crtasm**：询问关于听证会的结果和何时可能得知结果。
• **cft**：认为Wikimedia的法律挑战立场不够原则，仅关注分类规定而不反对整个1类义务或《网络安全法》本身。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于《网络安全法》的分类规定是否合理，特别是对于维基百科这样的非营利性网站是否应被纳入最严格的1类义务。
• 不同评论者对法律挑战的合法性和成功可能性持不同看法，部分评论者对Wikimedia的立场表示支持，而另一些则批评其缺乏原则性。
• 家长控制和个人责任的讨论也成为一个重要议题，部分评论者认为家长应负起责任，而非依赖政府或科技公司。

44721403.article_content:
17 July 2025
— Next week, on 22 and 23 July 2025, the High Court of Justice in London will hear the Wikimedia Foundation’s
legal challenge
to the
Categorisation Regulations
of the United Kingdom (UK)’s Online Safety Act (OSA).
The Wikimedia Foundation, the non-profit that operates Wikipedia and other
Wikimedia projects
, announced its legal challenge earlier this year, arguing that the regulations endanger Wikipedia and the global community of volunteer contributors who create the information on the site.
“The Court has an opportunity in this case to set a global precedent for protecting public interest projects online,” said
Stephen LaPorte
, General Counsel at the Wikimedia Foundation. “Wikipedia is the backbone of knowledge on the internet. It’s the only top-ten website operated by a non-profit and one of the highest-quality datasets used in training Large Language Models (LLMs). We trust the Court will protect Wikipedia—a vital encyclopedic resource—from rules crafted for the internet’s riskiest commercial sites and, in doing so, safeguard the open internet for everyone”.
Information on Wikipedia is written and curated by a global community of nearly 260,000 volunteer contributors. These volunteers set and enforce policies to ensure that information on the platform is fact-based, neutral, and attributed to reliable sources. Over the last 25 years, this human-centered content moderation model has established Wikipedia as an unparalleled resource for reliable information in over 300 languages; its 65 million articles are viewed more than 15 billion times per month worldwide.
The Wikimedia Foundation shares the UK government’s commitment to promoting online environments where everyone can safely participate. The organization is not bringing a general challenge to the OSA as a whole, nor to the existence of the Category 1 duties themselves. Rather, the legal challenge focuses solely on the new Categorisation Regulations that risk imposing Category 1 duties (the OSA’s most stringent obligations) on Wikipedia.
If enforced on Wikipedia, Category 1 demands would undermine the privacy and safety of Wikipedia’s volunteer contributors, expose the encyclopedia to manipulation and vandalism, and divert essential resources from protecting people and improving Wikipedia, one of the world’s most trusted and widely used
digital public goods
.
For example, the Foundation would be required to verify the identity of many Wikipedia contributors, undermining the privacy that is central to keeping Wikipedia volunteers safe. In addition to being exceptionally burdensome, this requirement—which is just one of several Category 1 demands—could expose contributors to data breaches, stalking, lawsuits, or even imprisonment by authoritarian regimes. Additional details about the concerning impacts of the Category 1 duties on Wikipedia are available in this
blog post
.
The Wikimedia Foundation will be joined in the case by longtime UK-based volunteer Wikipedia contributor
User:Zzuuzz
as a joint claimant. Their voluntary participation highlights what is at stake in this case for the everyday people who read and contribute to Wikimedia projects. It presents the perspective of a Wikipedia volunteer on how the OSA Categorisation Regulations directly threaten the ability of contributors to participate in knowledge sharing on Wikipedia, as well as compromising their rights to privacy, safety, free speech, and association.
The legal challenge is the first to be issued against the OSA’s Categorisation Regulations, as well as the first with a volunteer Wikipedia editor participating as a joint claimant. It follows years of dialogue with regulators and policymakers, in which the Foundation expressed its concerns, as well as
warnings from the UK Parliament
and
civil society
.
“Our concerns on the looming threats to Wikipedia and its contributors remain unaddressed”, said Phil Bradley-Schmieg, Lead Counsel at the Wikimedia Foundation. “We are taking action now to protect Wikipedia’s volunteers, as well as the global accessibility and integrity of free knowledge. We call on the Court to defend the privacy and safety of Wikipedia’s volunteer contributors from flawed legislation”.
Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects are safe and important resources through which people across the UK—and the wider world—learn, share knowledge, collaborate, and gain media literacy. Thousands of volunteer Wikipedia contributors are based in the UK, and Wikipedia hosts content from cultural institutions such as the British Library and Wellcome Collection. Content on Wikipedia and other Wikimedia projects was viewed 776 million times last month in the UK alone. Moreover, Wikipedia is used to preserve and promote cultural heritage in the UK, including Indigenous and minority languages such as Welsh. The
Welsh language version of Wikipedia
is the single most popular Welsh language website in the world and is an
official component of the curriculum
in Wales.

data.title: Stop selling “unlimited”, when you mean “until we change our minds”
data.author: heymax054
data.article_summary: 文章批评了AI公司以“无限”作为噱头吸引用户，随后对高频用户实施限制的策略。以Anthropic对Claude Pro和Claude Max添加每周使用限制为例，文章指出这种“诱导切换”做法破坏了开发者对平台的信任。文章强调，受影响的是深度依赖平台的早期用户和付费大户，而这种限制会导致用户寻找替代方案或延迟采用AI工具。Kilo Code则提出了一种更透明的按需付费模式，避免隐藏限制，并提供本周存入 credits 享受300% bonus 的促销活动，呼吁公司对定价保持诚实和透明。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：订阅制、无限量服务的可行性及其实际执行问题，尤其在AI服务中的应用。

不同观点：
• **epistasis**：用户在尝试取消订阅时遇到困难，批评Anthropic的取消流程不透明，认为这是不良的订阅陷阱（dark pattern）。不过最终成功找到取消选项。
• **TrackerFF**：认为提供“无限”服务的公司容易受到极少数重度用户的过度使用影响，建议引入结转（rollover）机制，让未使用的额度延至下个月，以提升用户体验。
• **mentalgear**：引用Apple的“无限”维修服务为例，指出“无限”不等于免费，并批评某些AI取代开发者的说法是不切实际的炒作。
• **conartist6**：强烈反对“AI将取代开发者”的观点，认为这是对技术潜力的过度夸大，类似于认为所有音乐都会使用自动调音。
• **cedws**：认为“无限计划”本质上是不稳定的，要么卖家亏损，要么买家受骗。建议按使用量付费更公平。
• **raffael_de**：认为“无限”和“终身”定价模式往往不可持续，可能导致公司破产或欺诈行为。
• **superasn**：理解用户对使用上限的挫败感，但指出一些用户过度使用资源导致平台对所有人更难持续。认为更透明的按使用量定价可能是解决方案。
• **sudhirj**：质疑Anthropic是否真的承诺过“无限”服务，认为用户可能误解了服务条款。
• **aeon_ai**：指出AI公司的单位经济不支持对计算密集型服务实行固定费率，透明度问题加剧了这种情况。建议更透明的按使用量定价或显著提高固定费率。
• **Dolores12**：支持Anthropic对重度用户的限制措施，称之为“滥用者”。
• **mmillin**：质疑Anthropic是否真的使用过“无限”一词，认为用户对“无限”的理解可能存在误差。
• **mattlondon**：认为大公司凭借其规模和基础设施优势会挤压小公司的生存空间，租用他人GPU的小公司难以竞争。
• **haritha-j**：认为当前的定价模式不可持续，类似于Uber Eats早期通过优惠吸引用户的策略，最终会面临调整。
• **jstummbillig**：批评对AI行业过度保守的看法，认为在快速变化的行业中应该允许试错和创新，同时保持对用户的尊重。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于“无限”服务的定义及其可行性，特别是在AI服务中的实际执行和用户体验问题。
• 用户对取消订阅困难的抱怨与公司对重度用户资源使用的限制是两个主要讨论方向。
• 不同用户对AI技术潜力的看法存在分歧，有人认为AI过度炒作，有人认为按使用量付费更公平。

Bottom line:
Anthropic just added weekly limits to Claude Pro ($20/month) and Claude Max ($200/month), affecting their heaviest users of Claude Code…mid-workflow.
Why it matters:
This is the same playbook we’ve seen AI companies
use before
—hook users with "unlimited" access, then cap the power users who matter most.
Theo from t3.chat
summed it up perfectly: "No free lunch lasts forever."
The Same Playbook, Different Day
Here's how the
AI pricing bait-and-switch
works:
Launch with
generous/unlimited limits
Build user
dependency
Add
caps
targeting "less than 5%" of users
Frame as "sustainability" or "fairness"
Sound familiar? That's because we've
seen this movie before
. Cursor
did it
. Windsurf
followed
. GitHub Copilot
tightened screws
. Now
Claude Code
.
The thing is, Anthropic isn't wrong about the economics. Running Claude Sonnet or Opus models costs real money—we're talking about serious compute infrastructure here. But that's
precisely
why the bait-and-switch approach is so damaging to the developer community.
That "5%" Drives
Everything
Who actually gets hit by these limits:
Power users
with deep workflow integration
Early adopters
who took platform risks
Team influencers
who drive organizational adoption
$200/month Claude Max subscribers
doing serious work
The real damage:
You're not frustrating 5% of users—you're breaking trust with the exact people who drive growth and adoption.
The Trust Tax Adds Up
Every bait-and-switch makes developers hedge bets instead of fully committing. Or maybe, at “best” they delay AI adoption, waiting for "stable" pricing. Or perhaps worst of all…self-limit usage to avoid hitting caps.
@dvyio on Twitter/X called this “
vibe limiting
”
And on HackerNews,
wowfunhappy observed
:
I'm probably not going to hit the weekly limit, but it makes me nervous that the limit is weekly as opposed to every 36 hours or something. If I do hit the limit, that's it for the entire week—a long time to be without a tool I've grown accustomed to!
When developers get "rate limit exceeded" while debugging at 2 AM, they're not thinking about your infrastructure costs—they're shopping for alternatives.
The Economics Aren't Secret
We all know AI inference costs money. Developers get resource constraints…we have them ourselves!
What we don't get:
Being sold "unlimited" and then discovering asterisks after we've built workflows around your tool.
What we want:
Transparent costs upfront so we can make informed decisions.
As
landl0rd on HN
pointed out:
You can tell how it's intentional with both OpenAI and Anthropic by how they're intentionally made opaque. I cant see a nice little bar with how much I've used versus have left on the given rate limits
A Different Approach: More AI for Less Money
At Kilo Code, we skipped the charade:
No "unlimited" promises
with hidden limits
Transparent pay-per-use
from day one
You control spending
and usage
Credits never expire
(bonus credits do)
This week only:
300% bonus credits on every deposit

data.title: Show HN: CUDA Fractal Renderer
data.author: tripplyons
data.article_summary: CUDA Fractal Renderer 是一个能够快速渲染分形的工具。它使用CUDA进行并行计算，支持通过指定种子生成不同分形，并可使用 `--grid-size` 参数并行生成多个分形。项目依赖CUDA和uv工具，安装和使用步骤包括设置虚拟环境、运行渲染命令以及查看生成的 `output.png` 图像文件。代码格式化可通过运行 `./format.sh` 完成。该项目基于MIT许可证，主要使用Python和CUDA编写。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕代码实现、技术细节和相关工具使用的讨论

不同观点：
• **neomantra**：赞赏代码的简洁和易于检查，并提到处理volumes是一个重大变化，同时建议将矩阵暴露给CLI以进行插值操作，还提到过去在GPGPU方面的工作经验，对比该实现的范围较小但更易理解。
• **sestep**：感谢提供了uv.lock文件，提到过去在尝试运行只有requirements.txt的研究项目时的困难，强调了解决老化代码的麻烦。
• **dcanelhas**：对代码中存在atomic add操作提出质疑，认为基于block/thread索引，不同线程不应该修改同一个像素。
• **porphyra**：表达了对用Python编写CUDA代码的喜爱，认为代码简洁是当前技术进步的体现。
• **bsenftner**：建议尝试分形体积计算或分形动画，认为这是CUDA值得探索的方向。
• **almostgotcaught**：提出一个相关问题，询问如何从图形代码（如DirectX或OpenGL）调用CUDA，而不是像当前代码那样不直接绘制到屏幕。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现的简洁性与可操作性是讨论的重点，neomantra和sestep都提到了代码易于理解和运行的优点。
• 对CUDA代码中的具体技术细节（如atomic add的必要性）存在争议，dcanelhas对代码的实现细节提出了疑问。
• 对CUDA在其他领域（如分形计算和图形代码集成）的应用提出了展望，bsenftner和almostgotcaught分别提出了分形计算的可能性和CUDA与图形API的集成问题。
• 历史经验的分享（如neomantra提到过去的GPGPU工作）为讨论增加了深度，提供了背景信息。

data.title: Exploiting zero days in abandoned hardware
data.author: ingve
data.article_summary: 本文总结了在DistrictCon的首次Junkyard竞赛中成功利用两款停产网络设备的过程，并获得“最具创新性利用技术”亚军。研究显示，停产硬件由于缺乏更新，存在未修复的漏洞，成为攻击者的理想目标。团队利用了Netgear WGR614v9路由器和Bitdefender Box V1的安全漏洞，通过链式攻击获得远程控制权限。对于Netgear，团队通过UPnP守护进程的多个漏洞（包括认证绕过、缓冲区溢出和命令注入）实现攻击。对于Bitdefender Box，则通过未经认证的固件降级漏洞和命令注入实现攻击。这些设备因停产而无法获得安全更新，导致其易受攻击。详细技术分析可在Trail of Bits的代码库中找到。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：EOL（生命周期终止）设备的安全性及处理方法

不同观点：
• [dguido] 认为应该公开EOL设备的漏洞，以便用户学习和理解如何编写和应对这些漏洞。他提到未来会公开更多此类信息，并提供了具体设备（如Netgear WGR614v9和BitDefender Box 1）的漏洞链接。
• [myself248] 指出拥有EOL设备的用户不一定要丢弃设备，但需要权衡继续使用的风险。他建议消费者在购买设备时考虑其整个安全生命周期，包括制造商的支持承诺和社区固件选项，并暗示如果设备不支持OpenWRT等开源固件，就不应购买。
• [bornfreddy] 对“无更新即易受攻击”的说法持怀疑态度，认为漏洞一直存在，只是发现技术有所进步。他质疑为何废弃硬件会比新路由器更危险，并认为除非设备支持OpenWRT等固件，否则成熟度带来的安全性有限。
• [ectospheno] 提供了一种替代方案，使用Dell电脑、Intel四端口网卡和OpenBSD系统，认为这些硬件和系统更新更有保障，并能提供更长的支持时间。
• [jgalt212] 提出关于Android TV OS是否为Sony等电视的计划报废的问题，暗示操作系统可能被设计为在一定时间后失去支持。
• [nickpsecurity] 讨论了安全更新机制的平衡问题，提出一种需要用户确认的签名内容更新机制，并建议在最低层次的固件更新中加入物理交互（如跳线或开关）以防止恶意更新。他还提到了一种ROM/flash组合的实现方式。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于EOL设备是否必然更危险，以及如何在安全性和用户控制之间取得平衡。
• 提出的解决方案包括使用开源固件（如OpenWRT）、选择支持长时间更新的硬件（如Dell和Intel）、以及设计更加安全的更新机制（如物理交互和签名确认）。
• 讨论还涉及了计划报废的概念，特别是在智能电视和操作系统更新支持方面。

44682450.article_content:
We successfully exploited two discontinued network devices at
DistrictCon’s inaugural Junkyard
competition in February, winning runner-up for
Most Innovative Exploitation Technique
. Our exploit chains demonstrate why end-of-life (EOL) hardware poses persistent security risks: when manufacturers stop releasing updates, unpatched vulnerabilities remain frozen in time like fossils, creating perfect targets for attackers.
Both of the devices we exploited, a
Netgear WGR614v9 router
and a
BitDefender Box V1
, were fairly popular devices designed to protect your home network. But since both have gone years without updates, we were able to fully exploit them remotely from the local network.
Figure 1: DistrictCon trophy
With the
second DistrictCon Junkyard competition
being announced for early 2026, we would like to share our experience and research from the first one. Our full analysis is available on the
Trail of Bits exploits repo
for readers interested in the complete technical details.
First, we developed three ways (videos
1
,
2
, and
3
) to hack the Netgear router by chaining multiple LAN-side vulnerabilities in the UPnP daemon, including authentication bypass, buffer overflows, and command injection, which gave us a remote root shell. We then exploited the Bitdefender Box (
video
) by leveraging a LAN-side unauthenticated firmware downgrade vulnerability combined with command injection in the firmware validation process, which also gave us a remote root shell.
Device analysis and firmware extraction
For the Netgear device, we disassembled it and identified debugging interfaces, data storage chips, and the SOC. Since Netgear provides firmware online, we downloaded it rather than extracting it ourselves. We used binwalk and unblob to recursively unpack the firmware, ran a port scan to identify interesting network services, and logged in to the serial console to check running processes, LAN-facing services, CPU specs, kernel version, and enabled mitigations. We initially looked at httpd but then pivoted to upnpd.
For the Bitdefender Box V1, we found a serial port, but the shell was locked down. We managed to extract firmware through the SPI flash chip and tried to get the latest version by reverse engineering the update mechanism, but the update servers were offline. We found what we think is the latest version by scraping APK mirroring websites since the firmware was included in the APKs. Without a shell on the device, we emulated the httpd binary locally using QEMU user mode for dynamic testing.
Exploiting the Netgear router’s UPnP
The Netgear WGR614v9 router runs a MIPS32-based system with multiple network services. After connecting to its UART interface (the serial debug port exposed on the board as “JP1”), we gained low-level system access during the boot process.
Figure 2: Netgear WGR614v9 router board
We focused on the Universal Plug-and-Play (UPnP) daemon: a service designed to simplify device discovery and configuration on networks. UPnP accepts SOAP messages (XML-formatted commands) to control router functions, making it a prime target due to its complex parsing requirements and privileged system access.
After completing our analysis, our exploitation chain leveraged four vulnerabilities:
An authentication bypass in the SOAP message handler that allowed password resets
Three buffer overflow vulnerabilities in both the BSS and stack memory regions
In our first exploit, bashsledding, we showcase an interesting variation of the classic nopsled technique. After discovering two ROP gadgets that can invoke “system,” we sprayed our shell command payload into NVRAM, which is memory-mapped into all processes, through the router’s domain-blocking feature. By prepending sequences of spaces (our “nops”) before the command and regardless of the exact landing position, the bash interpreter would harmlessly process spaces until reaching our command, creating a “sled” of valid shell syntax rather than CPU instructions. This technique provided reliable code execution.
The last exploit we demonstrated,
bigfish_littlepond
, cleverly pivots a limited memory corruption bug into a stronger command injection. The BSS overflow is used to modify an adjacent string pointer representing shell commands. Given the presence of the “
bpa_monitor
” string in upnpd and an exploitable command injection in that binary, we changed it to launch the
bpa_monitor
binary. An additional request containing our injection payload allows for full code execution.
You can find the full exploit code and writeup
on GitHub
, as well as videos for
bashsledding
,
break_block_bof
(our second exploit, not mentioned here), and
bigfish_littlepond
.
Breaking the Bitdefender Box with outdated firmware
The Bitdefender Box v1 represents an ironic target: a security appliance designed to protect home networks from threats, discontinued in July 2021. Created around 2017, it was part of a trend of AV vendors expanding into hardware security devices with subscript

data.article_summary: 《英国在线安全法》生效后，要求色情网站及成人内容平台实施用户年龄验证，导致英国VPN等规避工具的使用激增。专家早有预期，其他实施类似法律的国家也出现过类似趋势。该法要求网站对访问者进行“高效”年龄验证，包括上传身份证和自拍。虽然已有超过6,600家网站引入年龄检查，但规避手段如使用《死亡搁浅》游戏自拍绕过验证也开始流行。VPN下载量在iOS设备上增长显著，Proton VPN、Windscribe等服务报告用户激增。数字权利倡导者担心，此类技术手段可能带来长远后果，而非解决根本问题。同时，更多科技公司如微软也开始引入年龄验证。

不同观点：
• Veliladon认为，现行法律是由基督教民族主义者推动的，目的是泄露色情用户的个人身份信息（PII），并通过持续威胁平台以获得政治控制权。法律的实施超前于技术发展，例如Apple和Google的匿名认证技术尚未成熟。
• digitalsushi认为，随着内容过滤技术的进步，互联网可能面临更加分散和审查的风险。他提出，如果网络审查加剧，可能会回归类似杂志的旧模式，即通过编辑筛选内容，虽然这与当前注意力短暂的环境可能不兼容。

• faxmeyourcode关注未成年人暴露于不当内容的问题，认为虽然父母有责任，但环境影响也很大，且社交平台会推荐更多明确内容。
• izzydata建议创建一个全新的互联网基础设施，不依赖现有网络，避免受当前法律的限制。
• bilekas讽刺地表示，既然可以通过勾选框同意条款和条件，那么也可以通过勾选框验证年龄。
• bikeshed批评工党没有对法律进行任何修改就允许其生效。
• Fraaaank提问，为何法律不要求VPN提供商验证用户年龄。

• 争议焦点在于法律是否在技术尚未成熟时过早实施，以及这些法律是否真正为了保护用户或隐藏其他政治目的。
• 讨论还涉及到技术规避手段的有效性，如使用VPN、Tor等，以及未来可能出现的替代方案（如数字杂志）。
• 未成年人的网络保护问题也是讨论的重要部分，各方对如何解决这一问题存在不同看法。
