More Honey Bees Dying, Even as Antibiotic Use Halves
More Honey Bees Dying, Even as Antibiotic Use Halves
Despite tighter restrictions on antibiotics used in Canadian beekeeping, honey bee death rates are still rising.
A new study led by University of Guelph researchers, published in
Nature Sustainability
, is the first large-scale project to assess antibiotic usage trends and their impact on honey bee health in Canada.
The withdrawal of antibiotics, following recent regulation changes, was one of the top predictors of honey bee overwintering mortality — a result that surprised lead author Dr.
Brendan Daisley
.
Dr. Brendan Daisley
“You’d assume the lessening of antibiotics might be associated with improved health outcomes, especially since antibiotics are so overused,” says Daisley, a postdoctoral researcher in the
College of Biological Science
. “But without effective alternatives, it seems the bees have developed a dependency on them.”
Using national survey data, researchers investigated more than 700,000 honey bee colonies per year between 2015 and 2023. Colony losses varied by province, but overwintering mortality rose from an average of less than 20 to over 40%, even as antibiotic usage halved, decreasing from approximately 50 to 25% nationally.
During the period studied, a new framework in 2018 put forth by the World Health Organization (WHO) and adopted by U.S. and Canadian agencies decreased over-the-counter access for certain beekeeping antibiotics.
This was done to address antimicrobial resistance (AMR) — the rising resistance to antibiotics that makes infectious diseases more difficult to treat. AMR is one of top 10 public threats facing humanity, according to WHO.
“We didn’t know the repercussions of these global changes in antimicrobial stewardship,” he says. “But it shows one of the most important drivers of honey bee mortality rates is likely infectious disease, and the imbalance between ‘bad’ and ‘good’ microbes.”
‘Microbial apocalypse’ could explain global colony loss, rising food costs
Daisley is one of few scientists who study honey bees’ entire bacterial community, known as their microbiome, as a way to assess their health.
“It’s a catch-22 — we know antibiotics are very useful for controlling disease outcomes, but they also disrupt the microbiome and do not distinguish between harmful and beneficial bacteria,” says Daisley. “We could be experiencing a microbial apocalypse in front of our eyes.”
The findings are a major breakthrough in microbiome research, he says, and may help explain record losses of the world’s bee colonies.
Millions of colonies lost in the U.S. alone are already leading to the rising costs of honey and pollination services, Daisley says, as beekeepers are forced to increase imports of bees to compensate.
This further translates to rising food costs, decreased crop yields and the disruption of global food security.
‘All interconnected’: One Health approach needed for alternatives
In addition to antibiotic usage, researchers identified another unexpected predictor of honey bee mortality: nitrogen dioxide (NO2), a common air pollutant from diesel exhaust.
NO2 degrades floral odours and disrupts the bees’ ability to forage, researchers say, which could be contributing to colony loss.
“It’s all interconnected, and in my opinion, all links back to microbial ecology and the microbial homeostasis of pollinators,” Daisley says.
Given the complex relationships between bees’ microbiomes, their health and their environment, researchers call for a
One Health
approach, a systems-level view that assesses
human, animal and environmental health more holistically
.
“Honey bees epitomize the principles of One Health by serving as a tangible example of the interconnectedness of human, animal and environmental well-being — particularly through their microbiome, which reflects and mediates the impacts of ecological stressors, agricultural practices and disease transmission across systems,” Daisley says.
Solutions to stop colony loss will require the One Health approach, as factors like NO2 must be considered alongside antibiotic alternatives like probiotics.
Daisley co-leads the Canadian Bee Gut project to investigate the microbes of bees
In this emerging field, bee probiotics are still in development and far from widespread adoption. Daisley leads research to characterize several different probiotics’ mechanisms of action within the bees’ intestinal tracts.
“But we need more funding to support the study of alternatives,” Daisley says. “The next aim is also to comprehensively characterize the microbiome of bees, to develop a baseline understanding so we have something to compare it to.”
To accomplish that, Daisley and Dr.
Emma Allen-Vercoe
(
Department of Molecular and Cellular Biology
) lead
the Canadian Bee Gut project
at U of G, a nationwide crowdsourcing initiative that began in 2022. The project collects samples from about 1,000 beehives each year from every
44727420.article_summary: 尽管加拿大限制了养蜂业中抗生素的使用，蜜蜂的死亡率仍在上升。一项由圭尔夫大学研究人员主导的研究发现，随着抗生素使用减半，蜜蜂的越冬死亡率反而从不到20%上升到超过40%。研究表明，抗生素的减少可能导致蜜蜂对致病微生物的抵御能力下降，因为它们的微生物群受到破坏。此外，二氧化氮（NO2）污染也被发现是蜜蜂死亡率上升的一个意外因素，因为它干扰了蜜蜂的觅食能力。研究人员呼吁采用“同一健康”方法，综合考虑人类、动物和环境健康，寻找替代抗生素的解决方案，如益生菌。目前，加拿大正在开展一个全国性项目，研究蜜蜂的微生物群以应对这一问题。
44727420.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：蜜蜂种群健康下降的原因及相关因素

不同观点：
• JumpCrisscross：蜂蜜蜂并非北美本土物种，它们在与本土传粉者（如大黄蜂）的竞争中占优势，导致生物多样性下降。此外，家庭后院的养蜂活动可能无意中消灭了本地的大黄蜂和蝴蝶种群。
• mushroomba：现代养蜂实践类似于工厂化养殖，Tim Rowe的《The Rose Hive Method》提出了一种利用进化改善蜜蜂活力的方法。然而，商业养蜂的当前实践可能无法持续，尤其是对于对蜂蛰过敏的人。
• miellaby：文章将蜜蜂健康问题归因于抗生素和NO2，但实际上主要原因应为新烟碱类农药，这些化学物质对昆虫有广泛的杀伤作用。
• imzadi：如果养蜂人通过使用抗生素保持蜜蜂健康，停止使用抗生素可能导致蜜蜂健康状况下降，因为之前的抗生素使用可能杀死了健康的细菌。
• alionski：工业界和政府应更多关注野生蜜蜂的保护，因为“拯救蜜蜂”实际上是指野生蜜蜂，而非作为“牲畜”的蜂蜜蜂。
• horacemorace：昆虫数量的减少对环境有巨大影响，过去夏季经常需要清理挡风玻璃上的昆虫尸体，而现在不再需要。
• endo_bunker：抗生素使用与蜂群死亡之间的关系可能是因为抗生素主要用于不健康的蜂群。
• ceedan：蜂群崩溃症可能由瓦螨传播的病毒和杀虫剂引起。
• giantg2：细菌问题对养蜂人来说不是主要问题，可以使用抗生素治疗欧洲幼虫病，但美洲幼虫病不可治疗，生物组研究正在进行中。
• thebees：非洲化蜜蜂（“杀人蜂”）在许多中美洲和南美洲地区是主要的蜂蜜生产者。
• animitronix：蜜蜂问题主要是杀虫剂问题，而非抗生素问题。
• 7734128：或许应该避免使用抗生素。
• Gnarl：提出射频辐射可能是一个因素。
• more_corn：问题主要在于杀虫剂。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及多个可能影响蜜蜂健康的因素，包括外来物种竞争、抗生素使用、农药（尤其是新烟碱类）、瓦螨传播的病毒、射频辐射等。
• 争议的焦点在于主要导致蜜蜂种群下降的原因，有人认为是农药，有人认为是抗生素或外来物种竞争，还有人提出其他环境因素。
• 讨论还涉及保护野生蜜蜂的必要性和现代养蜂实践的可持续性问题。

data.title: Playing with Open Source LLMs
data.author: zer0tonin
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者探索使用大型语言模型（LLM）在终端中进行代码编写的过程。作者首先提到当前流行的工具Claude Code，虽然功能全面，但作者担心被绑定到不盈利公司的工具上。因此，他转而寻找开源替代方案。经过尝试，作者选择了Qwen3:8b模型，该模型由阿里巴巴开发，支持现代AI工具，并且在本地运行良好。作者使用Ollama搭建本地API来运行LLM，并通过Aider实现与模型的配对编程。Aider允许用户通过命令行与模型交互，指导其修改代码、运行检查工具并提交更改。尽管模型并不完全自主，需要用户引导，但整体体验较为高效。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：开放大型语言模型（LLM）的使用、实用性、技术细节以及开源与免费软件的区分。

不同观点：
• roadside_picnic认为开放模型最有价值的地方在于其透明性，用户可以深入了解和修改模型的内部结构，而不仅仅是运行它们。他分享了几个有趣且有教育意义的技术项目，如实现推测解码和强制结构化输出。
• simonw则从实用角度出发，认为在实际操作中，使用LLM生成代码的效率低于手动编辑，尤其是在使用较小模型时，时间和精力成本较高。
• v3ss0n指出模型选择的重要性，认为应该使用更好的模型如qwen3 8b-14b，而不是使用Deepseek R1 8B，后者是Qwen2的蒸馏版本。
• channel_t认为这种实验具有教育价值，但最终可能还是会转向使用大公司拥有的闭源模型。
• runningmike对使用开源机器学习工具的更新表示赞赏，认为这节省了大量时间。
• BoorishBears澄清Deepseek R1 8B的归属问题，指出其并非真正的Deepseek产品，类似于自己微调Llama并不意味着成为Llama的创造者。
• 44za12以讽刺的语气表示对开放源LLM的失望，认为其表现不佳，自己的工作因此更加安全。
• lrvick强调区分 freeware 和开源软件的重要性，指出只有所有源代码在OSI许可下发布并可重现的软件才是真正的开源软件。

补充讨论：
• 模型选择和性能表现是讨论的一个焦点，尤其是较小模型在实际应用中的局限性。
• 开源模型的透明性和教育价值得到部分用户的认可，但也有人认为最终可能还是会依赖闭源的大模型。
• 开源与免费软件的区分在技术社区中是一个重要的讨论点，lrvick提供了明确的定义和标准。

44726838.article_content:
Every 6 months or so, I decide to leave my cave and check out what the cool kids are doing with AI.
Apparently the latest trend is to use fancy command line tools to write code using LLMs.
This is a very nice change, since it suddenly makes AI compatible with my allergy to getting out of the terminal.
Me, browsing HN from my cave (by Stable Diffusion)
The most popular of these tools seems to be Claude Code.
It promises to be able to build in total autonomy, being able to use search code, write code, run tests, lint, and commit the changes.
While this sounds great on paper, I’m not keen on getting locked into vendor tools from an unprofitable company.
At some point, they will either need to raise their prices, enshittify their product, or most likely do both.
So I went looking for what the free and open source alternatives are.
Picking a model
There’s a large amount of open source large language models on the market, with new ones getting released all the time.
However, they are not all ready to be used locally in coding tasks, so I had to try a bunch of them before settling on one.
deepseek-r1:8b
Deepseek is the most popular open source model right now.
It was created by the eponymous Chinese company.
It made the news by beating numerous benchmarks while being trained on a budget that is probably lower than the compensation of some OpenAI workers.
The 8b variant only weights 5.2 GB and runs decently on limited hardware, like my three years old Mac.
This model is famous for forgetting about world events from 1989, but also seems to have a few issues when faced with concrete coding tasks.
It is a reasoning model, meaning it “thinks” before acting, which should lead to improved accuracy.
In practice, it regularly gets stuck indefinitely searching where it should start and jumping from one problem to the other in a loop.
This can happen even on simple problems, and made it unusable for me.
mistral:7b
Mistral is the French alternative to American and Chinese models.
I have already talked about their 7b model
on this blog
.
It is worth noting that they have kept updating their models, and it should now be much more accurate than two years ago.
Mistral is not a reasoning model, so it will jump straight to answering.
This is very good if you’re working with tasks where speed and low compute use are a priority.
Sadly, the accuracy doesn’t seem good enough for coding.
Even on simple tasks, it will hallucinate functions or randomly delete parts of the code I didn’t want to touch.
qwen3:8b
Another model from China, qwen3 was created by the folks at Alibaba.
It also claims impressive benchmark results, and can work as both a reasoning or non-thinking model.
It was made with modern AI tooling in mind, by supporting MCPs and a
framework for agentic development
.
This model actually seems to work as expected, providing somewhat accurate code output while not hanging in the reasoning part.
Since it runs decently on my local setup, I decided to stick to that model for now.
Setting up a local API with Ollama
Ollama is now the default way to download and run local LLMs.
It can be simply installed by downloading it from
their website
.
Once installed, it works like Docker for models, by giving us access to commands like
pull
,
run
, or
rm
.
Ollama will expose an API on
localhost
which can be used by other programs.
For example, you can use it from your Python programs through
ollama-python
.
My new pet (by Stable Diffusion)
Pair programming with aider
The next piece of software I installed is
aider
.
I assume it’s pronounced like the French word, but I could not confirm that.
Aider describes itself as a “pair programming” application.
Its main job is to pass context to the model, let it write the output to files, run linters, and commit the changes.
Getting started
It can be installed using
the official Python package
or via
Homebrew
if you use Mac.
Once it is installed, just navigate to your code repository and launch it:
export
OLLAMA_API_BASE
=
http://127.0.0.1:11434
aider
--model
ollama_chat/qwen3:8b
The CLI should automatically create some configuration files and add them to the repo’s
.gitignore
.
Usage
Aider isn’t meant to be left alone in complete autonomy.
You’ll have to guide the AI through the process of making changes to your repository.
To start, use the
/add
command to add files you want to focus on.
Those files will be passed entirely to the model’s context and the model will be able to write in them.
You can then ask questions using the
/ask
command.
If you want to generate code, a good strategy can be to starting by requesting a plan of actions.
When you want it to actually write to the files, you can prompt it using the
/code
command.
This is also the default mode.
There’s no absolute guarantee that it will follow a plan if you agreed on one previously, but it is still a good idea to have one.
The
/architect
command seems to automatically ask for a plan, accept it, and write the code.
The specificity of this c

data.title: Show HN: A GitHub Action that quizzes you on a pull request
data.author: dkamm
data.article_summary: **PR Quiz** 是一个 GitHub Action，利用 AI 根据 pull request 生成测验，帮助开发者检验对代码的理解。它要求用户拥有 OpenAI API Key 和 ngrok 认证 token，并在 GitHub 仓库中设置为 secrets。当 pull request 通过审核后，系统会触发测验生成，并在临时 web 服务器上通过 ngrok 提供访问。测验有时间限制和尝试次数限制，还可以排除特定文件。该工具确保代码不会发送给第三方，仅与 OpenAI 模型交互，也可修改为支持自托管模型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何确保理解AI编写的代码，以及如何改进代码审查流程。

不同观点：
• sunrunner认为，确保理解AI编写的代码是一个好问题，但同时也指出，人类常常也无法完全理解其他人类编写的代码。有效的代码审查依赖于审查者对任务有预先的心理模型，否则审查更像是模糊的标准合规，虽然有用但不理想。
• robotsquidward以调侃的方式表达了对当前开发环境的感慨，没有提出具体的解决方案或立场。
• throwaway889900提出了一种实际的操作建议，即通过提交PR来测试其他开发者是否认真审查代码，暗示有些开发者在代码审查中可能并不尽责。
• frenchie4111以讽刺的语气预测未来可能会出现由AI回答PR问答的工具，暗示对过度依赖AI的担忧。
• rmnclmnt对数据隐私表示担忧，质疑将代码发送给模型提供商（如OpenAI）是否合适，担心重蹈用户数据被用于广告分析的覆辙。
• waynesonfire以轻松的语气回应，表示这种方法可以用来确保理解自己的代码风格，但没有深入讨论其实际效果。
• donatj支持使用AI辅助的PR问答方式，认为这对审查非AI生成的代码也有帮助，指出公司内常有开发者批准他们不理解的PR，导致问题发生。
• hk1337简单表示不会实际使用这种工具，认为其作用不大。
• henriquegodoy询问是否可以自动化回答PR问题的过程，显示出对提高代码审查效率的兴趣。
• ElijahLynn认为这种方法可能非常有用，表现出对AI辅助工具的积极态度。
• Xss3强调如果开发者经常无法通过这种PR问答测试，就应该考虑将其列入绩效改进计划或解雇，认为理解自己的PR是基本要求。

补充讨论：
• 评论中涉及了对AI生成代码的理解和审查问题，以及对开发者责任和隐私问题的关注。
• 对AI工具在代码审查中作用的看法存在分歧，有人支持其提高审查质量，有人则对其持怀疑态度或不感兴趣。
• 争议的焦点包括如何有效进行代码审查、AI工具的实际效果以及数据隐私问题。

44726672.article_summary: **PR Quiz** 是一个 GitHub Action，利用 AI 根据 pull request 生成测验，帮助开发者检验对代码的理解。它要求用户拥有 OpenAI API Key 和 ngrok 认证 token，并在 GitHub 仓库中设置为 secrets。当 pull request 通过审核后，系统会触发测验生成，并在临时 web 服务器上通过 ngrok 提供访问。测验有时间限制和尝试次数限制，还可以排除特定文件。该工具确保代码不会发送给第三方，仅与 OpenAI 模型交互，也可修改为支持自托管模型。

主要讨论点：如何确保理解AI编写的代码，以及如何改进代码审查流程。

不同观点：
• sunrunner认为，确保理解AI编写的代码是一个好问题，但同时也指出，人类常常也无法完全理解其他人类编写的代码。有效的代码审查依赖于审查者对任务有预先的心理模型，否则审查更像是模糊的标准合规，虽然有用但不理想。
• robotsquidward以调侃的方式表达了对当前开发环境的感慨，没有提出具体的解决方案或立场。

• waynesonfire以轻松的语气回应，表示这种方法可以用来确保理解自己的代码风格，但没有深入讨论其实际效果。
• donatj支持使用AI辅助的PR问答方式，认为这对审查非AI生成的代码也有帮助，指出公司内常有开发者批准他们不理解的PR，导致问题发生。

data.title: Supervised fine tuning on curated data is reinforcement learning
data.author: GabrielBianconi
data.article_summary: 本文探讨了监督微调（SFT）在精选数据上的应用，并将其与强化学习（RL）的理论和实践联系起来。作者指出，SFT可以被视为在稀疏奖励设置下最大化RL目标的下界，从而解释了其良好表现的原因。基于此观点，作者提出了一种重要性加权监督微调（iw-SFT）方法，该方法优化了更紧的下界，并可能提升性能。实验表明，iw-SFT在多个大型语言模型和连续控制任务中，表现可与更先进的RL算法相媲美，例如在AIME 2024数据集上达到了66.7%的成绩。文章提供了相关代码和详细信息。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过精细调整小型模型并利用自动化筛选的高质量数据来降低推理成本和提升性能的可行性，以及对强化学习（RL）在AI系统中的角色和定义的讨论。

不同观点：
• anndvision 认为，通过在小模型上微调从大型模型自动筛选的高质量输出数据，可以在降低推理成本（最多降低30倍）和推理时间（最多降低4倍）的同时，超越大型模型的性能。他们通过在多个基准测试中的实验结果支持这一观点，并计划在未来几天更新更多实验结果。

• iandanforth 对将所有优化问题都视为强化学习（RL）的做法提出质疑。他认为，RL是一种涉及序列决策过程的优化方法，应该仅在存在代理（agent）在环境中进行多次决策时使用。如果缺乏这种互动，则不应称之为RL。

• mandevil 对两个独立研究人员同时研究这一现象表示好奇，并询问其背景，是否为某种副项目。

• henriquegodoy 支持将AI视为大型系统中的模块组件，而非完全代理的观点。他认为通过构建监控过程，可以在初始使用超大模型后将其简化为较小的模型，从而降低成本。

补充讨论：
• anndvision 提到了具体的实验结果和基准测试，包括在多轮迷宫导航、agentic RAG和agentic工具使用等任务中的表现，并提供了相关博客链接以供进一步阅读。
• iandanforth 强调了RL的定义和适用范围，指出只有在涉及时间序列决策的情况下才应使用RL，而不是将所有优化问题都归为RL。
• henriquegodoy 提出了一种从超大模型到较小模型的蒸馏过程，以实现成本降低和性能优化，并列举了在法律合规等领域的应用实例。

争议焦点：
• 对于RL的定义和适用范围存在争议。iandanforth 认为不应将所有优化问题都视为RL，而 anndvision 的实验似乎将某些优化问题纳入了RL的范畴。

44727788.article_content:
Computer Science > Machine Learning
arXiv:2507.12856
(cs)
[Submitted on 17 Jul 2025]
Title:
Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved)
Authors:
Chongli Qin
,
Jost Tobias Springenberg
View a PDF of the paper titled Supervised Fine Tuning on Curated Data is Reinforcement Learning (and can be improved), by Chongli Qin and 1 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
Behavior Cloning (BC) on curated (or filtered) data is the predominant paradigm for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) of large language models; as well as for imitation learning of control policies. Here, we draw on a connection between this successful strategy and the theory and practice of finding optimal policies via Reinforcement Learning (RL). Building on existing literature, we clarify that SFT can be understood as maximizing a lower bound on the RL objective in a sparse reward setting. Giving support to its often observed good performance. From this viewpoint, we realize that a small modification to SFT leads to an importance weighted variant that behaves closer to training with RL as it: i) optimizes a tighter bound to the RL objective and, ii) can improve performance compared to SFT on curated data. We refer to this variant as importance weighted supervised fine-tuning (iw-SFT). We show that it is easy to implement and can be further generalized to training with quality scored data. The resulting SFT variants are competitive with more advanced RL algorithms for large language models and for training policies in continuous control tasks. For example achieving 66.7% on the AIME 2024 dataset.

data.title: Stanford’s Department of Management Science and Engineering
data.author: curioustock
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了一些申请顶尖商学院（如斯坦福GSB、哈佛、MIT Sloan等）的候选人及其考试成绩和GPA。每个候选人都有独特的昵称，反映了他们的背景或特点，例如"Mr. Doesn’t Know When To Quit"、"Ms. Sassy"等。他们的GRE/GMAT成绩和GPA各不相同，显示了不同背景和学术表现的申请者。例如，有人GMAT高达760，GPA 9，也有人GPA较低但GMAT成绩不错。这些昵称和成绩展示了商学院申请者的多样性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：斯坦福大学的管理科学与工程（MS&E）硕士学位的价值和意义

不同观点：
• apparent认为，斯坦福的许多知名创始人是通过本科期间的"coterm"项目获得硕士学位的，这样可以节省时间和金钱。如果不需要搬家或者以较低的价格获得学位，这个项目是有价值的；但如果需要支付双倍费用并搬到斯坦福就读，价值就不那么明显了。
• MADEinPARIS提到一个辍学并成功融资2.5亿美元的例子，暗示该项目可能培养出一些被宠坏的学生。
• mathattack认为，MS&E项目对已经拥有电子工程或计算机科学学士学位的学生有一定价值，但对于历史专业的学生则不太可能赋予他们足够的管理能力。同时，怀疑该项目的7%录取率与coterm学生无关。
• coupdejarnac对斯坦福的MS&E研究生课程给予积极评价，认为通过非学位项目学习这些课程收获很大。
• TexanFeller对“管理科学”这一名称表示反感，认为管理不能被视为科学，引用费曼的视频来支持自己的观点。
• constantcrying认为，这种学位项目显得自恋，尤其在其文化背景中，这样的人作为同事或老板是难以接受的。
• lisper批评了文章标题的点击诱饵性质，认为这种标题自相矛盾，因为既然文章提到了这个概念，就说明有人知道它。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及项目的成本效益和时间节省问题，反映出对教育投资的不同看法。
• 对MS&E学位的实用性和其赋予学生能力的质疑，特别是对非技术背景学生的适用性。
• 对学位名称的哲学性批评，表明对管理是否能被科学化的不同理解。
• 文化差异在看待这种学位项目上的影响，以及对学位持有者的社会和职场接受度。
• 对文章标题风格的批评，反映出对媒体标题策略的不满。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：用户对Amodeling网站及其功能、设计和收费模式的评价与反馈

不同观点：
• [hnlmorg] 认为网站的示例需要更新，因为示例中的机器人设计与PlayStation的Astro Bot mascot过于相似，可能引发版权问题。此外，他支持网站的创意，但不喜欢按月订阅的收费模式，更倾向于按生成模型数量收费。他对按需付费（PAYG）选项表示兴趣，但质疑如果生成的模型质量不佳，用户是否会有选择机会或得到退款。

• [Jimmy6929] 分享了自己与朋友在3D建模和3D打印方面的经验，特别是为Warhammer制作自定义景观和建筑。他对Amodeling表示认可，但也提到在开发过程中遇到了一些下载功能的问题。

• [overgard] 提出了一个元问题，质疑为什么AI应用程序的按钮设计常常使用粉蓝渐变色，表示这种设计风格过于普遍和缺乏新意。

• [marcodiego] 遇到了技术问题，在访问Amodeling网站时出现客户端异常错误，暗示网站的稳定性或兼容性存在问题。

data.title: The Making of Dario Amodei
data.author: spenvo
data.article_summary:
Dario Amodei，Anthropic公司CEO，是人工智能领域直言不讳的领袖。2025年，他与业内同行、政府及公众对AI的看法产生激烈冲突。他预测AI可能很快将淘汰50%的初级白领工作，反对纽约时报提出的十年AI监管禁令，并支持对华半导体出口管制，引发Nvidia CEO黄仁勋的公开批评。

Amodei坚信AI发展速度超出多数人认知，其机遇与后果近在咫尺。他创立Anthropic，公司估值达610亿美元，年收入从2025年3月的14亿美元迅速增长至7月的45亿美元。与OpenAI不同，Anthropic主要通过API和向其他公司出售AI模型获利。

Amodei成长于一个富有责任感的家庭，母亲从事图书馆建设项目，父亲是皮革匠人。在Princeton攻读研究生期间，因父亲去世，他从理论物理转向生物学研究。

Amodei的紧迫感源于个人悲剧及对AI快速发展的认知，他的行动和言论正塑造AI行业的未来。

The Making Of Dario Amodei
AI’s most outspoken leader found direction in a personal tragedy.
Alex Kantrowitz
Jul 29, 2025
14
Share this post

Copy link

Share
Dario Amodei doesn’t hesitate
when I ask what’s gotten into him. The Anthropic CEO has spent 2025 at war, feuding with industry counterparts, members of the government, and the public’s perception of artificial intelligence.
In recent months, he’s
predicted
that AI could soon eliminate 50% of entry-level, white-collar jobs. He’s
railed
against a ten-year AI regulation moratorium in the pages of the New York Times. And he’s
called
for semiconductor export controls to China, drawing a public rebuke from Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.
Amid it all, Amodei meets me on the first floor of his company’s downtown San Francisco headquarters. He’s loose, energetic, and anxious to get started, as if he’s been waiting for this moment to address his actions. Sporting a blue shawl-collar sweater over a casual white t-shirt, and boxy thick-rimmed glasses, he sits down and stares ahead.
Underlying his efforts, Amodei says, is a firm belief that AI is moving faster than most of us appreciate, making its opportunities and consequences much closer than they appear. “I am indeed one of the most bullish about AI capabilities improving very fast,” he tells me. “As we've gotten more close to AI systems that are more powerful, I've wanted to say those things more forcefully, more publicly, to make the point clearer.”
Amodei’s outspokenness and sharp elbows have earned him both respect and derision in Silicon Valley. He’s seen by some as a technological visionary who pioneered OpenAI’s GPT-3 project (the seeds of ChatGPT) and a safety-minded leader who broke off and founded Anthropic. Others see him as a control-oriented “doomer” who wants to slow AI progress, shape it to his liking, and shut out the competition.
Love him or hate him, the AI field will have to deal with him. Amodei has turned Anthropic, currently valued at $61 billion, into an economic force. From a zero start in 2021, the company — though still unprofitable — has grown its annualized recurring revenue from $1.4 billion
in March 2025
to $3 billion
in May
to nearly $4.5 billion in July, leading Amodei to call it the “fastest growing software company in history at the scale that it's at.”
Perhaps more notable than Anthropic’s revenue is the way it’s coming in. Rather than relying primarily on applications like OpenAI’s ChatGPT, Amodei’s biggest bet is on the underlying technology itself. Most of the company’s revenue, Amodei tells me, is earned via its API, or through other companies buying Anthropic’s AI models and using them within their own products. Anthropic will thus be a barometer of AI’s progress, rising and falling on the strength of the technology.
As Anthropic grows, Amodei hopes its heft will help him influence the industry’s direction. And given his willingness to speak out, throw a punch, and take one, he’s probably right.
So if this man will steer what may be the world’s most influential new technology, it’s worth understanding what drives him, his business, and why his timeline is shorter than so many others’. And after more than two dozen interviews with him, his friends, colleagues, and competitors, I believe I have an answer.
A Curable Illness
Dario Amodei was a science kid. Born in San Francisco in 1983 to a Jewish mother and an Italian father, he was interested almost entirely in math and physics. When the dot-com boom exploded around him in his high school years, it barely registered. “Writing some website actually had no interest to me whatsoever,” he tells me. “I was interested in discovering fundamental scientific truth.”
At home, Amodei was very close with his parents, a loving couple who he says sought to improve the world. His mother Elena Engel ran renovation and construction projects for libraries in Berkeley and San Francisco. His father Riccardo Amodei was a trained leathersmith. “They gave me a sense of right and wrong and what was important in the world,” he says, “imbuing a strong sense of responsibility.”
That sense of responsibility showed up in Amodei’s undergrad years at Caltech, where he lambasted his fellow students over their passivity toward the forthcoming Iraq war. “The problem isn't that everyone is just peachy with the idea of bombing Iraq; it's that most people are opposed in principle but refuse to give one millisecond of their time,” Amodei
wrote
in The California Tech, a student newspaper, on March 3, 2003. “This needs to change, right now and without delay.”
Then, in his early 20s, Amodei’s life changed forever. His father Riccardo, who’d long fought a rare illness, lost the battle in 2006. Riccardo’s passing shocked Amodei, and he shifted his graduate studies at Princeton from theoretical physics to biology

data.title: A grand tour through the essays of Lewis H. Lapham
data.author: samclemens
data.article_summary: 这篇文章是作者对已故导师刘易斯的怀念与致敬，强调刘易斯对“声音”的重视，认为写作与阅读是作者与读者之间的共同探索，从中获得思想自由，为社会注入能量与希望。作者通过拼贴刘易斯作品中的句子，回顾其思想和影响，重温其对资本虚伪的批评，以及对人类可能性的探索。文章表达了对刘易斯智慧与幽默的感激，认为他的声音穿越时代，启发人们思考与自我探索。作者借此重新找到能量与希望，并强调独立思考的重要性，拒绝简单的零和解决方案，最终以开放性问题作结，邀请读者共同思考。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Lewis Lapham及其作品的评价和怀念

不同观点：
• [正面评价] ahi认为Lewis Lapham及其作品对个人成长有重要影响。他提到Lapham的作品在他青春期时为他提供了重要的文化启示，尤其是通过《Harper's》杂志。ahi强调Lapham的写作风格聪明、批判性强且常常幽默，展示了好写作的魅力。
• [对作品形式的不同偏好] unethical_ban虽然承认Lapham是一位出色的散文家，但表示对复合式散文风格不感兴趣。不过，他赞赏Lapham的季刊（Lapham’s Quarterly），并认为将大量作品集中在一个链接中是非常有价值的。

补充讨论：
• [Lapham的历史地位] ahi引用讣告中的描述，称Lapham为“最后一个贵族自由主义者”，暗示他在文化与政治领域的独特地位和影响。
• [作品的形式与收藏价值] unethical_ban提到Lapham's Quarterly的实体杂志带来的愉悦体验，强调了收藏和翻阅纸质杂志的独特价值。

• 对Lapham作品风格的个人偏好不同。ahi非常欣赏Lapham的写作风格，而unethical_ban则对特定的散文风格不感兴趣，但两者都认同Lapham的文学贡献和影响力。

44691242.article_content:
In his introductory essay for the inaugural issue of
Lapham’s Quarterly
, Lewis wrote (as he often had before) about his “risk-assessment model wired to the sound of the human voice.” If he read a piece without being able to hear its author speak—from whatever time, place, genre, species, leaning, or dimension—it wasn’t much of anything to him at all. To be mentored by him was to be tuned to this frequency. Which I’m grateful for, because while missing him since his passing a year ago I’ve been able to hear him any time by picking up his prose. It always answers the line. Lewis admired “voices that have survived the wreck of empires and the accidents of fortune,” and I know of no better way to honor him than to affirm that his is undoubtedly among them.
The patchwork essay below takes its brief from that initial preamble. “It is the joint venture entered into by writer and reader,” Lewis reminds us, “that produces the freedoms of mind from which a society gathers its common stores of energy and hope.” Back in 2018, on this quarterly’s tenth anniversary, I put together a collage essay, “
Midwinter Hotel
,” made up of sentences extracted from Voices in Time readings. Now I’m reporting back for duty, Captain. I’ve gone on a grand tour through Lewis’ work, hunting snark from his early days at the
Saturday Evening Post
, through his many years presiding over the Easy Chair and Notebook columns at
Harper’s
, and in those translucent preambles for his beloved
LQ
.
I was moved by his own remembrances of friends, mentors, and growing up around the San Francisco Bay (as I did a half-century after him). I smiled at his constant state of pique about capital’s fatuous venality. I wished I could discuss our disagreements just one more time while Lewis drank vodka from a wine glass and complained about having to leave the table to smoke. In short, I read, I stole, I arranged, I found energy again in the Laphamian vernacular, I glimpsed some honest hope for these
anni horribiles
. The result is something I could never have known how to say without him. No piece of his writing is cited more than once; none of his language has been changed.
“H
ere. Begin here. With the story.”
1
The remark was characteristic.
2
He thought that if only enough people had the courage to say what they meant, then all would be well.
3
I think of him as a man forever asking questions and offering advice, opening doors and windows, peering with a lantern into mine shafts.
4
“You were okay, kid,” he said.
5
So it has come to pass.
6
“Who could know what there is to be known?” he asked.
7
The sense of human possibility expands and contracts like the beating of the human heart.
8
He put the matter as plainly as it could be put.
9
How is it possible to formulate believable generalizations in a universe of specializations that recede from one another literally at the speed of light?
10
And for what?
11
Fortunately I don’t know the answers to these questions; if I knew them, I would be bound to proclaim myself a god and return to San Francisco in search of followers, a mandala, and a storefront shrine.
12
Isn’t that kind of the fun, the looking into the vast darkness ripe with wonders that will never cease?
13
Atoms wandering in the abyss, then in the womb for the nine months during which a human embryo ascends through a sequence touching on over 3 billion years of evolutionary change, up from the shore of a prehistoric sea, traveling as amphibian, fish, bird, reptile, lettuce leaf, and mammal to a room with a view of the Queensboro Bridge.
14
It is all the same story, all proof of the same mind, which, if I am to believe the evidence of the evolutionary record, is also my own.
15
The “I am” and the “It is” are both productions of the same independent film studio.
16
Don’t listen to consultants who tell you otherwise.
17
Would that it were so.
18
Easier said than done, the thinking for oneself.
19
The problem doesn’t yield to zero-sum solution.
20
Matter into mind, mind into matter, acorn into oak tree, oak tree into log, log into fire, fire into smoke and ashes.
21
Homer told a story and so did Einstein; so do General Motors and Donald Duck.
22
Nothing necessarily follows from anything else.
23
The future comes and goes so quickly that one gets used to surprise entrances and sudden exits.
24
Buy the bicycle or the truck, wrap up the handbag and the dress, take possession of the deck chair or the parrot, and you begin the world all over again.
25
All of which means what?
26
I offer the premise not as a rigorous statement of fact, but rather as a cautionary tale.
27
Regarding myself as neither art historian nor literary critic, I escape the chore of having to discern zeitgeists and deconstruct paradigms.
28
Which probably is why on passing a newsstand these days I think of funeral parlors and Tutankhamen’s tomb.
29
Every morning I read in the papers that I live in what the editorial writers like to call “an era of rapid and unprecedented change.”

data.title: Maru OS – Use your phone as your PC
data.author: fsflover
data.article_summary: Maru是一个将手机与桌面计算结合的操作系统，可以让手机通过连接HDMI屏幕和键鼠，变身为一个轻量级的桌面电脑。它基于Android Oreo构建，无预装软件，运行流畅。当手机连接显示器时，Maru会自动启动桌面模式，并在5秒内启动。桌面模式支持多任务处理和生产力应用，底层为Debian Linux，可自由定制。手机和桌面环境共享存储和网络连接，实现无缝切换。Maru让个人计算更简单，所有工作在一台设备上即可完成。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：移动设备与桌面设备融合的潜力和挑战

不同观点：
• bsimpson：认为将桌面Linux适配到移动设备上非常困难，Ubuntu等项目已经放弃，目前没有成功的例子。iOS在某些方面接近替代桌面，但生态系统依然分离。
• stego-tech：提到比尔·盖茨曾提出的情境感知操作系统概念，以及微软未实现的这些想法如何被苹果和谷歌部分采纳。对通过NFC进行身份验证的潜力表示兴趣。
• thesuperbigfrog：质疑Maru OS是否适用于当前设备，指出其最近更新在2019年。
• dbeley：认为Maru OS是废弃项目，但提到PostMarketOS和PinePhone等替代方案。
• harel：表达了对移动设备转换为全功能电脑的强烈需求，以减轻旅行时携带多设备的负担。
• gt0：认为移动桌面融合解决的是极少数人的问题，大多数需要便携电脑的人已经选择了笔记本电脑。
• mcv：认为这类融合概念每隔几年就会出现，但从未真正实现，如诺基亚的Maemo/Meego。
• blattus：认为消费者对“一个设备走天下”的概念感到兴奋，但现实中缺乏随时可用的显示器和键鼠等外设。
• doebler：指出即使有HDMI显示器和键盘，也很少有地方提供这些设备，因此携带笔记本更实际。
• urbandw311er：建议关注GrapheneOS，期待其桌面模式的未来发展。
• fmajid：提到Google宣布Linux终端支持图形应用，但指出Android终端目前仍存在许多问题。
• zorrn：认为苹果有能力实现移动和桌面系统的融合，但商业上可能不愿意，因为这会减少其销售多设备的机会。
• cadamsdotcom：展望通过手机运行Linux和UTM等实现无笔记本旅行，提到使用蓝牙键鼠和VR眼镜的可能性。
• WorldPeas：希望有一种经济实用的夹式手机键盘，结合RDP远程访问功能，以实现接近桌面体验的移动办公。
• FlyingSnake：指出Maru OS是废弃项目，推荐关注ubports项目作为更活跃的替代方案。

补充讨论：
• 移动桌面融合的技术挑战和资源限制是讨论的核心，尤其是Linux桌面在移动设备上的适配问题。
• 商业动机也是阻碍移动桌面融合实现的一个因素，如苹果可能因为销售策略而不愿推进此类项目。
• 不同用户对移动桌面融合的需求和期望各异，有些人认为这是小众需求，而另一些人则认为这对减轻旅行负担非常有用。
• 对现有项目的更新和替代方案的讨论，如Maru OS和ubports，显示出社区对持续发展的关注。

争议焦点：
• 是否真的存在足够大的用户需求来推动移动桌面融合的发展。
• 技术实现上的困难以及商业利益对这类融合概念的阻碍。

44727298.article_content:
Use your
phone
as your
PC
.
Unleash your mobile device with Maru, a context-aware, lightweight, open operating system that unites mobile and desktop computing.
Download Maru
"Simply plug your phone into an HDMI screen, connect up a keyboard and mouse, and you’ve got a lightweight desktop experience you can take anywhere."
"Want a complete desktop experience on your smartphone? Then take a look at the Maru operating system"
"Today's Android devices have plenty of RAM and viable processors: How great would it be to present the software directly on smartphones on an actual Debian system? Maru OS makes this a possibility."
Meet
Maru
.
Maru is a new kind of computing experience. It gives you a single, context-aware device that makes personal computing really simple. And guess what? That device is your smartphone.
When you're
on the go
, Maru is your
phone
.
Maru is built on the latest Android Oreo. It ships with
zero bloatware
, so your phone runs snappy and has lots of free space for all your apps.
When you're
at your desk
, Maru is your
desktop
.
Maru Desktop brings you
true multitasking
and
desktop productivity
. Peek under the hood and you'll find rock-stable Debian Linux, so you can customize it to your heart's content.
It's as
easy
as 1, 2, 3.
desktop_windows
Connect your phone to any HDMI screen.
Maru automatically detects when an external display is available and spins up your desktop. It boots in less than 5 seconds.
bluetooth
Pair up a bluetooth keyboard and mouse.
Any Android-compatible bluetooth peripherals will work with Maru.
favorite_border
Enjoy desktop productivity.
Gotta run? Disconnect from your screen and Maru will preserve your desktop state in the background so you can pick up right where you left off.
One device. A whole lot of
productivity
.
Maru takes advantage of your external display to bring you multi-app, desktop-class productivity. Create a spreadsheet, perfect your slide deck, or spiffy up your resume. You'll never believe you could get so much done with your "phone".
The only PC you need is the
one in your pocket
.
Maru takes personal computing one step closer to closed-loop. Your hardware's capabilities are shared across your mobile device and desktop so you don't have to context-switch around so much. Say goodbye to coordinating your work amongst dozens of different devices.
sd_storage
Shared storage
SD card data like camera photos and downloads are shared so you can coordinate your work seamlessly.
network_wifi
network_cell
Connectivity anywhere
Your network, whether WiFi or cellular, is shared between mobile and desktop. Never deal with spotty tethering hotspots again.
If you can
dream
it, you can
do
it.
Maru opens up a whole new world of possibilities. Nothing's stopping you from installing the tools you need to make Maru your own. Set up a portable development environment, fill out that annoying form that doesn't render properly on your mobile browser, or even run a webserver—it's really up to you.
Join the Maru community.
Be the first to hear of updates on Maru.

data.title: Show HN: Monchromate – the best greyscale browser extension
data.author: lirena00
data.article_summary: Monochromate是一款免费的浏览器扩展程序，通过将网页变为灰度模式，减少视觉刺激和沉迷浏览，帮助用户提升专注力和减少屏幕时间。它具有智能调度功能，可在特定时间自动启用灰度模式，支持自定义灰度强度和网站例外管理，确保工作关键网站保持彩色。该扩展轻量、快速，支持Chrome和Firefox，并提供隐私保护，不开跟踪或数据收集。用户可以通过简单的点击安装和调整设置，享受无干扰的浏览体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Mac电脑中内置的辅助功能"色彩滤镜"（Color Filters）的使用及其快捷操作

不同观点：
• 支持使用内置辅助功能：用户[tregoning]分享了自己使用Mac内置的"色彩滤镜"功能，并提供了如何通过菜单栏快捷键开启或关闭该功能的指南。该用户显然支持利用系统自带的辅助功能来改善用户体验，并提供了官方的支持链接和社区讨论链接以帮助其他用户。

• 使用官方资源和社区支持：[tregoning]提供了两个有用的链接，一个是苹果官方的使用指南，另一个是苹果用户社区中的相关讨论。这表明该用户认为官方资源和社区讨论对于解决问题非常有帮助，并愿意将这些资源分享给其他有需要的用户。

补充讨论：
• 快捷操作的便利性：用户强调了通过菜单栏快捷键快速切换色彩滤镜的功能，表明这一设计对于有相关需求的用户非常实用，有助于提高工作效率和用户体验。

• 社区互助的重要性：用户不仅分享了自己的使用经验，还提供了社区讨论链接，显示出对用户互助的重视，认为通过社区可以找到更多实用信息和解决方案。

没有明显的争议或对立观点，评论主要集中在对Mac内置辅助功能的使用分享和资源推荐上。

Focus on what
matters.
Turn down the colors, turn up your focus. Transform your browsing experience with a
powerful greyscale browser extension that helps reduce digital distractions, prevent
doomscrolling, and boost productivity. Perfect for students, professionals, and anyone
seeking mindful web browsing.

Why Choose Monochromate?
Powerful tools designed to enhance your digital well-being, reduce doomscrolling, and
boost productivity through smart greyscale filtering.
Smart Scheduler
Automatically enable greyscale mode during specific hours. Perfect for reducing evening
screen time, maintaining focus during work hours, or preventing late-night
doomscrolling.
Customizable Intensity
Fine-tune the greyscale intensity from 0-100% to find your perfect balance. Research
shows greyscale mode reduces screen time by making websites less visually stimulating
and addictive.
Site Exceptions
Smart blacklist management keeps work-critical sites in full color while applying
greyscale everywhere else. Perfect for photo galleries, design work, or any sites
requiring color accuracy.
Export & Sync Settings
Effortlessly sync your configurations across browsers with backup and restore features.
Keep your personalized settings consistent whether you're using Chrome or Firefox.
Fullscreen Mode Support
Unlike other greyscale extensions, Monochromate works seamlessly in fullscreen mode.
Enjoy distraction-free video watching, presentations, and gaming with consistent
greyscale filtering.
Privacy-First & Open Source
No data collection, no tracking, no analytics. Open source on GitHub with complete
transparency. All settings stored locally on your device for maximum privacy and
security.
Built with WXT Framework
Modern development framework ensures consistent performance across Chrome and Firefox.
Lightweight, fast, and optimized for minimal resource usage.
Cross-Browser Support
Available for both Chrome and Firefox with identical features. Built with

for consistent performance across browsers.
Clean & Intuitive Design
Polished UI/UX crafted with users in mind. Modern, clean interface that's intuitive to
navigate. Every interaction is thoughtfully designed for the best user experience.
Transform Your Browsing Today

screen time and stopped doomscrolling with Monochromate. Free forever.

Frequently Asked Questions
Everything you need to know about Monochromate greyscale browser extension.
What is Monochromate and how does it work?
Monochromate is a free browser extension that applies a greyscale filter to
websites, removing colors to reduce visual distractions and doomscrolling. It works
by modifying the CSS of web pages in real-time, making them appear in black and
white while preserving functionality.
Does Monochromate really reduce screen time?
Yes! Research shows that colorful interfaces trigger dopamine responses that make
websites more addictive. By removing colors, Monochromate makes websites less
visually stimulating, naturally reducing the time you spend browsing and scrolling.
Is Monochromate free and safe to use?
Absolutely! Monochromate is completely free and open-source. We don't collect any
personal data, track your browsing, or display ads. All settings are stored locally
on your device for maximum privacy and security.
Can I exclude specific websites from greyscale mode?
Yes! Monochromate includes smart site exclusion features. You can easily add
websites to your blacklist where colors should remain enabled - perfect for photo
galleries, design work, or work-critical applications that require color accuracy.
Which browsers support Monochromate?
Monochromate is available for both Chrome and Firefox with identical features. It's
built using the WXT framework, ensuring consistent performance and functionality
across both browsers. You can download it from the Chrome Web Store or Firefox
Add-ons.
How do I install and use Monochromate?
Installation is simple: visit the Chrome Web Store or Firefox Add-ons, click "Add to
Browser," and you're ready! Once installed, click the Monochromate icon in your
toolbar to toggle greyscale mode on/off. You can adjust intensity and manage site
exclusions from the popup interface.
I found a bug in Monochromate. How can I report it?
We appreciate bug reports! If you're comfortable with GitHub, please create an issue
on our
GitH

data.title: Stochastic Transparency [pdf]
data.author: E-Reverance
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某篇文章或话题的理解与关联讨论

不同观点：
• [kruffalon] 认为自己对相关内容了解不足，无法有效参与讨论。他原本希望通过阅读来探讨如何应对"stochastic terrorism"（随机恐怖主义），并认为透明度可能是一个好的起点。然而，他最终写下的内容与原文无关。

• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 指出该内容来自2010年，并将其与游戏《Baldur's Gate 3》中的头发表现技术联系起来。他认为当角色静止时头发效果很棒，但在移动时会有噪点问题，并考虑在GLES2 / GLES3中实现类似效果。

补充讨论：
• [kruffalon] 的评论反映了试图参与复杂话题但缺乏背景知识的困扰，同时表达了对"透明度对抗随机恐怖主义"的潜在兴趣。

• [01HNNWZ0MV43FF] 的评论偏向技术性，关注游戏图形技术的实现及其在不同版本的OpenGL ES中应用的可能性。

• 争议焦点：两者之间没有直接争议，但可以看出讨论的方向截然不同，一个是社会政治话题，另一个是技术实现问题。

data.title: Playing with more user-friendly methods for multi-factor authentication
data.author: noleary
data.article_summary:
Ned O'Leary提出了几种改进多因素身份验证（MFA）用户体验的方法：

1. **大盲法**：用户从52张扑克牌中选择5张，作为二次认证因素，易于记忆且难以猜测。
2. **魔方法**：用户打乱一个数字魔方，再次登录时重复相同操作，魔方有约4.3 x 10^19种可能配置。
3. **香农数法**：使用象棋对局作为认证因素，有约10^120种可能对局，提升安全性和趣味性。
4. **打字模式**：利用用户独特的打字速度作为认证因素。
5. **无硬件指纹**：展示指纹图片让用户确认，无需专用硬件。
6. **离线TOTP**：将TOTP密码打印在纸上通过邮寄传递，避免SMS漏洞。
7. **隐私优先**：利用自拍肖像进行身份验证，结合外观和技巧两个验证维度。
8. **歌唱认证**：用户通过唱歌进行认证，必须完整唱完一首歌以防欺诈。
9. **亲友协助**：系统随机选择亲属发送验证码，如叔叔帮助访问旧邮箱。

这些方法旨在提高MFA的用户友好性和安全性。

44716280.article_content:
I designed some more user-friendly methods for multi-factor authentication.
Ned O'Leary
Cofounder and CEO, Tesseral
When I tell people I work on authentication software, I nearly always hear some version of the same story:
I hate multifactor authentication
. No, really. People hate this stuff.
So I spend a lot of time thinking about how we can make MFA a better user experience. We don't always need MFA to be airtight, after all. Sometimes, the Google
match-a-number
MFA flow is good enough.
I thought I'd share here my best ideas for the future of multi-factor authentication. Here they are.
The big blind
We like
entropy
in auth factors, so it's intuitive to start with a familiar example of randomness: playing cards. For example,
Wikipedia says
there are about 2.5 million unique poker hands.
That makes poker hands a compelling secondary authentication factor. Here's what a simple version of the UI could look like: challenge the user to pick exactly five cards from a set of 52.
It's incredibly easy to remember your hand. Just ask any of your friends that play poker -- they can surely remember a bad beat. And it's pretty much impossible for an attacker to guess.
Cubes
This one's a bit tougher than poker, but it's much less risky. (I'm not sure how comfortable I am with just 2.5M possibilities). Instead of having the user pick 5 cards from a deck of 52, we have the user scramble a digital Rubik's cube.
Then, when the user logs back in, they just have to scramble the cube in exactly the same way. Easy. Here's what it'd look like:
We can rest easy knowing that there are roughly
4.3 x 10^19 possible configurations
of the cube.
The Shannon number
If we're looking for even
more
entropy in our auth factors, we could use chess games as an option. It's
been estimated
that there are 10^120 possible chess matches. That's a nice big number.
Imagine this: when you set up your account, you play out a chess match. When you log back in, you play out the exact same chess match. It's like a second password! There's no chance anyone would ever guess your chess match correctly.
It's clean and intuitive. Hard to beat. Plus it'll boost your chess skill.
Mavis Beacon teaches auth
Everyone types a little differently. We can exploit our unique typing tendencies as an auth factor. There's a simple version of this that relies solely on approximate words-per-minute (WPM), as shown below.
If you want access to your account, all you have to do is reliably reproduce the same typing speed!
Fingerprints without the hardware
Biometric factors like fingerprints are perfect -- except for the fact that they generally require fancy hardware. How does a normal web app take a fingerprint as an input?
Well, I just don't think it's necessary. You can simply
present the user with a fingerprint
and ask whether it's a match!
All the benefit, none of the fuss.
Airgapped TOTPs
Everyone still seems to use SMS-based MFA, but we all know by now that SMS opens vulnerability to
SIM-swapping attacks
.
How do we retain the user-friendly experience of SMS MFA while protecting ourselves from its vulnerabilities? I think I have a solution. We never put our passcodes over the air. Instead, we print them onto sheets of 8.5" x 11" paper and route them through a trusted Postal Service.
Maximum security.
Privacy first
Many of us would like to use photographs as an auth factor. We often require photographs as
part of onboarding
for certain sensitive applications (e.g., banking, ridesharing).
But users really don't like submitting photographs. It can feel a bit invasive. Plus, privacy considerations aside, it's just inconvenient and puts an annoying speedbump between the user and successful use of the software.
Good news: we don't need to grab a
photo
of the user. With today's multi-modal AI, we can simply infer identities from self-portrait.
With self-portraits, we get two distinct vectors of comparison: first, we can evaluate the portrait for its similarity to the user's real appearance; second, we can evaluate the portrait for the user's skill level.
That stuff is hard to fake!
Of me I sing
Biometric auth based on users' voices used to be reliable, but now it's too
easy to spoof
with AI tools. But AI still has a tough time singing as poorly as normal people do -- that's why Karaoke Auth is the future.
The user just has to pick a song and belt it out. For anyone thinking of implementing karaoke-based auth, I will caution you: it is
critical
to require the user to finish the entire song. Song fragments do not generate sufficient samples to protect against fraud.
Phone a friend
We can borrow an innovation from the Web3 crowd. Instead of sending a code to
your
email (predictable, boring, lame), the system sends a code to a randomly-selected relative. Like an uncle!
The user just has to help their uncle access a 22-year-old Hotmail account before the passcode expires (upon expiry, the system will select a different relative at random).

data.title: How the brain increases blood flow on demand
data.author: gmays
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要介绍了哈佛医学院的一项新研究，该研究揭示了大脑如何快速有效地将血液输送到需要更多氧气和营养的活跃区域。研究发现，大脑依赖于血管内皮细胞间紧密交织的通道进行通讯，这些通道通过所谓的缝隙连接迅速传递信号，从而调节血流量。该研究发表在《Cell》杂志上，有助于更好地理解神经退行性疾病以及脑成像（如功能性磁共振成像，fMRI）的解读。如果这些发现能在动物和人类中得到进一步验证，可能会为治疗认知问题提供新思路。这项研究还强调了联邦资助对科学研究的重要性。

44727191.article_content:
How the Brain Increases Blood Flow on Demand
New findings could improve understanding of neurodegeneration, interpretation of brain scans
By CATHERINE CARUSO
July 16, 2025
Research
3 min read
Blood vessels in the brain. Image: mr.suphachai praserdumrongchai/iStock/Getty Images Plus
At a glance:
A new study in mice describes how the brain rapidly and efficiently increases blood flow to active areas where oxygen and nutrients are needed most.
The work shows that the brain relies on a communication highway of tightly interlaced cells lining its blood vessels.
The insights could advance understanding of neurodegenerative diseases and improve interpretation of brain imaging.
Work described in this story was made possible in part by federal funding supported by taxpayers. At Harvard Medical School, the future of efforts like this — done in service to humanity — now hangs in the balance due to the government’s decision to terminate large numbers of federally funded grants and contracts across Harvard University.
All day long, our brains carry out complicated and energy-intensive tasks such as remembering, solving problems, and making decisions.
To supply the energy these tasks require while conserving this precious fuel, the brain has evolved a system that allows it to quickly and efficiently send blood only to the areas that need it most in any given moment. This system is essential to brain function and overall health, yet how it works has remained somewhat of a mystery.
Get more HMS news
Now, a team led by researchers at Harvard Medical School has uncovered new details of how the brain moves blood to active areas in real time. Their
findings are published July 16 in
Cell
.
In experiments in mice, the team discovered that the brain uses specialized channels in the lining of its blood vessels to communicate where blood is needed.
“This work helps us understand how you can get that super-important blood supply to the correct areas of the brain on a time scale that is useful,” said co-lead author
Luke Kaplan
, a research fellow in neurobiology in the Blavatnik Institute at HMS.
If confirmed in additional studies in animals and humans, the findings could be used to better understand findings on brain imaging tests such as functional MRI (fMRI). The insights may also advance understanding of neurodegenerative diseases, in which this communication system often breaks down, leading to cognitive problems.
A long-standing mechanistic puzzle
In the late 1800s, Italian physician Angelo Mosso observed something intriguing in a patient with a skull defect that left an area of his brain exposed: When the patient got angry, parts of the exposed area instantly swelled with blood — hinting at a connection between brain activity and blood flow.
A century later, this connection became the basis of fMRI, a type of brain scan that measures blood flow to different regions as a proxy for neural activity while individuals perform various tasks.
The brain is one of the body’s most energy-demanding organs, accounting for 2 percent of the body’s weight but consuming 20 percent of its total energy. To stay within budget, the brain must be highly efficient: It rapidly directs blood flow to the regions that need it the most, explained senior author
Chenghua Gu
, professor of neurobiology at HMS.
While the brain’s proportion of energy consumption varies across species depending on the organ’s complexity, Gu said, the brain is an energy-hungry organ in all mammals.
“There’s this an elegant evolutionary mechanism that’s distributing blood flow on demand throughout the brain, but we don’t understand how it works,” said co-lead author
Trevor Krolak
, a doctoral student in the Gu lab.
This blood-allocation process deteriorates in neurodegeneration, Kaplan noted, and understanding its inner workings could lead to new insights.
“If we don’t know how this system operates on a biological level, we won’t know how to fix it when it goes wrong,” he said.
A cellular signaling highway revealed
To understand what happens on a molecular level as different brain regions become active, the researchers performed a series of experiments in mice. Their analysis showed the brain rapidly communicates the need for more blood in a particular area via endothelial cells that line blood vessels in the brain. Furthermore, the researchers observed, the endothelial cells communicated so quickly and efficiently via so-called gap junctions — tiny channels that physically connect neighboring cells. The team also identified two genes pivotal to the function of this communication pathway.
A blood vessel in the brain. The left shows outlines of individual endothelial cells lining the vessel. The center shows smooth muscle cells that wrap around the vessel and produce the physical force needed to move blood through it. The right shows gap junctions that tightly connect neighboring endothelial cells, allowing them to rapidly transmit signals. Image: Gu Lab

The Trump administration announced its plan today to overturn a key
2009 Environmental Protection Agency finding
that underpins much of the federal government's actions to rein in climate change.

The agency proposes to undo the government's "endangerment finding," a determination that pollutants from developing and burning fossil fuels, such as methane and carbon dioxide, can be regulated under the Clean Air Act.

agency press release
.

. Transportation is the

in the United States.

"It boggles the mind and endangers the nation's safety and welfare."

dangerous flooding
in communities across the U.S.,
climate-fueled wildfires
that destroyed thousands of homes in Los Angeles and
hotter ocean temperatures
that made Hurricane Helene stronger and more likely to cause damage inland.
If the decision is upheld, it would speed President Trump's efforts to end former President Biden's ambitious climate agenda, and make it more difficult for future administrations to limit the human-caused greenhouse gas pollution that's heating the planet.

A cornerstone of U.S. climate action
In 2007 the
Supreme Court found in Massachusetts v. EPA
that the agency is required to regulate carbon dioxide and other greenhouse gas emissions under the Clean Air Act. Then in 2009 the EPA, during the Obama administration,
declared that greenhouse gases in the atmosphere were a hazard to people
.
The endangerment finding is the basis for rules regulating climate pollution from
coal and gas-fired power plants
,
car and truck exhaust
, and
methane from the oil and gas industry
.

In 2022 Congress included language in the climate-focused Inflation Reduction Act that labels greenhouse gases as pollutants under the Clean Air Act. That makes abandoning the finding more difficult. asking the EPA administrator to submit recommendations

data.title: ACM Transitions to Full Open Access
data.author: pcvarmint
data.article_summary: ACM正在向全面开放获取（Open Access, OA）模式转型，计划在2025年底实现所有研究内容的自由访问。这一转型旨在消除发现和创新的障碍，同时通过"ACM Open"框架确保出版计划的长期可持续性。该框架为机构提供无限制的OA出版，且不收取文章处理费（APCs）。定价基于机构的历史出版活动，具有公平和可预测的特点，并提供对ACM高级数字图书馆的完全访问权限，涵盖超过80万篇研究文章和多种研究工具。2026年，ACM数字图书馆将推出高级和基础访问选项，订阅ACM Open的机构将自动获得高级访问权限。高级功能包括对计算文献指南的访问、AI辅助搜索和研究影响跟踪等工具。OA文章的APC费用从700美元到1800美元不等，具体取决于作者身份和文章类型。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：不同学术会议和出版机构在开放获取（Open Access）方面的实践和政策比较，重点讨论USENIX和ACM的差异。

不同观点：
• **USENIX的优势**：  
  - USENIX会议帮助组织整个会议，而不依赖大量志愿者。
  - 所有论文都是开放获取的，不需要登录即可下载PDF。
  - 没有“总主席”和“地方主席”等角色，研究者可以专注于提交论文和参与程序委员会。

• **ACM的开放获取政策及其问题**：  
  - ACM在向开放获取方向发展，但具体许可条款不明确。
  - 根据柏林宣言，开放获取需要提供明确的授权，允许用户复制、使用、分发和展示作品，但ACM的论文似乎没有明确提供这种授权。
  - 即便能阅读和分享ACM的经典文章，但如果没有明确的许可，用户仍可能面临版权诉讼风险。

• **ACM开放获取的具体实施疑问**：  
  - ACM的声明提到机构订阅者可以访问大量研究文章和高级工具，但对已出版文章是否会开放以及新文章的开放范围不明确。
  - 疑问集中在已出版的800,000篇文章是否会解除付费墙，以及个人和机构的不同访问权限。

补充讨论：
• **出版费用**：  
  - 有评论提到出版费用高昂，从700美元到1800美元不等，反映了学术出版行业的商业模式问题。

• **对ACM开放获取进展的认可**：  
  - 一些评论对ACM在开放获取方面的进展表示欢迎，认为这是一个长期期待的变化。

争议焦点：
• **ACM的开放获取许可条款不明确**，特别是是否符合柏林宣言中的开放获取定义。这导致用户对其能否自由分享和使用论文存在疑虑。

44725966.article_content:
Open Access Publication & ACM
ACM's Transition to Full Open Access: A New Era for Computing Research
For more than seven decades, ACM has played a pivotal role in advancing computing research, fostering collaboration, and disseminating knowledge through its world-class Digital Library, influential publications, and premier conferences.
In a significant step to broadening access to computing research, ACM is transitioning to a fully Open Access (OA) publishing model by the end of 2025. This bold move marks a pivotal moment in making all ACM research content freely available and removing barriers to discovery and innovation.
ACM's journey towards Open Access has been a carefully considered, phased approach, ensuring the long-term sustainability of its publications program and the various educational, diversity, public policy, and community recognition initiatives it supports.
The move to Open Access is not just a change in policy, but a reflection of ACM's commitment to its community, where the goal is to remove barriers to publishing and accessing vital research, and accelerating the pace of discovery and innovation.
ACM’s approach to Open Access is centered on 2 key elements:
1. ACM Open – A Sustainable Open Access Framework for Institutions
ACM Open is a unique and innovative take on the Read & Publish model, offering institutions a seamless way to support Open Access publishing. For academic or research institutions, pricing is based on an institution’s publishing output, averaged over the previous three years, and remains fixed for the duration of the agreement. This approach ensures predictability in budgeting while providing unlimited Open Access publishing and full read access to ACM content.
Key Benefits of ACM Open:
Unlimited Open Access Publishing
Corresponding authors from participating institutions can publish an unlimited number of Open Access articles without Article Processing Charges (APCs).
Fair and Predictable Pricing
ACM Open’s fixed term annual price, based on an academic or research institution’s historical publishing activity, ensures transparency and budget stability. This pricing model helps institutions manage costs effectively while supporting Open Access publishing. For corporate pricing,
please refer here
. For government pricing,
please refer here
.
Premium Digital Library Access
Institutions subscribing to ACM Open receive full access to the Premium version of the ACM Digital Library, providing their users with unrestricted access to over 800,000 ACM published research articles, the ACM Guide to Computing Literature (which indexes more than 6,500 3rd party publishers with direct links to the content), advanced tools, and exclusive features.
2. ACM Digital Library – A Tailored Approach to Access and Engagement
ACM is introducing
Premium and Basic
access options for the ACM Digital Library in
January 2026
, supporting a sustainable approach to Open Access. Institutions that subscribe to ACM Open will automatically receive full Premium access. A stand-alone Digital Library Premium subscription will also be available, providing continued access to critical resources and tools that support world-class computing research.
The Premium ACM Digital Library Experience
Premium
access enables institutions to fully leverage ACM content, providing deeper insights, seamless workflows, and richer collaboration opportunities for their users.
Premium
features include:
Access to the ACM Guide to Computing Literature,
expanding research beyond ACM content for a broader view of computing research.
Advanced research tools,
including AI-assisted search, bulk downloads, and citation management, to streamline discovery and workflow.
Comprehensive research insights,
including article usage metrics, citation trends, and Altmetric tracking to measure research impact.

data.title: Russia Wants to Create a Silicon Valley in Cuba, Close to the United States
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 俄罗斯计划在古巴青年岛建立一个名为“数字礁”（Digital Cay）的高科技中心，目标是打造类似硅谷的技术创新枢纽，吸引超过1.5万名居民，包括专业技术人员和学生。该项目由古巴政府和亲政府媒体宣传，计划建设办公楼、实验室、住宅和娱乐设施等。然而，古巴当前基础设施薄弱，基本服务如电力、饮用水和交通匮乏，令该计划的实际可行性受到质疑。专家认为，该项目更多是俄罗斯扩大其在拉丁美洲影响力的地缘政治举措，可能涉及监控和技术控制风险。尽管古巴正经历严重的经济危机，该项目声称将为古巴数字和电信专业人士提供就业机会，但其实现前景仍不明朗。

• charlescearl提供了一个关于古巴信息科学的历史背景，强调古巴在20世纪80年代的信息化实践，尤其是Setién Quesada在图书馆活动中应用数学模型进行经济规划的例子，展示了古巴在信息化方面的创新和批判性思维。

An ambitious Russian plan promises to build a technology hub on the Isle of Youth, amid the collapse of Cuba's infrastructure.
The Cuban government announced this Friday the creation of
Digital Cay
, a Russian-backed project that aims to transform the Isle of Youth into a technological innovation center with standards similar to Silicon Valley.
READ ALSO:
Exchange rates today in Cuba: The euro continues to rise and the gap with the Cuban peso widens.
The proposal, presented by pro-government media outlets such as Cubadebate, envisions a technology cluster with more than 15.000 residents. Of these, 12.000 would be specialists and 3.000 students. The goal is to develop IT solutions tailored to Latin America and strengthen Russian industry in the region.
Dream infrastructure in a country without basic services
According to the released plans, the project includes the construction of offices, laboratories, industrial plants, residences, shops, recreational centers, schools, daycare centers, and university campuses.
However, the list contrasts with the reality in Cuba, where essential services such as electricity, drinking water, transportation, gas, and garbage collection are scarce. The project's own promoters emphasize that "high-quality communication routes" and basic services, which currently do not even operate in Havana, must be guaranteed.
More than development, a geopolitical move
Although the project is presented as an opportunity for Cuban technological development, experts warn that the Kremlin's true intention is to expand its influence in Latin America from a friendly territory.
Cuba, due to its proximity to the United States and its historical alignment with Russia, offers a strategic location for evading international sanctions and operating with greater freedom. In this context, Cayo Digital could also serve to conceal corporate identities and launch Russian products with a Latin American facade.
Surveillance and control risks
Despite the talk about “sovereign computing infrastructure,” there are preoccupied precedentscupPreviously, independent organizations have reported that similar Russian technologies have been used for espionage and political control.
READ ALSO:
Visa-free countries for Cubans in 2025: Complete list and requirements for traveling with a Cuban passport
In 2024, the Georgian government accused a Russian taxi app of transferring personal data to Moscow without authorization. And in Cuba, companies like NtechLab—specializing in facial recognition—have collaborated with surveillance systems associated with the regime's repressive apparatus.
A bet in the midst of the crisis
Cayo Digital's announcement comes as Cuba is experiencing one of its worst economic periods: daily blackouts, overwhelmed hospitals, shortages of supplies, and continued migration.
Despite everything, the project claims it will employ Cuban professionals from the digital and telecommunications sectors. Cubadebate highlighted that the José Antonio Echeverría Technological University offers training programs in Russian, which would facilitate the integration of local personnel with Russian technicians.
Stages and future promises
The project area orcupIt would cover 450 hectares. It is currently in the design phase. The first residences could be ready between 2026 and 2028, while the research centers and technology plants would be inaugurated before 2030, according to the developers.
So far, neither the Cuban government nor its media have questioned the real feasibility of this megaproject amid the national collapse.

data.title: AWS MCP Servers
data.author: belter
data.article_summary:
AWS MCP Servers 是基于 Model Context Protocol (MCP) 的专用服务器套件，帮助用户充分利用 AWS 资源。MCP 是一种开放协议，用于连接大型语言模型（LLM）应用与外部数据源和工具，提供标准化方式让 LLM 获取所需上下文。AWS MCP 服务器通过该协议为 AI 应用提供访问 AWS 文档、指导和最佳实践的能力，支持云原生开发和基础设施管理。

关键更新包括：2025年5月26日，所有 MCP 服务器的主要版本中移除了对 Server Sent Events (SSE) 的支持，团队正致力于支持更优的 Streamable HTTP 传输。AWS MCP 服务器适用于各种开发环境和 AI 工具，如 Q Developer、Cline、Cursor 和 Windsurf 等。用户可通过特定配置文件（如 `mcp.json`）在不同工具中使用这些服务器。

项目遵循 Apache-2.0 许可，欢迎社区贡献。更多信息和文档可在 AWS Labs 的 MCP 项目页面找到。

主要讨论点：MCP（可能指某种API或服务）的技术实现、实用性及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• [arianvanp] 认为MCP的代码看起来像是由AI生成的，给人一种不成熟的感觉。他还指出，MCP封装了许多API，但没有完全展示所有功能，这让人感到沮丧。他建议，如果亚马逊通过Smithy（亚马逊内部的协议中立API描述格式）增加JSONRpc支持，并通过Smithy生成代码，可能会得到更好的结果。

• [datadrivenangel] 关注MCP在激励机制和安全问题上的挑战，认为这些挑战可能会导致公司在初期热情消退后，因安全和商业模式问题而关闭MCP服务器。

• [blitzar] 表达了对使用MCP可能带来的高额账单的担忧，暗示了对成本控制的顾虑。

补充讨论：
• arianvanp对技术方案提出了具体建议，显示出对现有实现方式的不满，并提出了一种替代方案（Smithy + JSONRpc）。

• datadrivenangel提出了MCP在长期可持续性方面的潜在问题，特别是在安全和商业模式上的挑战。

• blitzar的评论虽然简短，但揭示了对使用成本的普遍担忧，这可能影响用户对MCP的接受度。

争议焦点：MCP的技术实现是否成熟及其长期可持续性。arianvanp对技术方案不满，datadrivenangel质疑安全和商业模式问题，blitzar则担心成本问题。这些都指向MCP在实际应用中可能面临的多重挑战。

What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and how does it work with AWS MCP Servers?
The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open protocol that enables seamless integration between LLM applications and external data sources and tools. Whether you're building an AI-powered IDE, enhancing a chat interface, or creating custom AI workflows, MCP provides a standardized way to connect LLMs with the context they need.
—
Model Context Protocol README
An MCP Server is a lightweight program that exposes specific capabilities through the standardized Model Context Protocol. Host applications (such as chatbots, IDEs, and other AI tools) have MCP clients that maintain 1:1 connections with MCP servers. Common MCP clients include agentic AI coding assistants (like Q Developer, Cline, Cursor, Windsurf) as well as chatbot applications like Claude Desktop, with more clients coming soon. MCP servers can access local data sources and remote services to provide additional context that improves the generated outputs from the models.
AWS MCP Servers use this protocol to provide AI applications access to AWS documentation, contextual guidance, and best practices. Through the standardized MCP client-server architecture, AWS capabilities become an intelligent extension of your development environment or AI application.
AWS MCP servers enable enhanced cloud-native development, infrastructure management, and development workflows—making AI-assisted cloud computing more accessible and efficient.
The Model Context Protocol is an open source project run by Anthropic, PBC. and open to contributions from the entire community. For more information on MCP, you can find further documentation
here

data.title: The world's first passenger jet was a death trap. Now it's brought back to life
data.author: rmason
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了世界上第一架商用喷气式飞机——德哈维兰DH106 1A彗星号（Comet G-ALYP）的首飞历史及其影响。1952年5月2日，这架飞机从伦敦机场起飞，飞往约翰内斯堡，标志着喷气式飞机时代的到来。相比之前的螺旋桨飞机，彗星号提供了更平稳、安静的飞行体验。然而，由于一系列事故，该机型很快停飞并被淘汰。如今，德哈维兰飞机博物馆恢复了这架飞机的内部，重现了当年的飞行体验。博物馆还保存了二战时期的蚊式战斗机原型。文章强调了彗星号在航空史上的重要性及其最终因设计缺陷而失败的命运。

De Havilland Aircraft Museum, England
—
Today, jet-powered plane travel is easy to take for granted. We’re used to that surge of speed along the runway that pins us to our seats, those moments when we burst through ominous clouds into bright blue skies, and the gentle pings warning us to fasten seatbelts. And we’re used to arriving at our destination in one piece.
But commercial jet travel is only 73 years old. Britain’s late Queen Elizabeth II was already the monarch when the de Havilland DH106 1A Comet G-ALYP took off from London Airport — as Heathrow was then known — about 3 p.m. on May 2, 1952, carrying the world’s first fare-paying jet passengers. Over the next 23 hours, with five stops along the route, it made its way 7,000 miles south to Johannesburg.
That flight marked a huge breakthrough in comfort and speed, compared to even the era’s top-of-the-range propeller aircraft like the Lockheed Constellation. Gone were the constant vibrations and the sonic assault from piston engines. The world had suddenly, irreversibly, entered the jet age.
And the first jet-plane builder to claim a place in the skies, beating out United States rivals like Boeing, was the British aviation company de Havilland. That advantage wouldn’t last: the original Comet DH106 enjoyed only a brief reign before a series of catastrophes led its entire fleet to be pulled out of service and then tested to destruction or left to rot.
The DH106 1A Comet has been restored at the de Havilland Aircraft Museum near London.
Barry Neild/CNN
Generations later, the only way to experience what it was like on board those first Comets is to look at grainy black-and-white film footage or color publicity photos of smiling families sitting on board DH106 1As.
Or at least, until recently, those images were all we had. Now a gang of enthusiasts has painstakingly pieced one of those pioneering jetliners back together — with thrilling results.
‘A beautiful sight’
Into the past:
The interior of a Comet DH106 1A — the world's first passenger jet plane — has been recreated at the de Havilland Aircraft Museum near London.
Barry Neild/CNN
Comfort in the sky:
The DH106 represented a revolution in air transport, being smoother and less noisy than the propeller planes that came before. Even in standard class, seating was roomy with plenty of leg space.
Barry Neild/CNN
Flight deck:
The controls look complicated but would've been familiar to the pilots of the day, many of whom had military aviation backgrounds, having flown during World War II.
Barry Neild/CNN
Maps and mathematics:
The cockpit also included a table for the navigator, who would manually calculate position based on speed and direction. An astrolabe was fitted in the ceiling of the plane so that the navigator could also take position readings using the stars.
Barry Neild/CNN
Jet power:
The Comet DH106 1A was powered by four de Havilland Ghost turbo jets which were embedded into the wings.
Barry Neild/CNN
Mosquito fighter:
The de Havilland Aircraft Museum is also home to the only prototype World War II plane still in existence. The Mosquito fighter, which was made on the site of the museum, was constructed from wood.
Barry Neild/CNN
Tested to destruction:
After fatal incidents involving the Comet, engineers rigorously tested the aircraft's fuselage and found that its rivet holes couldn't handle regular changes in pressure, leading to catastrophic breaches.
Barry Neild/CNN

The de Havilland Aircraft Museum is one of the world’s more obscure repositories of aviation artifacts. Located in a belt of farmland and greenery northwest of London, close to the eternally congested M25 highway that encircles the British capital, it’s easy to miss. There are signposts, but they point to a narrow lane between hedgerows that looks as if it leads to a farmyard or dead end.
Indeed, drive down it, and the first notable sight is a grand old manor house — Salisbury Hall, built in the 16th century and once home to Winston Churchill’s mother — that usually oversees some kind of agricultural outpost. But keep going, turn a corner, and the museum reveals itself: a field filled with the hulks of old airplanes and a series of hangars that hint at more treasures inside.
The site itself is a piece of aviation history. It was here, during World War II, that a local aircraft manufacturer, founded by British aviation pioneer Geoffrey De Havilland, began work to create and test the DH98 Mosquito, an unusual wood-framed combat plane renowned

data.title: YouTube rolls out age-estimation tech to identify US teens
data.author: speckx
data.article_summary: YouTube宣布将在美国推出年龄估算技术，以识别青少年用户并提供更适龄的体验。该技术通过多种信号估算用户年龄，而不仅依赖用户注册时填写的生日信息。被识别为青少年的用户将受到额外保护，包括禁用个性化广告、限制某些内容的重复观看以及提供屏幕时间和就寝提醒等数字健康工具。如果系统错误地将成年用户识别为未成年人，用户可通过信用卡、政府ID或自拍验证年龄。该技术将逐步向部分美国用户推出，并根据效果进一步推广。此举是YouTube为提升青少年用户安全性的最新措施，此前已推出YouTube Kids和监督账户等功能。与此同时，美国一些州也正通过立法来规范未成年人使用社交媒体。英国本周也开始实施年龄验证检查。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube针对未成年用户的保护措施及其潜在问题

不同观点：
• **对年龄验证机制的担忧**：
  - [Karawebnetwork] 认为YouTube要求通过信用卡、政府ID或自拍来验证年龄，可能会导致隐私泄露问题。如果平台错误地将成年用户识别为未成年人，可能会迫使他们离开平台。
  
• **建议通过硬件和家长控制来解决问题**：
  - [somethoughts] 建议推出一系列品牌化的Android手机和Chromebook，锁定使用Google Family Link，并通过营销活动教育家长如何设置和使用这些工具。这种方法比AI更具确定性，并能避免数字隐私问题。

• **对YouTube公告的批评**：
  - [hnburnsy] 批评科技媒体没有链接到YouTube的官方公告，读者需要自行查找信息。

• **对青少年识别的质疑**：
  - [jszymborski] 质疑什么样的信号可以识别青少年，而不会导致极高的误报率。

• **潜在的正面影响**：
  - [jauntywundrkind] 认为这一措施可能激励一些年轻人去寻找更高层次的内容，可能对用户行为有正面影响。

• **对YouTube动机的怀疑**：
  - [Traster] 怀疑YouTube要求用户提供法律ID的真实目的是增强其广告技术堆栈，而不是单纯为了保护未成年人。

• **对老账户的疑问**：
  - [pyuser583] 问到YouTube上开设超过18年的账户是否会被默认视为成年。

• **技术规避的担忧**：
  - [bell-cot] 一方面希望YouTube的技术能有效运作，另一方面也担心有人可以轻松构建浏览器插件来规避这些措施。

补充讨论：
- 评论中涉及的隐私问题、广告技术、算法调整以及潜在的技术规避手段都是围绕YouTube新措施的讨论焦点。
- 争议的焦点在于YouTube是否真正关心未成年人的保护，还是以保护为名收集更多用户信息以增强广告业务。

YouTube on Tuesday announced it’s beginning to roll out age-estimation technology in the U.S. to identify teen users in order to provide a more age-appropriate experience. The company says it will use a variety of signals to determine the users’ possible age, regardless of what the user entered as their birthday when they signed up for an account.
When YouTube identifies a user as a teen, it
intr
oduces new protections and experiences, which include disabling personalized advertising, safeguards that
limit repetitive viewing
of certain types of content, and enabling
digital well-being tools
such as screen time and bedtime reminders, among others.
These protections already exist on YouTube, but have only been applied to those who verified themselves as teens, not those who may have withheld their real age. For instance, in 2023,
YouTube began limiting repeated viewing of videos
that could trigger body image issues or those that display social aggression. The company has also been developing
digital well-being tools since 2018
.
If the new system incorrectly identifies a user as under 18 when they are not, YouTube says the user will be given the option to verify their age with a credit card, government ID, or selfie. Only users who have been directly verified through this method or whose age has been inferred to be over 18 will be able to view the age-restricted content on the platform.
The machine learning-powered technology will begin to roll out over the next few weeks to a small set of U.S. users and will then be monitored before rolling out more widely, the company says.
The plans to introduce age inference technology were
announced in February
as part of YouTube’s 2025 roadmap. The plans are also the latest step in attempting to make YouTube safer for younger users, following the
2015 launch of the YouTube Kids app
and the
2024 rollout of supervised accounts
. The features also arrive as social media more broadly is coming under increased government scrutiny in the United States, where platform makers, including Apple and Google,
have pitted their lobbyists against those from big tech companies
like Meta over who’s responsible for age verification and children’s safety.
In the meantime, a handful of U.S. states have taken matters into their own hands, as
over a dozen
states have passed or proposed laws to regulate minors’ use of social media. Many of these require age verification or parental consent, including those in Louisiana, Arkansas, Florida, Georgia, Utah, Texas, Maryland, Tennessee, and Connecticut, among others. (However, some laws, like those in Utah and Arkansas, are blocked by litigation at this time and are not enforceable, while others are still pending implementation.)

introduced this family project
in the spring of 2024.
I won’t reproduce those arguments for why we’re working on this, but in the current climate I feel like I hardly need to.
Since that post, our aversion to Google dependency has only grown stronger. Progress has been non-zero but not fast.
Here’s the table, with progress notes below.

Play my music
Plex, USB

TV

Pink indicates a strong desire to get off the incumbent service, green means we’re happy-ish with what we’re using, and blue
means that, happy or not, it’s not near the top of the priority list.
I’ll reproduce the metrics we care about when looking to replace Google products, some combination of:
Not ad-supported
Not VC-funded
Not Google, Microsoft, or Amazon
The list used to include “Open Source” but I decided that while that’s good, it’s less important than the other three criteria.
Now let’s walk down the chart.
Office
·
This is going to be a wrenching transition; we’ve been running the family on Google stuff forever, and I anticipate
muscle-memory pain. But increasingly, using Google apps feels like being in enemy territory. And, as I said last time, I
will not be sorry to shake the dust of Google Drive and Docs from my heels, I find them clumsy and am
always having trouble finding something that I know is in there.
While I haven’t dug in seriously yet, I keep hearing reasonably-positive things about Proton, and nothing substantive to
scare me away.  Wish us luck.
Data sharing (progress!)
·
Dropbox is, eh, OK. It doesn’t seem actively evil, there’s no advertising, and the price is low.
Photos
·
We’re a four-Android family including a couple of prolific photographers, and everything just gets pumped into Google and
then it fills up and then they want more money.  If we could configure the phones to skip Google and go straight to Dropbox,
that would be a step forward.
Video meetings
·
Google meet isn’t painful but I totally suspect it of data-mining what should be private conversations. I’m getting the
feeling that the technical difficulty of videoconferencing is going steadily down, so I’m reasonably optimistic that
something a little less evil will come along with a fair price.
Maps
·
The fear and loathing that
I started feeling in 2017
grows only stronger.  But replacements
aren’t obvious.
It’s a pity, maps
and directions and reviews feel like a natural monopoly that should be a public utility or something, rather than a corporate moat.
Browser (progress!)
·
Chrome has seriously started making my flesh crawl; once again, enemy territory. Fortunately, there are lots of good options;
Even people like us who have multiple lives we need to keep separate can find enough better browsers out there.
Maybe I’ll have a look at one of the new genAI-company browsers ha ha just kidding.
Search
·
The reports on Kagi keep being positive and giving it a try is definitely on the To-Do list.
Chat
·
Signal is the only sane choice at this point in history for personal use.
Photo editing
·
Adobe’s products are good, and I’m proficient and happy with Lightroom, but they are definitely suffering from bad genAI
craziness. Also the price is becoming unreasonable.
I’ve had a few Lightroom software failures in recent months and if that
becomes a trend, looking seriously at the alternatives will move to the top of the priority list.
In-car interface
·
It’s tough, Android Auto is a truly great product. I think I’m stuck here for now, particularly given that I plan to be
driving a
2019-model-year car
for the foreseeable future. Also, it
supports my music apps.
Discover music and play mine (progress!)
·
Progress here. I’ve almost completely stopped using YouTube Music in favor of Plex and Qobuz. Really no downside; YTM has
more or less completely lost the ability to suggest good new stuff.
TV
·
Video continues morphing itself into Cable TV redux. We have an old Roku box that works fine and I think I’ve managed to find
its don’t-spy-on-us settings. We’ll keep subscribing to Apple+ as long as they keep shipping great shows.  I have zero regrets
about having
left Prime behind
.
As for the rest, we’ve become migrants,
exclusively month-at-a-time subscriptions for the purpose of watching some serial or sports league, unsubscribe after the season
finale or championship game. The good news is that I
haven’t encountered much friction in unsubscribing, just a certain amount of earnest pleading.

data.title: Defending against account takeovers with passkeys and DBSC
data.author: gnabgib
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了如何通过增强身份验证和安全措施防御账户接管，重点介绍了使用密钥（passkeys）和设备绑定会话凭证（DBSC）应对当前主要安全威胁。文章指出，钓鱼攻击和凭证盗窃日益猖獗，尤其是cookie和认证令牌的盗窃增加显著。为应对这些威胁，Google Workspace推出了三项安全增强措施：

1. **密钥支持**：现已向超过1100万用户提供，具备防钓鱼和更强安全性的无密码登录方式，并允许管理员审核注册和限制使用实体安全密钥。
2. **设备绑定会话凭证（DBSC）**：目前在开放测试阶段，加强登录后的会话保护，防止其他设备使用被盗会话cookie。
3. **共享信号框架（SSF）接收器**：即将推出封闭测试，用于实时接收安全信号，帮助检测和应对风险变化。

这些措施旨在提升Google Workspace用户的安全性，有效防御账户接管风险。
