44725402.article_content:
Identity and Security
Defending against account takeovers from today’s top threats with passkeys and DBSC
July 29, 2025
Andy Wen
Senior Director, Product Management, Workspace
Google Workspace Newsletter
Keep up with the evolving future of work and collaboration with insights, trends, and product news.
SIGN UP
Over the past year, defenders have been facing heightened pressure on two fronts. First, attackers are intensifying their phishing and credential theft methods, which drive
37%
of successful intrusions. Second, we’ve seen an exponential rise in cookie and authentication token theft as a preferred method for attackers, with an
84%
increase in email-delivered infostealers in 2024 compared to the previous year. That trend has only intensified in 2025.
Today, we’re sharing three enhancements in account security to help organizations mitigate these types of attack vectors.
Passkey support is now generally available to more than 11 million Google Workspace customers, with expanded admin capabilities to audit enrollment and restrict passkeys to physical security keys.
Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) is now available in open beta to bolster protections after sign-in.
Later this year, we will introduce a shared signals framework (SSF) receiver in a closed beta for select customers and partners to evaluate and provide feedback.
These advancements can meaningfully enhance account security, marking a major step forward in defending against account takeovers for Google Workspace customers. Let’s take a closer look.
An easier and more secure way to sign in
Passkeys
are a passwordless sign-in method that can offer users a convenient and secure authentication experience across websites and apps. Unlike passwords, which can be guessed, stolen, or forgotten, passkeys are unique digital credentials tied to a user’s device. Here are some of the benefits of passkeys:
Phishing resistance:
Passkeys are inherently more phishing-resistant because users cannot be tricked into handing over passkeys to a malicious actor.
Ease of use:
Signing in with passkeys is as simple as unlocking your device, such as using a PIN or biometrics such as a fingerprint or facial recognition.
Strong security:
Unlike passwords that are often re-used, each passkey is unique and generated for each specific website or service.
Signing into a personal or work Google Account with a passkey on a mobile device
Signing in with passkeys is 40% faster than passwords for Workspace users.
To date, we have millions of users across enterprises, nonprofits, and educational institutions benefiting from using passkeys.
“We realized, as always in security, you have to keep moving, keep improving,” said
Odi Iancu, Executive Director of Enterprise Systems & Cloud Platforms at Wake Forest University
.
“But we have the tools available to us in Google Workspace for Education Plus to improve our security posture even further by moving to phishing-resistant second factor, leveraging security keys and passkeys.”
To learn more about Wake Forest University’s experience with Google Workspace, read their
customer story
.
Securing your account after sign-in
To further enhance account defenses after sign-in, we are adding an innovative protection to our security arsenal: Device Bound Session Credentials (
DBSC
). Available in the Chrome browser on Windows, DBSC strengthens security after you are logged in and helps bind a session cookie — small files used by websites to remember user information — to the device a user authenticated from.
Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC) provides:
Enhanced post-authentication protection:
Helps ensure only the originating device can access the active session.
Reduced risk of cookie theft:
Makes it meaningfully harder for stolen session cookies to be exploited on other devices by malicious actors.
Strengthened session integrity:
Helps bolster protections further with more granular account attributes when used together with
context-aware access
(CAA), even if an attacker obtains login credentials after the initial login.
Some of our customers have already begun using DBSC to protect their Workspace users, with more customers looking forward to leveraging the expanded functionality with context-aware access (CAA).
Admin console UI for the Google session control section to enable Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC)
Securing user accounts when a change in risk is detected
While passkeys and DBSC make it markedly more difficult for bad actors to gain unauthorized account access, being able to secure user accounts when a change in risk has been detected is essential. To that end, we are developing a receiver to consume security signals from security partners. The
Shared Signals Framework (SSF)
is an OpenID standard designed to enable platforms to exchange crucial security signals in near real-time. This framework acts as a robust system for "transmitters" to promptly inform "receivers" about significant events, facilitating a coordinate

data.title: EPA to revoke endangerment finding, the basis for regulating greenhouse gases
data.author: rntn
data.article_summary: 美国环境保护署（EPA）提议撤销2009年一项关键的科学结论，即六种温室气体对公共健康构成威胁，需根据《清洁空气法》进行监管。这一结论是监管汽车等排放源的科学依据。EPA局长Lee Zeldin宣布此决定，称其为“美国历史上最大的放松监管行动”，旨在恢复消费者选择权并降低生活成本。撤销该结论将取消所有相关温室气体排放法规，预计每年为美国人节省540亿美元。然而，EPA自己的报告显示，限制汽车和卡车排放预计在未来30年内产生超过2.1万亿美元的净收益。此举引发广泛批评，认为在气候变化影响日益严重之际，撤销结论是“刑事上的疏忽”。该决定的合法性受到质疑，最高法院曾裁定温室气体可作为空气污染进行监管。

44726832.article_content:
EPA proposes rollback of pollution limits
Details on Trump EPA proposal to roll back Biden-era pollution limits
03:51
The
Environmental Protection Agency
has decided to revoke a key scientific finding it published 16 years ago that six greenhouse gases are a threat to public health and must be regulated under the Clean Air Act.
Known as the "
endangerment finding
," it is the 2009 scientific basis for which the EPA has regulated greenhouse gas emissions from new motor vehicles, as well as other sources of climate pollution, but Administrator Lee Zeldin announced on
a conservative podcast
Tuesday that the agency is revoking the finding, calling it, "the largest deregulatory action in the history of America."
Since it was signed by then-Administrator Lisa Jackson in 2009, the finding has been used by the EPA to regulate sources of climate change-causing pollution from cars, power plants and other sources of transportation like planes, as well as oil and gas operations.
But Tuesday, the EPA
issued a press release
saying if the draft to revoke the finding is finalized, it would "repeal all resulting greenhouse gas emissions regulations for motor vehicles and engines, thereby reinstating consumer choice and giving Americans the ability to purchase a safe and affordable car for their family while decreasing the cost of living on all products that trucks deliver."
During his appearance on the "Ruthless Podcast," Zeldin criticized the endangerment finding, saying it put too many regulatory restrictions on transportation and stationary sources of greenhouse gas pollution.
"There are people, who in the name of climate change, are willing to bankrupt the country," he said.
Zeldin also said regulating climate pollution costs Americans too much money. If the proposed finding is finalized, it "is expected to save Americans $54 billion in costs annually through the repeal of all greenhouse gas standards," according to the EPA press release.
But the EPA's own
regulatory impact report
says limiting emissions for cars and trucks is expected to generate more than $2.1 trillion in net benefits over the next 30 years, including $820 billion in fuel savings and $1.8 trillion in public health and climate benefits.
Repealing the finding comes at a time when climate change impacts appear to be reaching new heights as 2024 was the hottest year on record, and natural disasters are growing more intense,
destructive
and deadly. Since 2010, there have been 246 billion-dollar disasters striking every U.S. state, causing more than $1.7 trillion in damages, and killing more than 7,700 people,
according to archived data from NOAA
.
"For the EPA to repeal the 2009 finding borders on criminal negligence," said Robert Howarth, a professor of ecology and environmental biology at Cornell University, in a statement. "The science was clear in 2009 and has become much stronger and clearer since: climate disruption is a large and growing problem; it is caused primarily from our use of fossil fuels and the resultant emissions of carbon dioxide and methane; and it is a deadly problem."
Legality of the endangerment finding
In 2007, the Supreme Court ruled in
Massachusetts v. EPA
that greenhouse gases are a form of air pollution that can be regulated under the Clean Air Act, but it tasked the EPA with making a scientific finding about whether the gases harm public health.
Two years later, the EPA published the endangerment finding, relying on extensive scientific evidence and public input to definitively state that greenhouse gases, which cause climate change, threaten health and the welfare of current and future generations.
"I think it's the most impactful thing I worked on in my career," said a former EPA employee who was a key author on the 2009 endangerment finding and requested anonymity because of current contractual obligations with the federal government.
"This body of scientific evidence met the endangerment test of the Clean Air Act," he told CBS News. "It has stood the test of time and the science has only gotten stronger."
The EPA's new proposal aims to question the agency's ability to set standards for car emissions, according to the press release. The full draft of the rule is not yet accessible on the EPA website or federal register to review.

44726832.article_summary: 美国环境保护署（EPA）提议撤销2009年一项关键的科学结论，即六种温室气体对公共健康构成威胁，需根据《清洁空气法》进行监管。这一结论是监管汽车等排放源的科学依据。EPA局长Lee Zeldin宣布此决定，称其为“美国历史上最大的放松监管行动”，旨在恢复消费者选择权并降低生活成本。撤销该结论将取消所有相关温室气体排放法规，预计每年为美国人节省540亿美元。然而，EPA自己的报告显示，限制汽车和卡车排放预计在未来30年内产生超过2.1万亿美元的净收益。此举引发广泛批评，认为在气候变化影响日益严重之际，撤销结论是“刑事上的疏忽”。该决定的合法性受到质疑，最高法院曾裁定温室气体可作为空气污染进行监管。

44727812.article_content:
Have you ever wanted to build your own reasoning model but thought it was too complicated or required massive resources? Think again. With NVIDIA’s powerful tools and datasets, you can train a small, effective reasoning model in
about 48 hours
, all
on a single GPU
. Even better, we’ve made all the code available to you to get started right away.
Let’s dive in.
Quick links to dataset and codes:
Hugging Face:
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
GitHub:
Data Curation Code
with NVIDIA
NeMo Curator
GitHub:
Training and Evalulation Code
with NVIDIA
NeMo Framework
Reasoning models and test-time computation
The advent of reasoning (or thinking) language models is transformative. By leveraging test-time computation scaling laws, more time is spent on generating tokens and internally reasoning about various aspects of the problem before producing the final answer. This makes them exceptionally skilled at tasks demanding deep critical thinking and reasoning, such as math and coding. This advancement signifies a paradigm shift in how language models are trained and used in various settings.
NVIDIA stands at the forefront of this advancement with its introduction of the
Llama Nemotron
family of open models, which are designed for high-performance reasoning across a broad range of tasks. To learn more about these models, check out
this blog post
. The principles discussed in this blog also apply to other leading models such as ServiceNow’s
Apriel Nemotron 15B
, highlighting the broader relevance of reasoning models in enterprise problem domains. To learn more about this model, check out
this blog post
.
From “reasoning off” to “reasoning on”: controllable reasoning modes
A key innovation of the
Llama Nemotron
models is their dynamic reasoning toggle, which allows users to switch between standard chat (“reasoning off”) and advanced reasoning (“reasoning on”) modes during inference via a simple instruction in the system prompt. This flexibility allows for optimized resource utilization: engaging deep reasoning capabilities for complex tasks like scientific analysis or coding, while reverting to a lightweight mode for simpler interactions for reduced latency and computational costs.
Our open post-training dataset for reasoning
To empower the developer community, NVIDIA has open-sourced a substantial portion of the data that was used in the post-training pipeline of the Llama Nemotron models. The
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
, containing over
32 million samples
across areas such as math, coding, chat, and sciences, provides a foundation for practitioners to train their own reasoning models. This dataset is key to teaching your model how to control its reasoning mode, mirroring Llama Nemotron capabilities.
In this blog post, we’ll explore how you can leverage the
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
,
NVIDIA NeMo Curator
, and
NVIDIA NeMo Framework
to train your own reasoning language model over a weekend.
The anatomy of the Llama Nemotron Post-Training dataset
The
Llama Nemotron Post-Training Dataset
is meticulously synthesized to enhance the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Organized into distinct subsets for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL), it encompasses samples from various problem domains. The following is a breakdown of the samples across different domains at the time of this writing.
Category
Sample Count
Math
22,066,397
Coding
10,108,883
Science
708,920
Instruction Following
56,339
Chat
39,792
Safety
31,426
Total Samples
32,011,757
Table 1. Sample domain and distribution of the Llama Nemotron post-training dataset
All samples in this dataset are in JSON lines (JSONL) format and contain metadata such as license type, source model, as well as the Llama Nemotron model(s) trained with that sample. Each sample consists of a prompt, along with an expected response with detailed chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning traces followed by responses (i.e., “reasoning on”), as well as samples with direct responses (i.e., “reasoning off”). More concretely, each sample has the following attributes:
input
: the prompt(s) to the model in the multi-turn chat completions message format. It always starts with a message with the role
user
, followed by zero or more turns, and ending with a message with the role
assistant
, such as:
[
{"role": "user", "content": "Can you help me understand the Pythagorean theorem?"},
{"role": "assistant", "content": "The Pythagorean theorem states that... Does that make sense?"},
{"role": "user", "content": "Yes, but I have a follow up question..."},
#
# ... (zero or more messages),
#
{"role": "assistant", "content": "Sure, happy to help!"},
]
output
: the expected response from the model (ground truth), such as:
The Pythagorean theorem states that in a right triangle, the square of the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides: a² + b² = c².
reasoning
: whether the sample is for reasoning “on” mode or not.

on
”, then the output conta

data.title: Lovense: The Company That Lies to Security Researchers
data.author: campuscodi
data.article_summary: 本文披露了Lovense应用程序中的严重安全漏洞。主要问题包括：通过用户名轻易获取用户邮箱的漏洞，以及无需密码仅凭邮箱即可接管账户的漏洞。具体而言，攻击者可以通过API请求和XMPP服务器操作，在几秒钟内将用户名转换为邮箱。此外，攻击者还能利用硬编码的密钥生成认证令牌，接管包括管理员账户在内的任何账户。这些漏洞于2025年3月报告给Lovense，但修复过程缓慢且不彻底。尽管Lovense声称已修复，但研究人员发现问题仍未解决。最终，Lovense通过漏洞悬赏平台HackerOne支付了奖金，但修复进展令人失望。

44723773.article_content:
Lovense: The Company That Lies to Security Researchers
0
viewing
July 28, 2025 • BobDaHacker
This post has been updated with new information showing the account takeover vulnerability was previously reported and allegedly fixed in 2023. See the update at the bottom. Lovense couldn't get any scummier.
What Happened
So it all started when I was using the Lovense app and muted someone. That's it. Just muted them. But then I saw the API response and was like... wait, is that an email address? Why is that there?
Just muting someone exposed their email - wtf
After digging deeper, I figured out how to turn any username into their email address.
So we had two big problems:
Email Disclosure
- Any username could be turned into their email address
Account Takeover
- Make auth tokens with just an email, no password needed
How Bad Was It?
The Email Thing (not fixed)
The email disclosure vulnerability was surprisingly straightforward once you understood the flow. Here's exactly how it worked:
The Attack Steps:
Get a GToken with encryption parameters:
Make a POST request to
/api/wear/genGtoken
with your account credentials
This returns a gtoken and encryption keys (x and y parameters)
Look up any username:
Take any Lovense username you want to get the email for
Encrypt the username using AES-CBC with the keys from step 1
Send POST request to
/app/ajaxCheckEmailOrUserIdRegisted?email={encrypted_username}
Include your gtoken and X parameter in headers
Get the encrypted user data:
The API returns encrypted user information including a fake email
Decrypt the response using the same AES-CBC keys
Extract the real email through XMPP manipulation:
Connect to Lovense's XMPP server using your account
Take the fake email from step 3's API response and convert it to XMPP JID format (@ replaced by !!!, add _w suffix)
Example:
cfc561791785b996b989593402dc41a8!!!lovense.remote.email_w@im.lovense.com
Add this fake JID as a contact to your XMPP roster
Send a presence subscription request to that JID
Fetch your roster - this returns both the fake JID you added AND the user's actual JID with their real email
Example real JID:
xyzeva!!!riseup.net_w@im.lovense.com
(which reveals the real email:
xyzeva@riseup.net
)
The XMPP server links them by ofId, so you can match and extract the real email
Remove the contact to clean up
The whole process took maybe 30 seconds per username manually, with the script we made though to automate it, it took less than 1 second for a username to be converted to an email. We could have easily harvested emails from any public username list. This is especially bad for cam models who share their usernames publicly but obviously don't want their personal emails exposed.
Taking Over Accounts (partially fixed)
While Eva and I were checking out the Lovense Connect app later, we found something even worse (Eva did most of the work) - it was making gtokens (auth tokens) without ever asking for a password. Just an email was enough.
The Attack Steps:
Get the target's email
- Either from the email disclosure bug or if you already know it
Set up the request parameters:
userName
: The target's email
userType
: "0"
pf
: "connect-pc" (platform)
ver
: "1.7.9" (version)
Generate the signature:
Create an MD5 hash of:
{platform}-#-{version}-#-{email}##0
Append timestamp:
{md5hash}-#-{timestamp}
Encrypt the signature
using AES-CBC with:
Key: The app's hardcoded appId (
a79643e665bb9833
)
IV: The app's hardcoded appSecret (
2DF65319C4D46284
)
Send POST request
to
https://apps.lovense-api.com/api/connect/genGtoken
Get back a valid gtoken
- No password needed!
These tokens worked on:
Lovense Extension
Lovense Connect
StreamMaster
Cam101 (through the login link)
Even admin accounts
Cam models use these tools for work, so this was a huge deal. Literally anyone could take over any account just by knowing the email address.
The Timeline (Get Ready for This)
March 26, 2025
: We reported both bugs to Lovense with help from Internet of Dongs.
March 26, 2025
: They said they're looking at it.
March 27, 2025
: They confirmed the bugs exist and they're working on fixes.
March 28, 2025
: We also put both bugs on HackerOne.
April 8, 2025
: On HackerOne:
Email bug: They said it's "already known and fixed in new version" (not released yet). Paid $1,000 total.
Account takeover: They downgraded it from critical to high saying it "doesn't involve database access." Also paid $1,000.
April 9, 2025
: After we explained you can literally take over ANY account including admins, they finally made it critical and added $2,000.
May 30, 2025
: We told them nothing was fixed.
June 4, 2025
: This is where it gets insane. They said:
Account takeover was "fixed on April 7" (it wasn't)
For the email leak, here's a snippet from their email:
"Following your report, we conducted a thorough investigation and rolled out initial mitigation steps, including a temporary fix for the script path issue you identified. However, resolving the root cause involves deeper architectur

• [Detrytus] 质疑这种做法的合理性，认为面包的表皮（即外壳）是最好吃的部分，因此不理解为什么有人会选择让内部变棕色而让外壳保持白色。

• [kazinator] 关注微波加热过程中食物内部和外部的不同反应，强调对加热时间的精确控制。
• [reverendsteveii] 将微波技巧与历史悠久的蒸面包技术相比较，认为这是一种新颖但非全新的技巧。
• [kelseyfrog] 通过将该技巧与Panko制作方法相联系，提供了一个实际应用的例子。
• [Detrytus] 提出了对该技巧的质疑，认为面包的外壳是其精华部分，因此不认同这种加热方式的合理性。

争议焦点：主要集中在是否有必要通过微波让面包内部变棕色而外部保持白色，以及这种做法是否影响了食物的最佳口感。

data.author: qsort
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在红队与蓝队框架下的应用及其在软件开发和安全测试中的作用。

不同观点：
• _alternator_: 认为LLM在添加测试方面有价值，因为测试便宜且易于修改，但在修复错误或添加功能时可能会作弊或写出不健壮的代码。
• recipe19: 认为仅依赖单一防御层是天真且危险的，应该有多层防御，因为不可能通过单一层次达到100%的安全。
• ants_everywhere: 认为AI在红蓝队都有用，且引用了AlphaEvolve作为红蓝队方法的例子，同时指出了安全系统的强度取决于层次和并行元素。
• ashton314: 通过RSA算法的例子说明红蓝队方法在数学中的应用。
• javier_e06: 认为在软件开发中，编码和测试不是两个对等的 forces，测试本身也是代码，也有可能存在错误。
• nostrademons: 从商业角度分析，蓝队行业比红队行业更具经济价值，因为蓝队确保基础服务运行，而红队则是附加的。
• furyofantares: 提到开放模式和封闭模式的思维方式，认为创意生成和批判应在不同阶段进行，类似于写作和游戏设计中的团队分工。
• mathattack: 认为LLM更适合用于“批判我的草稿”而不是“写第一稿”，因为LLM的建议需要手动检查。
• jacobjwebber: 认为创意的关键在于“筛选想法”而不是生成想法。
• TheGRS: 认为代理模型应参与红蓝队及管理任务，开发者更多是监督角色。
• spoaceman7777: 认为LLM更适合蓝队，因为人类更擅长红队。
• pamelafox: 分享了使用LLM进行自动化红队测试的经验，通过 adversarial LLM 和各种包来测试应用程序的响应。
• LeifCarrotson: 认为红队的重要性在于防止部署不安全的系统，但有些人为了短期利润而选择不进行测试和安全措施。
• resters: 提出LLM的上下文大小和推理能力之间的权衡，认为不同任务需要不同特性的LLM。
• zkmon: 认为红队不是单独的队伍，而是背景环境，进化通过前台和背景的互动和适应发生。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了LLM在红蓝队中的具体应用实例，如RSA算法和AlphaEvolve项目。
• 强调了多层次防御在安全系统中的重要性，以及在软件开发中测试和编码的不同角色。
• 提到了LLM的局限性，如不可靠性和不透明性，以及如何在实际应用中有效利用这些工具。
• 争议焦点在于LLM在红队和蓝队中的具体作用和有效性，以及在经济和商业背景下的价值判断。

data.title: Pay per crawl: Enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers
data.author: jaredwiener
data.article_summary: Cloudflare推出"按爬取付费"（Pay Per Crawl）功能，让内容创作者可以对AI爬虫访问其内容进行收费。当前，内容创作者只能选择完全开放或完全封锁AI爬虫，而这一新功能提供了一种新选项：创作者可以对访问收费，从而实现内容变现。通过使用HTTP响应代码402（需要付款），当AI爬虫请求内容时，要么支付费用获取访问权限，要么被拒绝访问。创作者可以设置统一的收费标准，也可以选择允许某些爬虫免费访问或完全阻止。Cloudflare作为收费方，并通过技术手段确保爬虫的真实性，防止假冒。该功能赋予创作者对其内容的更多控制权和经济收益机会。

44726161.article_content:
Introducing pay per crawl: Enabling content owners to charge AI crawlers for access
2025-07-01
Will Allen
Simon Newton
5 min read
A changing landscape of consumptionÂ
Many publishers, content creators and website owners currently feel like they have a binary choice â either leave the front door wide open for AI to consume everything they create, or create their own walled garden. But what if there was another way?
At Cloudflare, we started from a simple principle: we wanted content creators to have control over who accesses their work. If a creator wants to block all AI crawlers from their content, they should be able to do so. If a creator wants to allow some or all AI crawlers full access to their content for free, they should be able to do that, too. Creators should be in the driverâs seat.
After hundreds of conversations with news organizations, publishers, and large-scale social media platforms, we heard a consistent desire for a third path: Theyâd like to allow AI crawlers to access their content, but theyâd like to get compensated. Currently, that requires knowing the right individual and striking a one-off deal, which is an insurmountable challenge if you donât have scale and leverage.Â
What if I could charge a crawler?Â
We believe your choice need not be binary â there should be a third, more nuanced option:
You can charge for access.
Instead of a blanket block or uncompensated open access, we want to empower content owners to monetize their content at Internet scale.
Weâre excited to help dust off a mostly forgotten piece of the web:
HTTP response code 402
.
Introducing pay per crawl
Pay per crawl
, in private beta, is our first experiment in this area.Â
Pay per crawl integrates with existing web infrastructure, leveraging HTTP status codes and established authentication mechanisms to create a framework for paid content access.Â
Each time an AI crawler requests content, they either present payment intent via request headers for successful access (
HTTP response code 200
), or receive a
402 Payment Required
response with pricing. Cloudflare acts as the Merchant of Record for pay per crawl and also provides the underlying technical infrastructure.
Publisher controls and pricing
Pay per crawl grants domain owners full control over their monetization strategy. They can define a flat, per-request price across their entire site. Publishers will then have three distinct options for a crawler:
Allow:
Grant the crawler free access to content.
Charge:
Require payment at the configured, domain-wide price.
Block:
Deny access entirely, with no option to pay.
An important mechanism here is that even if a crawler doesnât have a billing relationship with Cloudflare, and thus couldnât be charged for access, a publisher can still choose to âchargeâ them. This is the functional equivalent of a network level block (an HTTP
403 Forbidden
response where no content is returned) â but with the added benefit of telling the crawler there could be a relationship in the future.Â
While publishers currently can define a flat price across their entire site, they retain the flexibility to bypass charges for specific crawlers as needed. This is particularly helpful if you want to allow a certain crawler through for free, or if you want to negotiate and execute a content partnership outside the pay per crawl feature.Â
To ensure integration with each publisherâs existing security posture, Cloudflare enforces Allow or Charge decisions via a rules engine that operates only after existing WAF policies and bot management or bot blocking features have been applied.
Payment headers and access
As we were building the system, we knew we had to solve an incredibly important technical challenge: ensuring we could charge a specific crawler, but prevent anyone from spoofing that crawler. Thankfully, thereâs a way to do this using
Web Bot Auth
proposals.
For crawlers,
this involves:
Generating an Ed25519 key pair, and making the
JWK
-formatted public key available in a hosted directory
Registering with Cloudflare to provide the URL of your key directory and user agent information.
Configuring your crawler to use
HTTP Message Signatures
with each request.
Once registration is accepted, crawler requests should always include
signature-agent
,
signature-input
, and
signature
headers to identify your crawler and discover paid resources.
GET /example.html
Signature-Agent: "https://signature-agent.example.com"
Signature-Input: sig2=("@authority" "signature-agent")

;keyid="poqkLGiymh_W0uP6PZFw-dvez3QJT5SolqXBCW38r0U"

data.title: Copyparty – Turn almost any device into a file server
data.author: saint11
data.article_summary: Copyparty 是一个便携式文件服务器，支持可恢复上传/下载，具有去重、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、媒体索引、缩略图等功能。它仅需 Python 环境，无其他依赖，可通过浏览器访问，支持多种协议如 HTTP、WebDAV、FTP、TFTP、SMB/CIFS。主要功能包括文件上传/下载、文件搜索、批量重命名、媒体播放、RSS 订阅、QR码快速访问等。Copyparty 还支持自定义配置和多种服务器协议，提供灵活的文件管理和用户权限设置。项目旨在简化文件共享，并提供丰富的用户界面和操作体验。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕"Copyparty"软件的功能、技术实现、许可证争议以及用户体验的讨论。

不同观点：
• **对软件功能的赞赏**：
  ◦ [skibz] 通过视频演示中文件上传和下载的例子，强调了软件的强大和令人印象深刻的功能。
  ◦ [vorgol] 认为该工具被严重低估，称其为惊人的工具，并推荐观看演示视频。
  ◦ [akk0] 称赞Copyparty是一个了不起的软件，并提到自己拥有该软件的限量版光盘。
  ◦ [darkwater] 认为这是高级用户梦寐以求的工具，强调其多功能性和开发者的高水平，同时询问开发者是否使用了任何LLM/agent。

• **对许可证问题的讨论**：
  ◦ [eadmund] 引用了GitHub上的文档，讨论了SeaFile和Nextcloud的许可证问题，认为AGPL许可证保护了用户和开发者的权益，而不是一个问题。

• **对软件应用场景的扩展讨论**：
  ◦ [sunshine-o] 强调了软件的速度和性能，并提出了是否可以基于Syncthing协议构建类似应用的问题。

• **对视频演示的即时反应**：
  ◦ [dmd] 起初认为这只是另一个文件浏览器，但在继续观看后表示惊讶。
  ◦ [visil] 认为这是一个令人惊叹的软件，并赞扬开发者对安全的重视。

• **用户实际使用体验**：
  ◦ [ratbum] 分享了自己使用该软件作为音乐播放器的实际体验，尽管界面不美观，但功能有效。
  ◦ [aquova] 表示首次了解该软件，并认为如果其功能如宣传所示，将非常有价值。

• **对软件细节的幽默评价**：
  ◦ [skrebbel] 对演示服务器上的"Activate Windows"水印表示有趣。

• **对隐私和自动更新的关注**：
  ◦ [j-bos] 引用了视频中的话，强调软件没有遥测和自动更新功能，同时仍然具有丰富的功能，表示赞赏。

• **对软件安装和使用的技术问题**：
  ◦ [HelloUsername] 提到在使用VPN时访问演示服务器返回403错误。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于软件许可证的"问题"上，[eadmund] 认为AGPL许可证是保护用户和开发者的，而不是一个问题。
• 讨论中也涉及了对开发者独自开发如此强大软件的能力和使用Python编程语言的赞赏。
• 对软件性能、功能和实际应用场景的深度探讨，展示了用户对该软件的高度兴趣和期望。

data.title: Performance and telemetry analysis of Trae IDE, ByteDance's VSCode fork
data.author: segfault22
data.article_summary:
这篇文章分析了字节跳动旗下的Trae IDE（Visual Studio Code的一个分支）在性能和隐私方面的问题。研究发现，Trae IDE存在资源消耗过高的问题，例如在相同项目下运行时，其进程数量和内存使用远超VS Code和Cursor IDE。具体来说，Trae最初有33个进程，内存占用达到约5.7 GB，经过更新后，进程数减少到约13个，内存占用降至1.9-2.5 GB。

此外，网络监控显示，即使在用户关闭遥测功能后，Trae IDE仍持续向字节跳动基础设施发送数据，且数据传输量较大。这些问题引发了对隐私和数据传输透明度的担忧。尽管开发团队在最新版本中部分解决了进程过多的问题，但遥测数据传输问题仍未得到有效解决。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕软件中的遥测技术及其数据收集实践的分析和争议

不同观点：
• kiitos认为在观察遥测选项测试时，如果用户不按提示重启编辑器，就无法得出有效结论。他对这种测试的有效性表示怀疑。
• barkingcat提到TheiaIDE作为一个VSCode的替代品，具有类似的功能，并提到其被一些大公司采用。这表明存在其他具有遥测功能的IDE选择。
• fjghajkhdfgjlk对CapCut（桌面版）的遥测数据收集感兴趣，尤其是其视频编辑器的UI体验，尽管担心可能存在间谍软件。
• spyridonas建议对Kiro（AWS分支）进行类似的分析，尤其是其数据收集实践，显示出对不同产品遥测实践的关注。
• cchance认为一些系统信息和使用模式的收集并不具侵犯性，并表示不介意这些数据被收集，反映出对遥测数据接受度较高的立场。
• drewbitt质疑为什么公司不愿意让用户关闭遥测，暗示对用户选择权的关注。
• asciii对分析中的过程表示赞赏，并猜测减少进程数量可能与增加的端点活动有关，显示出对遥测实现方式的深入思考。
• hollowonepl偏好使用TUI（如helix editor）并提到ZED可能包含遥测，显示出对遥测技术的警惕。
• happycodinggg详细解释了遥测数据与间谍软件的区别，强调了透明度、匿名性和用户可选性是关键问题，反驳了一些对遥测技术的误解。
• theusus指出讨论中未明确提到是哪一个IDE，提示可能存在误解或混淆。
• efitz建议使用pi-hole来阻止遥测端点，并提到对公司忽视用户偏好的不满，表明了一种主动防御遥测的策略。
• raverbashing对使用Bytedance的VSCode分支表示不理解，暗示对某些公司的不信任。
• leetbulb担心遥测事件可能被用来泄露任意数据，如源代码，显示出对遥测技术潜在滥用的担忧。
• drewbitt提供了一个GitHub链接，指出其中没有遥测，提供了一个具体的例子来讨论遥测的存在与否。
• isatty质疑为什么人们选择使用被认为是间谍软件的软件，而不是免费软件，反映出对开源和免费软件的偏好。

补充讨论：
• 对遥测数据的具体内容、存储方式、用户可选性和透明度是讨论的核心，尤其是其是否构成隐私侵犯。
• 不同用户对遥测技术的接受程度不同，有些人认为基本系统信息不具侵犯性，而另一些人则担心潜在的数据泄露风险。
• 对具体IDE（如Trae、Kiro、TheiaIDE、CapCut）的讨论显示出对不同产品遥测实践的关注，以及用户在选择软件时面临的权衡。
• 技术解决方案（如使用pi-hole）和替代软件（如TheiaIDE、TUI）在讨论中被提到，显示出用户在处理遥测问题时的实际策略。

Performance and Telemetry Analysis of Trae IDE: A Deep Dive into ByteDance's VSCode Fork
Executive Summary
This analysis examines concerning performance and privacy issues discovered in Trae IDE, ByteDance's fork of Visual Studio Code. Key findings include excessive resource consumption (33 processes vs 9 in VSCode), persistent telemetry transmission despite user settings, and concerning community management practices.
1. Background and Methodology
During evaluation of development environments for a personal project, I conducted a comparative analysis of three popular IDEs: Visual Studio Code, Cursor, and Trae (ByteDance's VSCode fork). This analysis revealed significant discrepancies in resource usage and network behavior that warranted deeper investigation.
Testing Environment:
OS: Microsoft Windows 11 Pro
CPU: Intel Core™ i7-14700KF
RAM: 64GB
Test Project: Identical codebase loaded in each IDE
Monitoring Tools: System Informer, Fiddler Everywhere
2. Resource Consumption Analysis
Process Count and Memory Usage

data.author: fidotron
data.article_summary: 日本知名模型制造公司田宫（Tamiya）的前社长及董事长田宫俊作于7月18日去世，享年90岁。他带领田宫从运输和木材业务转型为高精度塑料模型和遥控车制造商，尤其以迷你四驱车闻名。田宫俊作推动公司从木质模型转向塑料模型，并创造了田宫的标志性品牌形象和高质量声誉，包括著名的“双星”logo和“白盒”包装设计。他为确保模型精度，曾购买保时捷911并拆解以完善模型细节。2018年，他获得日本媒体艺术节的终身成就奖。他的贡献对模型爱好者和汽车 enthusiasts 产生了深远影响。

44728188.article_content:
Shunsaku Tamiya, former president and chairman of Tamiya, Inc., passed away on July 18. His death was announced on July 21, with funeral services attended by close family and friends. Mr Tamiya led the transformation of Tamiya into a world-renowned manufacturer of high-precision plastic model kits, radio control vehicles, and motorized Mini 4WD racers.
He joined the company founded by his father originally as a transport firm, and switched to supplying lumber after the war. That brought about an expansion into wooden models, primarily of ships and planes. After a fire destroyed the company’s lumber supply, it focused primarily on the models.
Not long after, plastic technology improved and began taking over the model kit market. Shunsuke Tamiya spearheaded the shift to
puramo
(a portmanteau of “plastic” and “model”) and in the process changed the industry. He helped fuel enthusiasm for cars, as well as other types of transportation, for generations of children and adults alike.
Shunsaku Tamiya was responsible for creating Tamiya’s signature branding and reputation for quality. He invited his brother Masao to create the “twin stars” logo and hired illustrators to create the “white box” look that made Tamiya stand out in sharp contrast to the box art of other model makers.
Most of all, he was the driving force in the unmatched precision Tamiya kits have come to be celebrated for. Famously, while creating the model kit for the 1976 Porsche 934 Turbo RSR, Tamiya-san sent his designers to Porsche’s Zuffenhausen factory several times to get the measurements and details just right. However, despite repeated trips there were still doubts about the kit’s accuracy. So Tamiya bought a Porsche 911 and completely disassembled it to get every detail correct. Eventually, the car was put back together, and Shunsaku Tamiya personally ferried Jody Scheckter and his wife to the 1976 Japan Grand Prix in it.
In 2018 Shunsaku Tamiya was given a Lifetime Achievement Award at the Japan Media Arts Festival for his contributions to the hobby industry. His contributions to the imaginations of petrolheads, however, will live on for many more years to come. Shunsaku Tamiya was 90 years old.

data.title: Htmx and URL State Management
data.author: lorenstewart
data.article_summary:
文章介绍了如何在HTMX中通过URL管理应用状态，避免复杂的客户端状态处理。核心思想是将状态存储在URL参数中，使页面状态可书签化和共享。文章通过一个示例演示了这一模式的实现步骤：

1. **服务器读取URL状态**：服务器端点读取URL参数并渲染初始视图。
2. **使用表单和隐藏字段保持状态**：通过HTML表单和隐藏字段在不同交互中保持状态一致。
3. **自动更新浏览器URL**：利用`hx-push-url`自动更新URL，确保状态同步。

这种方法依赖于URL作为单一状态来源，通过服务器端渲染和简单的HTML机制实现状态管理，避免了复杂的JavaScript操作。CSS类和隐藏字段帮助保持和反映当前状态。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网页应用中的状态管理与URL模式选择

不同观点：
• [Gilipe] 认为当前的模式非常可靠，建议放弃使用 HTMX 以减少依赖性。
• [cloudking] 喜欢简洁的方案，推荐使用 Alpine.js，这是一个轻量级的 React 替代方案，大小约为 16kb，适合构建反应式单页应用。
• [PaulHoule] 认为这是一种1990年代的经典模式，即使没有 HTMX 也能很好地工作。
• [Arch-TK] 以讽刺的口吻质疑 URL 携带信息的能力，例如自动滚动到特定标题。

补充讨论：
• [Twey] 指出示例中的 URL 由于内容动态变化而不适合作为书签，建议使用基于项目唯一标识（如主键或时间戳）的 URL 方案以实现可书签化。
• [cadamsdotcom] 认为将查询保存到 URL 是一种极好的用户体验设计，但因时间限制往往未被实现。他提到使用 LLM 可以快速构建这种模式，并询问是否存在现成的库或 React hook 来简化实现。
• [rorylaitila] 补充了 HTMX 类似技术的一个额外用例，即如何同步更新页面中非替换内容部分的链接状态，并介绍了自己库中的 'sync-params' 功能。
• [torstenvl] 强调状态管理应始终保持一致，过多依赖服务器端状态会破坏书签和分享功能，并询问持不同意见者的理由。
• [o11c] 提到可以使用 `location.hash` 存储较长状态，并建议不要基于 LocalStorage 恢复状态，以免破坏多标签页的正常功能。

争议焦点：
• URL 是否应该以及如何用于携带和恢复页面状态，以实现书签和分享功能。
• 状态管理中客户端和服务器端的平衡，特别是如何处理依赖性与用户体验之间的取舍。

总结：讨论围绕网页应用状态管理的不同实现方式展开，包括 URL 模式、HTMX 和 Alpine.js 等技术选择，以及客户端和服务器端的权衡。

Bookmarkable by Design: URL-Driven State in HTMX
When you move from React to HTMX, you trade complex state management for server-side simplicity. But you still need to handle filters, sorting, pagination, and search. Where does that state live now?
The answer is surprisingly elegant: in the URL itself. By treating URL parameters as your single source of truth, you get bookmarkable, shareable application state without needing to install another dependency.
The Pattern in Action
A URL like
/?status=active&sortField=price&sortDir=desc&page=2
tells you everything about the current view. It’s not just an address: it’s a complete state representation that users can bookmark, share, or refresh without losing context.
Quick Start: Three Essential Steps
The entire pattern revolves around three synchronized steps:
Server reads URL parameters
and renders the appropriate view
Forms and hx-include preserve all state
when making HTMX requests
Browser URL updates automatically
with hx-push-url
Let’s build this step by step.

• [cadamsdotcom] 认为将查询保存到 URL 是一种极好的用户体验设计，但因时间限制往往未被实现。他提到使用 LLM 可以快速构建这种模式，并询问是否存在现成的库或 React hook 来简化实现。
• [rorylaitila] 补充了 HTMX 类似技术的一个额外用例，即如何同步更新页面中非替换内容部分的链接状态，并介绍了自己库中的 'sync-params' 功能。
• [torstenvl] 强调状态管理应始终保持一致，过多依赖服务器端状态会破坏书签和分享功能，并询问持不同意见者的理由。
• [o11c] 提到可以使用 `location.hash` 存储较长状态，并建议不要基于 LocalStorage 恢复状态，以免破坏多标签页的正常功能。

争议焦点：
• URL 是否应该以及如何用于携带和恢复页面状态，以实现书签和分享功能。
• 状态管理中客户端和服务器端的平衡，特别是如何处理依赖性与用户体验之间的取舍。

总结：讨论围绕网页应用状态管理的不同实现方式展开，包括 URL 模式、HTMX 和 Alpine.js 等技术选择，以及客户端和服务器端的权衡。

data.title: iPhone cameras are good
data.author: sergiotapia
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了为什么iPhone拍摄的照片很少被印刷和展示。尽管iPhone相机表现出色，但在细节上仍与专业相机有明显差距。文章指出了几个关键问题：iPhone的鱼眼镜头会导致扭曲，尤其是在照片边缘的人物显得向中心倾斜；iPhone在处理阴影和光线时过度计算，导致面部特征失真，不如专业相机捕捉的自然和立体；iPhone的照片缺乏背景虚化（bokeh）效果，使得主体不够突出；肤色和光影处理也不如老款专业相机真实。这些细微差别对人类视觉感知影响显著，因此iPhone照片通常不适合用于大幅打印或展示。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：手机摄像头与专业相机的拍摄效果对比

不同观点：
• FredPret：认为专用相机（如无反相机）在搭配优质镜头时，拍摄效果远胜于iPhone，尤其是在旅行和家庭照片中。但iPhone的优势在于便携性和易用性，适合随手拍摄。
• hatthew：指出手机摄像头存在过度锐化的问题，导致细节处的色彩失真。同时澄清iPhone并没有鱼眼镜头，而是广角镜头，这种镜头只是放大了现实中的畸变。
• can16358p：认为iPhone摄像头在获取即时、算法处理过的HDR照片方面表现出色，尤其适合微距拍摄，但整体效果仍不及专用相机。
• dagmx：认为文章对焦距和色彩处理的比较不清晰，强调手机与相机在传感器大小、噪点控制和景深等方面的实质差异，而非表面上的比较。
• aosaigh：认为手机摄影在社交媒体上看起来不错，但在打印和仔细观察时，质量和编辑问题显现。同时，使用取景器拍摄有一种独特的体验。
• StrLght：认为iPhone照片在手机屏幕上看起来不错，但在放大、打印或在大屏幕上观看时，效果不佳。
• atonse：注意到iPhone视频在Apple TV上播放时出现奇怪波动，怀疑是iCloud压缩问题，并认为真实相机提供的控制和效果更好。
• tverbeure：不满iPhone对小细节的处理，认为其效果像被过度处理过。
• nixass：对Pixel手机照片在显示器上的表现失望，计划重新使用尼康D3200拍摄。
• sturza：认为手机摄影经过优化，适合手机显示，但不适合桌面观看或打印。
• bdamm：强调iPhone照片在实际应用中，因被拍摄者的舒适度和心态而显得更好，而非纯粹的技术效果。
• cunidev：认为大尺寸传感器在手机中能显著提升拍摄质量，但需避免过度AI处理。

补充讨论：
• epicureanideal：提出是否可以通过软件去除鱼眼畸变的问题，引发对镜头畸变及其修正的进一步讨论。
• aosaigh：对使用取景器拍摄的独特体验表示欣赏，认为这种体验在手机上无法获得。

争议焦点：
• 手机摄像头是否能在所有场景下替代专用相机，特别是在细节处理、色彩准确性和拍摄体验方面。
• 文章中对焦距和色彩处理的比较是否准确、合理。

总结：讨论主要围绕手机摄像头与专用相机在便携性、拍摄效果、用户体验和适用场景等方面的对比，各有优劣，取决于用户需求和使用场景。

44723461.article_content:
"iPhone Cameras are Actually Really Good"
Ever wonder why you never see a smartphone photo printed and
framed on the wall? I'll explain exactly why.
The photos above look similar at a glance, but there are some key
differences that seem small but are actually very sensitive to our
perception of humans:
The fish eye iPhone lens creates distortion, look at the
feet of the pink player. There's also distortion of the
players on the edges who appear to be leaning toward the
center in the iPhone photo.
Compare the jawlines (important!) of the players. The
iPhone photo is much less flattering. Real cameras
capture shadow more accurately. An iPhone does lots of
computation to try to make everything well-lit, but it
ruins important facial features in the process.
The blurred background of the right photo makes the
players "pop". This is called bokeh. The landscape is
also much more accurate to human perception, again due
to fish-eye distortion of the iPhone camera.
Let's take a look at an individual player:
More things to notice:
in the iPhone photo, the player is "leaning". His (long)
feet are on the left and his head is on the right of the
image. In the right image, the image accurately portays
his balanced and confident stance.
The players body is much more flattering in the right
image. His chest and shoulders look larger compared to
the "stumpy" appearance on the left.
The jawline is much more flattering in the right image.
The iPhone image almost entirely deletes the jawline on
the shaded side of his face.
The iPhone has a "hotdog" skin complexion.
Off with their heads!
Looking into their headshots in particular here, notice the
following:
The player in pink has natural color in his cheeks in the
bottom photo, but the iPhone photo puts it through the
computational mixer and loses this entirely.
The iPhone fails to accurately capture the golden hour sun
in the hair of the players.
The leftmost player's head is substantially distorted by
iPhone.
The above photo is from a professional camera. Let's compare iPhone
with its mighty 48 MP to a 2004 Sony Digicam with a paltry 5.1 MP on
auto mode:
Some notes comparing the above photos:
The iPhone photo again has the "hotdog" skin complexion. The
digicam photo is more realistic and aesthetic.
The iPhone photo has worse subject-background separation.
The water in the background is actually more detailed than
reality, which is captured in the digicam photo. The iPhone
foreground is also artificially well-lit. This detail
distracts from the subject.
The digicam photo has more dramatic highlights and shadows,
and more accurately captures the lighting on the child. If
you look at the right knee on the iPhone photo, there is a
clear lighting defect computed by the millions of lines of
code in Apple's image processing software.
I am sure there are many more differences that I am not able to see.
All these details might seem minor, but the human eye is incredibly
sensitive when perceiving other humans.
So this is why you don't see iPhone photos framed on walls. It's also
why top brands like The Masters never post iPhone photos.
Most photos are of people, but I'll add a couple more photos that
show the distortion inflicted by iPhone cameras:

不同观点：
• **质疑OP的概括性言论**：readthenotes1表示怀疑，认为OP对土木工程师的描述过于泛化，并提问其他土木工程师对此有何看法，暗示这种概括可能不准确或不公平。
• **对土木工程师的正面评价**：一些网友可能认为土木工程师在社会中扮演重要角色，强调他们的专业性和对基础设施建设的贡献，反驳任何对该职业的轻视。
• **对职业刻板印象的担忧**：部分网友可能指出，职业刻板印象可能导致对土木工程师的误解，强调需要根据个体表现来评价，而不是基于职业标签。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：OP的概括性言论是否准确、公平，是否会导致对土木工程师的误解或轻视。
• **职业重要性**：一些评论可能强调土木工程师在城市发展和公共安全中的重要性，认为他们的工作应得到更多认可和尊重。
• **个体差异**：有网友可能提到，任何职业群体中都存在个体差异，不能一概而论，呼吁对个体能力和贡献进行具体分析。

data.article_summary: "Placing functions" 是 Rust 中的一种语言特性提案，通过将对象的创建与初始化分离，使得函数的返回值直接在调用者的栈帧上构造，从而提高性能并支持更多特性（如 dyn AFITs）。该概念通过 `placing` crate 实现，使用过程宏模拟这一特性。关键在于使用 `MaybeUninit` 来处理内存位置的创建和值的初始化，并确保正确实现 `Drop` 以处理析构。尽管过程宏需要大量注解且无法访问类型信息，但这种方法证明了放置函数的可行性和潜在优势。放置函数还可以嵌套使用，进一步增强其灵活性。

placing functions
â 2025-07-08
what are placing functions?
a basic desugaring
thinking in placing functions
prior art in rust
q&a
what about placing arguments?
what about borrows / local lifetime extensions?
what about pinning?
are annotations necessary?
what about self-referential types?
why not directly rely on init<t> or &out?
can placing functions be nested?
conclusion
What are placing functions?
About a year ago I observed that
in-place construction seems surprisingly
simple
.
By separating the creating of the place in memory from writing the value to
memory, itâs not that hard to see how we can turn that into a language feature.
So about six months ago, thatâs what I went ahead and did and created the
placing crate
: a proc-macro-based prototype for âplacing functionsâ.
Placing functions are functions whose return type is constructed in the callerâs
stack frame rather than in the functionâs stack frame. This means that the
address from the moment on construction is
stable
. Which may not only lead to
improved performance, it also serves as the foundation for a number of
useful features like supporting
dyn
AFITs (Async Functions in Traits)
1
.
In this post Iâll be explaining how placing functions desugar, why placing
functions are the right solution for emplacement, and how placing functions
integrate into the language. Not in as much detail as Iâd do for an actual RFC,
but more as a broad introduction to the
idea
of placing functions. And to get
right into it, here is a basic example of how this would work:
struct
Cat {
age
:
u8
,
}
impl
Cat {
#[
placing
]
// â Marks a function as "placing".
fn
new
(
age
:
u8
) ->
Self
{
Self
{ age }
// â Constructs `Self` in the caller's frame.
}
fn
age
(&
self
) -> &
u8
{
&
self
.age
}
}
fn
main
() {
let
cat = Cat::new(
12
);
// â `Cat` is constructed in-place.
assert_eq!(cat.
age
(), &
12
);
}
A basic desugaring
The purpose of the
placing
crate is to prove that placing functions should not
be that hard to implement. I managed to implement a working prototype in a few hours over my winter holidays. In total I've spent maybe four or so days on the implementation. Iâm not a compiler engineer though, and I expect that the lovely folks on
T-Compiler can probably recreate this in a fraction of the time it took me.
Since I don't know my way around the rustc frontend, I implemented the placing crate entirely using proc macros. The upside was that I could get something working more quickly. The downside is that proc macros donât have access to type information, so I had to hack around that limitation. Which results in an API that requires a lot of proc macro attributes. But thatâs ok for a proof of concept.
Letâs walk through the basic example I
showed earlier, but this time using the proc macros. Starting by installing the
placing crate:
$
cargo add placing
We can then import
placing
and define our main struct
Cat
. We need to
annotate this with the
#[placing]
attribute macro because we need to change
the internal representation slightly. Here is what this looks like:
//! Original
use
placing::placing;
#[
placing
]
pub struct
Cat {
age
:
u8
,
}
Letâs take a look at what the
#[placing]
annotation expands to. As I said in
the intro: placing functions separate the creation of the memory location from
the initialization of the values in said location. For our type
Cat
, the
location must be of type
MaybeUninit<Cat>
. But because we want to keep the
type the same, even if we change how the internals work, we actually want to
keep
Cat
as the outer type name and move the fields into an internal
MaybeUninit
:
//! Desugared
use
std::mem::MaybeUninit;
/// This keeps the same external type,
/// but changes the internals to store the fields
/// in a `MaybeUninit`.
#[
repr
(transparent)]
pub struct
Cat(MaybeUninit<InnerCat>);
/// These are the fields contained in the original
/// type `Cat`. But separated so that they can be
/// wrapped in a `MaybeUninit` internally.
struct
InnerCat {
age
:
u8
,
}
Our desugaring needs to add one last bit to our type definition to ensure it works correctly.
Because we are now holding a
MaybeUninit
we have to make sure it calls its
destructors when dropped. This means our desugaring  needs to generate a
Drop
implementation
that calls through the
MaybeUninit
.
//! Desugared
impl
Drop
for
Cat {
fn
drop
(&
mut
self
) {
// The constructors guarantee this will never
// be dropped before it has been initialized.
unsafe
{
self
.
0.
assume_init_drop
() }
}
}
Now that we have our type definition, letâs show how to implement the
new
constructor. Because we donât have access to type information the placing crate
requires annotations on both the impl block and the method:
//! Original
#[
placing
]
impl
Cat {
#[
placing
]
fn
new
(
age
:
u8
) ->
Self
{
Self
{ age }
}
}
This is the trickiest part of the desugaring because it needs to split up the
constructor into two parts. One to create the place, the other to initialize the
value

data.title: When JavaScript Decided My Day Starts at 9AM
data.author: SenHeng
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了JavaScript中使用`new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')`创建日期对象时，默认时间为UTC凌晨，而非本地时间。例如在日本（UTC+9），`new Date('2000-01-01')`实际为`2000-01-01T09:00:00+09:00`。这导致作者的管理仪表板在日期过滤时，遗漏了早上9点前的数据。

**问题原因**：`new Date()`将日期字符串解释为UTC时间。

**解决方案**：明确设置时间为本地时区的午夜，并设定最大日期范围到当天最后一毫秒：
```javascript
const minDate = new Date(`${minInputDate}T00:00:00`);
const maxDate = new Date(`${maxInputDate}T23:59:59.999`);
```

**经验教训**：处理跨时区数据时，需注意日期字符串的解释方式，建议显式设置时间或使用本地时间构造日期。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：JavaScript中的日期和时间处理方法及其相关问题

不同观点：
• [svachalek] 认为JavaScript内置的Date类不好用，建议使用第三方库来处理日期和时间。他还提到了新的Temporal提案，作为一种潜在的更好选择。
• [hatthew] 强调业务逻辑应始终使用UTC时间，只在接近用户界面时进行本地时间的转换。
• [jahrichie] 支持使用UTC时间，并指出不应信任客户端的时间，认为服务器端时间更可靠。
• [kayodelycaon] 引用MDN文档，指出了当时区偏移量不存在时，日期形式会被解释为UTC时间，而日期时间形式会被解释为本地时间，并以Brendan Eich创建JavaScript的幽默故事作结尾。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了JavaScript内置Date类的缺陷以及可能的替代方案（如Temporal提案）。
• 对UTC时间和本地时间的使用场景和转换时机存在不同见解，特别是涉及业务逻辑和用户界面时。
• 争议的焦点在于如何有效处理JavaScript中的日期和时间问题，包括使用何种时间标准以及在何种层级进行时间转换。

44691986.article_content:
published:
2025/07/26
category:
dev
tags:
javascript
,
date
,
timezones
TL;DR:
new Date('2000-01-01') creates a date at midnight UTC, not local time.
In Japan (UTC+9), that means 2000-01-01T09:00:00, so our dashboard filters missed all data created before 9AM.
The Bug
We noticed something strange while fetching data for an admin dashboard:
records created before 9AM were missing!
Our date filters were simple:
<input type="date" />
Which outputs a simple string like
const minDateString = '2000-01-01';
So we wrapped it in a Date constructor and compared it in our filter
new Date(minDate) < item.date && item.date < new Date(maxDate);
How hard can it be, right? Well...
Why It Happened
I knew that
new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')
sets the time to midnight. What I didn’t know was that it sets it to midnight in UTC.
For Japan (UTC+9), that means the Date actually becomes
2000-01-01T09:00:00+09:00
.
So when we said “greater than January 1st”, we really meant “greater than 9AM on January 1st”. Hence, anything created from midnight to 8:59:59 was excluded.
The Fix
Instead of letting new Date() assume UTC, explicitly set it to midnight. (And while we're at it, set the max date range to 1ms before the next day.)
const minDate = new Date(`${minInputDate}T00:00:00`);
const maxDate = new Date(`${maxInputDate}T23:59:59.999`);
Lessons Learned
new Date('YYYY-MM-DD')
→ midnight UTC
Always check how date strings are interpreted when time zones matter.
For filters, prefer constructing with year/month/day explicitly or append a local time.

data.title: Two Birds with One Tone: I/Q Signals and Fourier Transform
data.author: teleforce
data.article_summary:
这篇文章主要讨论了信号处理中的I/Q信号及其在无线通信中的重要性。I/Q信号常被视为进入信号处理领域的“门槛”，因为其概念较为复杂，令许多人望而却步。文章首先比较了音频信号和无线电信号，指出虽然两者都是实数波形，但I/Q处理在无线通信中尤为关键。

文章详细解释了电磁波作为信息载体的作用，描述了正弦波的参数（振幅、角频率、相位移）如何用于编码信息。I/Q信号的复杂性主要源于“相位”概念，包括相位移和相位角的区别。

为了在不干扰的情况下传递更多信息，文章引入了正交性的概念，解释了如何利用正交载波实现多路复用。正交性在数学上类似于线性代数中的垂直关系，是解决波形干扰问题的关键。

文章分为两部分，第一部分探讨I/Q处理在无线系统中的意义，第二部分将其与傅里叶变换这一信号处理的核心工具联系起来。通过这些解释，文章旨在揭开I/Q信号的神秘面纱。

When a new member arrives at the Signal Processing Club, this is what they find at the club gate: I/Q signals. Perhaps a secret plot to keep most people out of the party?
Some return from here to try another area (e.g., machine learning, which pays more and is easier to understand but less interesting than signal processing). Others persist enough to push the gate open for implementation purposes (even a little understanding is sufficient for this task) but never fully grasp the main idea. So what exactly makes this topic so mysterious?
To investigate the answer, we start with an example audio signal drawn in the figure below that displays amplitude versus time for some spoken words.
For a comparison, a radio signal with digital modulation is plotted below.
Clearly, both audio and radio signals are simple real waveforms plotted with time. Why then I/Q processing is not common in traditional audio applications but an integral part of radio communications? For this purpose,
Part 1 delves into the significance of I/Q processing in wireless systems, and
Part 2 broadens the scope, linking the I/Q signals (also known as quadrature signals) to Fourier Transform, the most important tool in all signal processing applications.
Let us start with the nature of an electromagnetic wave.
An Electromagnetic Messenger
Wireless systems employ an electromagnetic wave acting as a carrier of information hidden in the variations of its parameters.
The Sinusoidal Wave
This electromagnetic wave is produced by an oscillator through acceleration and deceleration of charges in the forward and reverse directions. Since the charges primarily oscillate back and forth, the wave exhibits a sinusoidal form.
A reverse process occurs on the receive side. The impinging EM wave influences the electrons in the antenna through its electric and magnetic fields. The acceleration and deceleration of these electrons under the influence of these fields creates a tiny sinusoidal electrical signal.
In signal processing, a pure sinusoidal signal is also known as a
tone
. The title of this article refers to this tone, as we will now see how this simple signal alone leads us towards a deep understanding of I/Q signals now and Fourier Transform later.
The Message
This sinusoidal wave can be written as
\[
x(t) = A \cos (\omega t + \phi)
\]
where
$A$ is the amplitude,
$\omega$ is the angular frequency, and
$\phi$ is the phase shift.
I/Q Signals: Mystery # 1
Much of the confusion behind I/Q signals is hidden underneath the idea of phase. Therefore, instead of simply using the term phase, I will differentiate between the following expressions.
Phase shift: This occurs when the waveform is displaced to the right or left from the zero time reference (not aligned with how the waveform is defined, e.g., with peak of a cosine or zero of a sine).
Phase angle: This is the angle of a complex number in the plane formed by real and imaginary parts (more on this later). A good example of phase angle is the
carrier phase offset
between the Tx and Rx local oscillators.
Are these different versions of phase related to each other? The answer depends on the context and I will use the term phase shift or phase angle in the article for clarity.
Any of the above three parameters of a sinusoid can be altered with time to encode a message. The information in this message can be
user-generated (e.g.,
wireless communications
),
arising from the laws of nature (e.g.,
radar
, astronomy, remote sensing, biomedical), or
both (e.g., navigation and positioning systems,
beamforming
).
To people familiar with signal processing, the logical route from here is to show that the phase shift of the sinusoid can only be measured in two dimensions, not one. But this approach will require the reader to understand orthogonality, which is where we go next.
Are There More Carriers?
In bygone times, messages were delivered either by homing pigeons traveling long distances or by spies arriving on horseback at the gates of a walled city. For obvious reasons, having more messengers was essential for surveillance and governance. Therefore, kingdoms used to rely on flocks of pigeons and networks of spies.
Similarly, the question is how to get more carriers in the case of a sinusoidal wave to deliver more messages. To achieve this goal, there should be no interference among the carriers as a fundamental requirement. However, as shown in the figure below, when two carriers with different amplitudes (or phase shifts or frequencies) combine, they create a wave with an amplitude (or phase shift or frequency) that differs from both of the original carriers. Clearly, two waves cannot coexist without meddling with each other.
To solve this problem, we need to learn about orthogonality.
A Numerical Prism
In mathematics, orthogonality is a concept that generalizes the geometric idea of perpendicularity to linear algebra.

为了在不干扰的情况下传递更多信息，文章引入了正交性的概念，解释了如何利用正交载波实现多路复用。正交性在数学上类似于线性代数中的垂直关系，是解决波形干扰问题的关键。

文章分为两部分，第一部分探讨I/Q处理在无线系统中的意义，第二部分将其与傅里叶变换这一信号处理的核心工具联系起来。通过这些解释，文章旨在揭开I/Q信号的神秘面纱。

data.title: Microsoft Introduces 'Copilot Mode' in Edge
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary: 微软推出了Edge浏览器中的“Copilot模式”，这是一种利用AI技术革新网页浏览体验的新方式。与传统浏览方式不同，Copilot模式不仅仅打开多个标签页等待用户操作，而是主动预测用户需求，充当协作工具，帮助用户整理信息、比较选项、快速决策，并通过语音导航加速日常任务。用户可以允许Copilot访问所有打开的标签页以获得更好的上下文理解，未来还可以让它访问历史记录和凭据以执行更复杂的任务，如预订服务。该模式旨在减少干扰，保持用户专注，并通过个性化设置确保隐私和安全。Copilot模式现已免费向部分市场开放，用户可选择使用经典模式或尝试这一新体验。

主要讨论点：微软的Copilot及相关产品策略

不同观点：
• **nolok**：认为微软的Copilot产品线混乱且性价比低，用户真正需要的是能通过自然语言处理Excel任务的AI工具。现有的AI工具无法满足这一需求，微软花了大量资金却没做出实用的产品。

• 一些用户对现有产品的不满与期待改进，而另一些用户则对AI驱动的未来产品表示兴趣。

Introducing Copilot Mode in Edge: A new way to browse the web
By
Sean Lyndersay
For decades, the way we’ve used browsers has remained linear: open a tab (or 20), search for something, read a page, repeat. It’s a model that’s worked well, but it hasn’t fundamentally changed. Until now. As AI begins to reshape nearly every facet of digital life, we’re witnessing a turning point in how we interact with the web. Now, it’s worth asking: is your browser working for you as much as it should?
This is why today we’re excited to launch
Copilot Mode
, a new experimental mode in Microsoft Edge, and our next step towards building a more powerful way to pilot the web.
With Copilot Mode on, you enable innovative AI features in Edge that enhance your browser. It doesn’t just wait idly for you to click but anticipates what you might want to do next. It doesn’t just give you endless tabs to sift through but works with you as a collaborator that makes sense of it all. It keeps you browsing, cuts through clutter and removes friction to unlock your flow – all built to the highest Microsoft standards of security, privacy and performance trusted by billions of people and businesses worldwide – with you as the user always in control.
When you open a new tab in Edge with Copilot Mode on, you’ll see a clean, streamlined page with a single input box that brings together chat, search and web navigation. Copilot understands your intent and helps you get started faster. Copilot Mode also sees the full picture across your open tabs, and you can even instruct it to handle some tasks. Turn your browser into a tool that helps you compare, decide and get things done with ease. Over time, we will continue to improve and add features to Copilot Mode. And if at any time you prefer today’s classic experience on Edge, you can change this in your browser settings.
Copilot Mode is available for free, for a limited time, starting today in all
Copilot markets
, exclusively on Edge for Windows and Mac.* This is a fully opt-in feature –  be sure to click and try out the latest features. Help us shape the future of AI-powered browsing.
If you’re ready to join us on this journey, head over to
aka.ms/copilot-mode
to try Copilot Mode today.
Browse smarter with multi-tab context
With your permission, you can let Copilot see all your open tabs so it can understand the full context of what you’re exploring online. This means better comparisons, faster decisions and less tab toggling. For example, when researching vacation rentals across multiple sites, chat with Copilot to quickly identify which option is closest to the beach and includes a full kitchen – saving time and reducing friction.
Accelerate everyday tasks with Actions
Starting today, Copilot in Edge supports natural voice navigation. You can speak directly to Copilot about what you’re trying to do – whether it’s locating information on a page, or having Copilot open a few tabs to compare options between products. Just say what you need, and Copilot will help you move faster with less clicking and typing.
Coming soon, you will be able to give Copilot permission to access the additional browser context it needs, such as your history and credentials, to take more advanced and seamless actions – like booking reservations or managing errands on your behalf. Imagine simply asking, “Find me a paddleboard rental near work,” and Copilot not only finds the best option, but checks the weather, makes the booking and even suggests sunscreen or tutorial videos to help you prepare.
Stay focused and in your flow with easier access to Copilot
Bring Copilot into any webpage without losing your place. Whether converting recipe measurements or translating content, Copilot appears in a dynamic pane while keeping the original page visible. It’s perfect to help cut through distractions like pop-ups and long-winded blog posts, and to get straight to the information you need.
Pick up where you left off
Copilot will soon be able to guide you in your tasks and organize your browsing – past and present – into helpful, topic-based journeys. These journeys offer suggestions for what to do next, helping you stay focused and keep projects moving forward. For example, if you’ve been researching how to start an online business, Copilot can recognize that and surface relevant insights like recommending a tutorial to watch as you explore different website-building methods. You will always be in control, with Copilot only able to access your browsing content when you choose to enable it, and with clear visual cues when it is helping in the background. With such a powerful feature, our teams are committed to user privacy and security, and we are taking our time to make sure this is built right.

data.title: USB-C for Lightning iPhones
data.author: colinprince
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一款适用于多种iPhone型号的USB-C保护壳——iPh0n3保护壳。该产品售价为49.90瑞士法郎，目前所有型号均已售罄。用户可以登记邮箱以获取到货通知，需求量大的型号将优先补货。该保护壳支持通过USB-C进行充电和数据传输，兼容无线和MagSafe充电，且增强了磁吸效果。不过，某些需要从手机取电的配件（如有线音频设备、外部存储或显示器）需取下保护壳使用Lightning接口。该产品由瑞士制造，采用坚固的深灰色尼龙12塑料。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一款设备的优缺点及其相关配件的讨论，特别是对接口类型（USB-C、Lightning）和传输速度的看法。

不同观点：
• seltzered_认为，该设备如果配备耳机插孔就会非常完美，并提到了2017年一个相关的Kickstarter项目，该项目尝试为iPhone制作一个可以为AirPods充电的USB-C保护壳。
• colinprince对某个视频表示赞赏，并分享了视频链接，但未详细说明具体观点。
• BobbyTables2对某人拥有大量设备表示惊讶，认为这超出了普通爱好者的范围。
• p_ing指出，该设备只提供USB 2.0的速度，认为如果速度不是问题，那这是一个不错的升级。
• tamimio认为，比起更换为USB-C接口，他更希望Lightning接口能提升到USB 3.0的速度，并认为Lightning接口设计本身是坚固的。
• chromatin则表达了相反的观点，表示自己其实希望为USB-C设备配备Lightning接口，与tamimio的观点形成对比。
• OrvalWintermute用幽默的方式表达了对该设备的高度兴趣，并希望能够购买。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了接口类型（USB-C与Lightning）和传输速度的争议，特别是p_ing和tamimio对于USB 2.0速度和USB 3.0需求的看法，与chromatin对接口类型的反向需求形成对比。
• BobbyTables2对设备拥有者的设备数量表示惊讶，引发了对设备拥有量与爱好者身份的讨论。
• 链接和视频内容提供了额外的背景信息，特别是关于历史上对iPhone接口扩展的尝试。

data.title: Canada's Travel Boycott Backfires on Ordinary Canadians
data.author: mikhael
data.article_summary: 加拿大人正感受到国内旅行成本飙升的影响。由于美国旅行禁令，更多人选择国内游，导致航班和酒店需求增加，价格随之上涨。许多人在Reddit上抱怨国内航班和住宿比国际旅行还贵，例如有人发现四口之家的航班费用高达3500美元，而飞欧洲却更便宜。数据显示，酒店价格同比上涨3%，而安大略省一周的小屋租金可达2000至3000美元。政府虽尝试通过"Canada Strong Pass"计划降低价格，但国内旅行对许多人来说仍成为奢侈。高税费和需求增加是价格高昂的主要原因。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：加拿大抵制某些商品的目的和效果

不同观点：
• 观点一：抵制行动的重点不在于让加拿大人立刻看到经济上的便宜，而是在于对企业施加压力，促使其改变不当行为。例如，[palata]指出，抵制的目的不是为了让商品立刻变得更便宜，而是为了更长远的社会或政治影响。

• 观点二：有人认为抵制行动应该直接带来经济上的好处，比如让加拿大人能够以更低的价格购买商品。这种观点关注的是短期内的消费者利益，而非长期的政治或社会影响。

• 观点三：另一种看法是，抵制行动的效果需要从多个维度来衡量，包括对企业声誉的影响、对国际关系的影响等，而不仅仅是看国内价格的变化。[Someone123]可能认为，抵制可以通过影响企业决策，从而带来更广泛的变化。

补充讨论：

data.title: Dropbox Passwords Is Closing
data.author: h1fra
data.article_summary: Dropbox Passwords sera supprimé le 28 octobre 2025, dans le cadre de la concentration de Dropbox sur d'autres fonctionnalités. À partir du 28 août 2025, l'accès sera limité à la consultation seule, et à partir du 11 septembre 2025, l'application mobile cessera de fonctionner. Les utilisateurs doivent exporter leurs mots de passe avant le 28 octobre 2025, sous peine de perte définitive des données. Dropbox recommande l'utilisation de 1Password pour transférer les informations. Les administrateurs doivent s'assurer que chaque membre de l'équipe exporte ses données. Après la date limite, toutes les données seront supprimées définitivement et de manière sécurisée.
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Dropbox放弃密码管理产品的战略合理性及其产品扩展策略

不同观点：
• [stmw] 认为从战略上，Dropbox放弃密码管理产品是合理的。虽然密码管理是其核心产品的天然补充，但维护这类产品非常复杂，尤其是在浏览器、网站以及移动端不断变化的情况下。如果没有显著的用户附着率，放弃该产品是合理的决策。

• [rjh29] 对比了Google，指出Google虽然经常取消产品，但在核心应用如文件、密码、书签、地图和邮件等方面保持了长期稳定性。暗示Dropbox在核心产品稳定性上不如Google，质疑其放弃密码管理产品的决策。

• [treetalker] 对Dropbox不断扩展产品线表示不满，认为Dropbox应该专注于其核心功能，即文件存储服务。对未来可能推出的如Dropbox Email或基于大语言模型（LLM）的产品表示讽刺和怀疑。

补充讨论：
• 对密码管理产品的维护难度进行了讨论，指出其技术复杂性和持续维护的挑战。
• 不同用户对产品扩展策略的态度不一，有的理解技术维护的困难，有的则希望公司专注于核心业务，避免过度扩展。
• 争议焦点在于Dropbox是否应该扩展产品线以及放弃密码管理产品的合理性，一方认为这是战略调整的必要举措，另一方则质疑其产品管理和长期战略的稳定性。

44727653.article_content:
Interruption de Dropbox Passwords
Mis à jour Jul 29, 2025
person icon
Les informations contenues dans cet article concernent tous les utilisateurs de Dropbox Passwords, sauf indication contraire.
Pourquoi Dropbox Passwords ne sera bientôt plus disponible ?
Dans le cadre de nos efforts pour nous concentrer sur l’amélioration d’autres fonctionnalités de notre produit de base, Dropbox Passwords sera supprimé le 28 octobre 2025.
Nous vous recommandons de transférer vos mots de passe vers une autre application de gestion de mots de passe telle que
1Password
, un gestionnaire de mots de passe hautement fiable et sécurisé.
Quand Dropbox Passwords sera supprimé ?
Dropbox Passwords sera entièrement supprimé le 28 octobre 2025. Les modifications apportées au produit se feront de manière progressive. Les dates clés sont les suivantes :
28/08/25 : Dropbox Passwords sera disponible en lecture seule dans l’application mobile et l’extension de navigateur
. Vous pourrez toujours consulter vos noms d’utilisateur, mots de passe et informations de paiement enregistrés, mais vous ne pourrez plus en ajouter de nouveaux. Par ailleurs, la fonctionnalité de saisie automatique sera désactivée.
11/09/25 : l’application mobile Dropbox Passwords cessera de fonctionner
. Cependant, vous pourrez toujours accéder à vos informations de mots de passe via l’extension de navigateur.
28/10/25 : Dropbox Passwords sera entièrement supprimé
. Vous ne pourrez plus accéder aux noms d’utilisateur, mots de passe et informations de paiement enregistrés, ni en ajouter de nouveaux. Ces informations seront supprimées de manière permanente et sécurisée de nos serveurs. La fonctionnalité de surveillance du dark web sera supprimée.
Comment exporter mes données Dropbox Passwords ?
Il existe plusieurs façons d’exporter les mots de passe stockés dans Dropbox Passwords vers d’autres gestionnaires de mots de passe. Nous vous recommandons d’utiliser
1Password
pour importer facilement vos informations de mot de passe et protéger vos comptes à l’avenir.
warning icon

Vous pouvez exporter tous les identifiants de connexion et cartes de paiement de votre compte depuis Dropbox Passwords sous forme de fichier CSV. Pour une expérience optimale, nous vous recommandons d’utiliser l’extension de navigateur. Pour créer votre fichier CSV, suivez les étapes suivantes :

44729180.article_content:
The world's biggest passenger planes keep breaking down
Angus Whitley and Danny Lee / Bloomberg
Mon, 28 Jul 2025, 9:44 am
6 min read
In this article:
AIR.PA
BA
In its youth, the A380 was a triumph of international collaboration, with 4 million parts made by 1,500 companies worldwide
The world’s largest commercial passenger jet, the Airbus A380, enjoyed an unexpected resurgence hauling full loads of passengers when global travel rebounded after the pandemic. But keeping the ageing superjumbo safely airborne is becoming an increasingly expensive headache for airlines.
Two decades after its maiden flight, regulatory bulletins ordering repairs, inspections or replacement parts for the massive four-engined plane are piling up. While some are procedural, such as a demand for timely equipment checks, others are more serious.
Leaking escape slides, cracked seals and a ruptured landing-gear axle feature among 95 airworthiness directives for the A380 listed by the European Union Aviation Safety Agency since January 2020.
That’s about double the number of directives for large Boeing Co aircraft in the same period.
With newer, more fuel-efficient jets in short supply, airlines committed to the twin-deck A380 have little choice but to keep flying it. In its youth, the A380 was a triumph of international collaboration, with 4 million parts made by 1,500 companies worldwide. Now, in old age, the aircraft’s complexity is testing aviation’s fractured supply chains in the post-Covid era.
“The A380 is a complex aeroplane whose scale does make it more demanding to maintain compared to other aircraft,” the European Union Aviation Safety Agency said in a statement. “It is very important for safety that there is no stigma attached to publishing an airworthiness directive -– safety must come first.”
The agency said such directives, which mandate actions to make an aircraft safe, “can vary hugely in scope and urgency.” The volume of airworthiness directives for different planes “is not a good basis for comparison,” EASA said.
Stranded Passengers
However, with the capacity to carry 485 passengers or more, delays caused by mechanical failures can be costly and create a cascade of scheduling headaches. A Qantas Airways Ltd. A380 on the flagship Sydney-London route broke down in Singapore on May 7 with fuel-pump problems. The onward flight to London was pushed back more than 24 hours and passengers accommodated in hotels.
That was at least the second fuel-pump issue to delay QF1 in Singapore since Qantas reactivated its A380s. More recently, Qantas passengers who were due to depart Singapore on July 14 for Sydney on an A380 were delayed for days because of technical difficulties. Plans to retrieve them sooner were complicated by damage to another A380 at Sydney airport, when an aerobridge slammed into one of the engines.
Story Continues
A British Airways A380, G-XLEB, recently spent more than 100 days in Manila. After returning to London Heathrow in mid-June, it flew just seven days of the next 30, according to Flightradar24. Still, IAG SA-owned British Airways from next year will embark on an interior upgrade program, including overhauling A380 cabins, suggesting the airline will keep flying the plane for years.
For airlines using the A380, large-capacity alternatives are scarce. Boeing’s new 777X is years behind schedule and Airbus can’t make long-haul A350s fast enough. Meanwhile, A380 operators are left with an out-of-production superjumbo that will only become more needy and more expensive to run. In online aviation forums, some services are gaining a name for breakdowns, cancellations or overnight delays.
In a statement, Airbus said the A380 “continues to operate scheduled services with a high level of operational reliability, standing at 99% for the global fleet over the past 12 months. Airbus is committed to providing full technical support to customers to ensure that they can optimize operations with their A380 fleets, and this will continue as long as the aircraft remains in service.”
An Airbus A380 airplane during its maiden flight in France in 2005. Photographer: Marc de Tienda/Bloomberg
60,000 Hours
Meanwhile, A380s are taking up space and manpower in workshops around the world, exacerbating a shortage of repair facilities for the wider commercial fleet. A comprehensive check of the massive plane can consume 60,000 hours of labour, according to aircraft repairer Lufthansa Technik.
Qantas is sending some double-deckers to Dresden in Germany to be overhauled; British Airways flies its to Manila for repairs; and Emirates, the world’s biggest operator of A380s, maintains some in China.
Some of the aircraft’s recent faults stem from prolonged periods on the ground during the pandemic, when airlines parked their A380s in the Californian desert, central Spain or the Australian outback.
An airworthiness directive from the European Union Aviation Safety Agency on May 16 ordered emergency inflatable escape slides to be replaced. Glu

data.title: Someone made a 128000 line PR to opencut
data.author: agtestdvn
data.article_summary: 这篇文章主要描述了OpenCut项目的一次代码合并请求和相关更新。贡献者donghaozhang试图将480个提交合并到主分支，并列举了所做的多项改进和新增功能，包括视频导出、文本到图像转换、图像编辑、媒体面板导出按钮、AI视频生成、项目卡片组织、Electron构建支持等。此外，还进行了全面的测试套件和文档更新，涵盖视频处理、AI工作流和UI测试等方面。代码改动包括增强`.gitignore`以覆盖更多构建输出和环境文件，以及改进FAL.ai API的错误处理，提供更友好的用户提示信息。项目团队对贡献表示感谢，并提到需要手动审查部分代码以确认其对项目的实用性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对一个大型代码变更请求（PR）的讨论，尤其是其质量、目的以及是否应该被接受。

不同观点：
• **支持与同情的观点**：
  - *maxbond*：认为不应嘲笑请求帮助的人，因为他们并没有自大，而是明确表示需要指导，且没有期望这个10万行代码的变更会被接受。
  - *cadamsdotcom*：提出随着新技术的发展，社区需要学习新的礼仪，这种情况在技术进步中常见。

• **反对与批评的观点**：
  - *fn-mote*：认为这种PR显然是会被立即拒绝的，没必要浪费时间阅读，将其比作垃圾信息。
  - *delecti*：对PR没有被立即拒绝表示不满，认为项目维护者有超乎寻常的耐心。
  - *andrewmcwatters*：认为这种行为是荒谬的，并指出在实际工作场所中也遇到过类似情况。

• **中立但分析的观点**：
  - *kelseyfrog*：指出问题的根源显而易见，但没有进一步展开。
  - *bee_rider*：猜测提交者的意图可能是先大量生成代码再让维护者选择有用的部分，但这种方式显然不合适。

• **关于AI工具的讨论**：
  - *a2128*：提到曾遇到类似PR，怀疑使用了AI工具，认为这对非程序员有帮助，但可能带来数据丢失或安全漏洞的风险。
  - *RGBCube*：分享使用Claude Code的经验，指出其生成过多代码且需要大量指导，但认为对繁重工作有用。

• **其他关注点**：
  - *Ancalagon*：关心在Claude Code上花费的成本。
  - *bwfan123*：以幽默方式评论这种高产量的工作在某些公司可能得到奖励。
  - *5pl1n73r*：质疑AI工具能生成多大可工作的代码库。
  - *mgerdts*：引用Coderabbit的代码审查时间估算，认为有趣。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于这种大型且质量存疑的PR是否应该被接受，以及如何应对新技术带来的新挑战。
- 关于AI工具的讨论反映了当前技术在实际应用中的潜力和局限性。
- 评论中也包含了对标题和帖子风格的批评，认为其有误导性或不合适。

  - *fn-mote*：认为这种PR显然是会被立即拒绝的，没必要浪费时间阅读，将其比作垃圾信息。
  - *delecti*：对PR没有被立即拒绝表示不满，认为项目维护者有超乎寻常的耐心。
  - *andrewmcwatters*：认为这种行为是荒谬的，并指出在实际工作场所中也遇到过类似情况。

• **中立但分析的观点**：
  - *kelseyfrog*：指出问题的根源显而易见，但没有进一步展开。
  - *bee_rider*：猜测提交者的意图可能是先大量生成代码再让维护者选择有用的部分，但这种方式显然不合适。

• **关于AI工具的讨论**：
  - *a2128*：提到曾遇到类似PR，怀疑使用了AI工具，认为这对非程序员有帮助，但可能带来数据丢失或安全漏洞的风险。
  - *RGBCube*：分享使用Claude Code的经验，指出其生成过多代码且需要大量指导，但认为对繁重工作有用。

• **其他关注点**：
  - *Ancalagon*：关心在Claude Code上花费的成本。
  - *bwfan123*：以幽默方式评论这种高产量的工作在某些公司可能得到奖励。
  - *5pl1n73r*：质疑AI工具能生成多大可工作的代码库。
  - *mgerdts*：引用Coderabbit的代码审查时间估算，认为有趣。

补充讨论：
- 争议焦点在于这种大型且质量存疑的PR是否应该被接受，以及如何应对新技术带来的新挑战。
- 关于AI工具的讨论反映了当前技术在实际应用中的潜力和局限性。
- 评论中也包含了对标题和帖子风格的批评，认为其有误导性或不合适。

主要讨论点：神经刺激技术在治疗阿尔茨海默病及改善老年人记忆中的应用和安全性

不同观点：
• **支持神经刺激技术的观点**：  
  pedalpete 作为开发神经刺激技术的参与者，提供了研究证据支持其观点。他提到其公司开发的技术（https://affectablesleep.com）在健康老年人中改善了淀粉样蛋白反应和记忆，并在轻度至中度阿尔茨海默病患者中增加了睡眠质量。他强调多项研究表明慢波增强技术是安全的，且尚未发现任何负面影响。神经刺激通过触发大脑的保护机制，增加神经元的同步放电（慢波），从而增强大脑的类淋巴系统以清除代谢废物（如淀粉样蛋白、tau蛋白等）。相比复杂的药物相互作用，神经刺激似乎没有这些副作用。

• **提到其他类似技术**：  
  pedalpete 还提到了另一个类似的技术（https://www.cognitotx.com/），该技术使用开放式听觉和视觉刺激，也能在大脑中产生类似的反应。不过，据他所知，这种刺激相当耗人。

补充讨论：
• **对神经刺激技术安全性的争议**：  
  pedalpete 引用的文章指出，药物治疗存在脑肿胀和脑出血的风险，需要严密监控。而神经刺激技术在这方面似乎具有优势，但他也承认需要更多的研究来确认其长期安全性。

• **与其他治疗方法的比较**：  
  pedalpete 强调了神经刺激技术相比药物治疗的潜在优势，尤其是其在安全性方面的表现。药物通常具有复杂的相互作用和副作用，而神经刺激技术在这方面似乎更具吸引力。

• **研究证据的引用**：  
  pedalpete 提供了两个研究链接来支持他的论点，分别是关于神经刺激技术在老年人中的应用及其在阿尔茨海默病患者中改善睡眠的效果。这为他的观点提供了科学依据。

总的来说，评论主要围绕神经刺激技术在治疗阿尔茨海默病及改善老年人记忆中的应用和安全性展开，支持者认为该技术安全有效，并提供了研究证据支持其观点，同时也提到了类似技术的应用和挑战。

Laura Donnelly

A new drug could halt the progression of
Alzheimer’s disease
.
Trials suggest the treatment, called trontinemab, could be the most powerful weapon yet against dementia.
Research will now examine whether the drug should be given to those without any symptoms in order to prevent the disease.
Results presented at the Alzheimer’s Association International Conference in Toronto found the “game-changing” treatment can clear the devastating plaques associated with Alzheimer’s far more rapidly than any current licensed drug.
Nine in 10 patients prescribed trontinemab experienced amyloid clearance within 28 weeks, meaning visible markers of disease had vanished.
Experts hope these changes will be matched by improvements in memory and functioning, with an 18-month trial of 1,600 patients now under way.
Separate research will examine whether the drug could be given to people without any signs of dementia, in the same way that statins are used to ward off heart disease.
On Monday, experts said the findings were “very promising”, suggesting that the drug was much more powerful than existing medications, with far fewer side effects.
Around one million people in the UK suffer from dementia, with Alzheimer’s disease the most common form.
Powerful precise effects at low doses
Trontinemab is one of a class of new medicines aimed at clearing amyloid plaques. The new findings from phase two trials suggest that, in less than seven months, it has outperformed the ability of existing drugs to clear plaques in 18 months.
Experts hope that if given early enough, the drug could save some patients from developing symptoms at all. It has been engineered to more easily cross the blood-brain barrier, meaning it can ensure powerful precise effects at low doses.
The lack of side effects means it could be offered to large populations. This also means it could be offered at a far lower price than current medications, which require intense monitoring, including regular scans.
Experts believe it could become the first Alzheimer’s drug to be funded by the NHS.
Last year, medicines regulators in the UK gave the green light to the
first two treatments found to slow progression of Alzheimer’s disease
.
Both
lecanemab
and
donanemab
use monoclonal antibodies to clear amyloid plaques in Alzheimer’s disease. In trials they have been found to slow decline by 27 per cent and 35 per cent respectively, over 18 months. However, the risk of brain swelling and brain bleeds means they need intense monitoring.
The new drug appears to have a far better safety profile. The phase two trial of 149 patients found less than five per cent of cases suffering amyloid-related imaging abnormalities, and all cases quickly resolved.
It also requires less frequent infusions, with mass trials to examine the impact of giving the drug to patients once a month for six months, then every three months.
Scientists have been intrigued by the promise of trontinemab because of the way it has been designed to be transported across the blood brain-barrier, which normally prevents chemicals in the bloodstream from entering the brain.
‘Game-changing’
Prof Sir John Hardy, the chairman of molecular biology of neurological disease at University College London’s Institute of Neurology said the advance could be “game-changing”.
He told The Telegraph: “This is absolutely great news. It sucks the plaque out of the brain really quickly, much faster than we have seen with lecanemab or donanemab.”
The scientist, who was the first to identify the role of amyloid in the disease, said the drug’s safety profile was a “massive improvement” on the current drugs on the market, raising hopes it could be used both to prevent disease and stop it in its tracks.
He said: “There is no doubt this could be game-changing. We hope that if we can use these drugs to people early, we can halt the progression of disease, even before people have symptoms. Now we need to see the size of the clinical effect.”
Neither of the current drugs have been funded by the NHS as a result of their high costs, much of which stems from the need for intense monitoring, including regular scans.
Prof Hardy said: “These results show it is much faster and safer than previous drugs, which means less monitoring. That brings down the cost significantly, it means fewer MRI scans, so that would surely mean it would get Nice [National Institute of Health and Care Excellence] approval.”

Artificial Intelligence (AI) may have elevated the level of convenience in accomplishing some day-to-day tasks, but it has also become the scourge to professional photographers. In the past years, we’ve been seeing examples of wildlife photographs being modified or regenerated by AI and getting posted on social media with incorrect and misleading captions, often generated by AI as well. These used to be straightforward cases of copyright infringement, but there is no clear line when it comes to derivative work, especially when the variation can easily be defined in the image generation prompt.
In the past week, a number of prominent nature photographers showed how their photographs were being stolen and mangled into “AI-nonsense”, deceiving countless others into believing the made-up stories in the captions. The perpetrators look for beautiful wildlife photos and to skirt copyright infringement scanners, use AI to re-generate the photo to be posted on social media.

data.author: mfiguiere

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：YouTube针对未成年人的账号禁令及其影响

不同观点：
• 观点一：该禁令仅限制创建账号，而不禁止观看视频。WantonQuantum指出，这一禁令只是禁止16岁以下的人创建账户，而不是禁止他们观看YouTube上的视频。这意味着未成年人仍然可以访问平台内容，只是无法进行互动（如点赞、评论、订阅）。

• 观点二：关注实际执行和影响。一些用户可能会认为，虽然该禁令在理论上只限制账户创建，但实际操作中可能会对未成年人访问内容产生影响，尤其是那些依赖登录账户才能观看的个性化内容或受年龄限制的内容。

• 观点三：对家长监管的影响。有用户可能认为，这一禁令可能会促使家长更好地监督孩子的网络使用情况，因为孩子在没有账户的情况下可能会受到更多的内容限制。然而，也有观点认为，家长可能需要更多工具和指导来有效管理孩子的在线活动。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于禁令的实际效果和执行细节。一些用户质疑该禁令是否能够真正保护未成年人，还是只是形式上的限制。
• 例子：有用户提到，某些平台的内容过滤和年龄验证机制并不完善，未成年人可能通过虚假信息轻松绕过这些限制。
• 技术实现：讨论中涉及到技术手段在实施此类禁令中的作用，如IP地址追踪、设备识别等，可能对平台的技术能力提出更高要求。
